en: For strength thee! For well-being! You are the winds. May the god Savitṛ impel you toward the most excellent work. Swell forth!

O inviolable cow, [go] as a portion for the gods and for Indra; let neither the thief nor the malevolent man have power over you. May you not suffer harm under this master of cattle; protect the many cattle of the sacrificer.
Thou art the seat of cattle; the Rakṣas is burnt away, the enemy is burnt away.
The sacrificial ladle has indeed gone forward toward the sacred grass, prepared by Manu and fashioned with self-power;
the sages bring it from the front.

Thou art pressed out for the gods; thou art the tuft of Viṣṇu, let loose as the portion of kine. On the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I cut the sacrificial grass (barhis), the seat of the gods.
From this, O sacrificial grass, sprout forth with a hundred shoots; may we sprout forth with a thousand shoots.
The womb of Aditi art thou; the girdle of Indrāṇī art thou. May Pūṣan tie thy knot; may it not loosen for thee.
With the two arms of Indra I lift thee up; with the head of Bṛhaspati I carry thee. Traverse the wide mid-air;
I set thee upon the back of Aditi.
Be purified for the divine rite; you are the purifier of the Vasus, with a hundred streams, a thousand streams, and an unbroken body.
You are heaven; you are earth; you are the cauldron of Mātariśvan.
Sit in the abode of the all-encompassing sacrificer.
For nourishment, O Ādityas, you are the girdle. Whom have you milked? May she be Viśvāyu (possessing all life), O so-and-so! Whom have you milked? May she be Viśvabhū (all-becoming), O so-and-so!
Whom have you milked? May she be Viśvakarman (all-acting), O so-and-so! The drop is offered, the spray is offered; O Agni, protect against the scattered drops.
Cook it well for the gods; cook the oblation for Agni. To the great firmament, Svāhā! For Heaven and Earth, for Indra!
I extend you, O Viṣṇu, as a portion with Soma; protect the oblation, O Waters, and remain awake.

For your attire, for your work, for your well-performed deed—O divine waters, you who move forward, you leaders, go forward at the head of this sacrifice; lead the sacrifice forward, lead the lord of the sacrifice forward. Indra chose you for the conquest of Vṛtra; you chose Indra for the conquest of Vṛtra. You are sprinkled. Let the divine hosts settle down. You are a tree, increased by rain.
Traverse this wide mid-air; the *rakṣas* is burnt away, the enemy is burnt away. You are the yoke-pole; shake off him who shakes us, and him whom we shake off—shake him off!

[Page I,3] You are the best carrier of the gods, the most liberal, the most fulfilling, the most beloved, the best invoker of the gods; you are the unswerving vessel for the oblation. Be firm, do not waver! You are the stride of Viṣṇu. Wide space for the wind! With the eye of Mitra I gaze upon the will of the god.
At the impulse of Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, and with the hands of Pūṣan, may they offer [the oblations].
For your protection, not for harm; I set aside these [grains] acceptable to Agni, and those acceptable to such-and-such [deity]. This is for the gods, and this is ours together.
May the dwellings be made firm. Svāhā! To Heaven and Earth! I have been released from the noose of Varuṇa; I have beheld the light of heaven.
The light of Vaiśvānara, the wide mid-region—enter it; I set you down in the lap of Aditi.
May the god Savitṛ purify you with a flawless strainer,
with the rays of the sun, the Vasu.
I sprinkle you, acceptable to Agni; I sprinkle you, acceptable to [Name]. Whatever impure part of you was seized, let that be purified.

You are the skin of Aditi. Shaken off is the Rakṣas, shaken off is the enemy. You are the skin of Aditi. May the skin of Aditi recognize you. You are the broad stone, belonging to the tree. May the skin of Aditi recognize you. You are the tongue of Agni, the release of speech.
For your long life! You are the great pressing-stone, made of wood; prepare the oblation for the gods, prepare it well, prepare it perfectly!
You are the *kuṭaru* bird, honey-tongued; through you may we conquer every encounter. Speak forth nourishment, speak forth vigor, speak forth the increase of wealth!
[Page I,4] You are increased by the rain; may that which is increased by the rain recognize you. Blown away is the *rakṣas*, blown away is the enemy.
The portion of the *rakṣases* has been cast forth. You are the skin of Aditi; shaken off is the *rakṣas*, shaken off is the enemy. You are the skin of Aditi. Back!
May the skin of Aditi know you; you are the bowl, the daughter of the mountain. May the skin of Aditi know you; you are the bowl, the daughter of the mountain.
May the daughter of the mountain know you; you are the pillar of Aditi; you are grain; satisfy the gods! For out-breath you, for in-breath you, for diffused breath you!
Touch each other along a long extension! With the eye of Mitra I gaze upon you for the sake of life.
May the god Savitṛ, the golden-handed, receive you.
The Rakṣas is burnt away; the enemy is burnt away. Do not burn me; you are firm. Make the earth firm.

O Agni, strike down the raw-eating fire; drive out the flesh-eater. O Agni, bring the place of sacrifice for the gods. You are the support; make the mid-air firm. You are the sustainer; make heaven firm. You are the upholder; make all things firm. You are consciousness; you are total consciousness; in all [beings]...
Sit in the quarters, O kinsmen; surround this sacrificer. Let these kinsmen surround this sacrificer.
Heat yourselves with the heat of the Gharma of the Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, the Bhṛgus, and the Aṅgirases.
Those potsherds which the wise ones collect for the heat—
let Indra and Vāyu release them as well under the ordinance of Pūṣan.
At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I pour together [the grains].
May the god Savitṛ purify you with an unbroken filter,
with the rays of the Vasu Sūrya.
May the waters come together with the plants; may the plants come together with the sap. May the wealthy, moving, and auspicious waters have united with the auspicious [plants].

May the people settle; for procreation, thee! Thou art the Gharma, the life of all. O Gharma, rest upon the Gharma! Spread wide! Spread wide! May the lord of the sacrifice spread wide! May thy body be united with [his] body!
Agni, the sage and lord of booty, has stepped around the oblations, bestowing treasures upon the donor.
May the god Savitṛ cook you on the highest vault of the earth; O Agni, receive the sacred formulation (brahman).

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee. Thou art the right arm of Indra, thousand-edged and hundred-pointed; Vāyu is thy keen-edged brilliance. O Earth, place of divine sacrifice, may I not harm thee! Go to the root of the plants, go to the cow-pen, the stall; may Parjanya rain for thee; bind [them], O god Savitṛ!
With a hundred nooses, in the furthest distance, bind him who hates us and whom we hate;
let him not escape from there. O auspicious plants, may I not harm your root. Go to the fold, to the cow-pen; may Parjanya rain for you.
Bind him with a hundred nooses, O God Savitṛ, in the furthest distance—he who hates us.
And him whom we hate, bind him here; let him not escape from this. Let not your drop leap up to heaven;

go to the fold, the place of cattle. May Parjanya rain for you. Bind him, O God Savitṛ, with a hundred fetters in the furthest distance—him who hates us and him whom we hate; bind him here, let him not escape from this, O Vasus.

May the Rudras encompass you with the Gāyatrī metre; may the Rudras encompass you with the Triṣṭubh metre; may the Ādityas encompass you with the Jagatī metre. You are the one who leaves no enemy behind on earth; you are the non-sacrificer to the gods; you are the seat of truth; you are the seat of cosmic order;
you are the seat of the Gharma vessel.

In ancient times, having taken up the earth—the giver of life, vast and overflowing—from the one who was cruel and gliding away, they established it in the moon by means of funeral offerings; the wise sages, pointing toward it, performed sacrifice.

The Rakṣas is burnt away; the enemy is burnt away. Do not wipe away my life-span, do not wipe away my breath, do not wipe away my sight or hearing, do not wipe away my speech or my cattle, do not wipe away my sacrifice or my progeny. You are luster; you are the bright; you are light;
you are immortality; you belong to the All-Gods.
Thou art the oblation for Vaiśvānara, with uplifted vigor, possessing true might.
Thou art power; overcome the adversary, overcome those who attack us in battle.

Thou art thousandfold potency; do thou quicken me. Thou art the clarified butter of clarified butter, the oblation of oblations, the truth of truth, anointed with truth. With truth I anoint thee. With unimpaired sight I gaze upon thee for the increase of wealth and for the sake of good progeny.
Thou art the beloved abode of the gods, the inviolable place of sacrifice for the gods;
I take thee for the feast of the gods.

O divine waters, you are pure; having been purified, you have served the gods. May we, being pure, serve as your servers, well-served by you. You are black, dwelling in the clefts; become clarified butter for Agni. You are the altar; I sprinkle you, who are dear to the sacrificial grass (*barhis*).
You are the sacrificial grass; I sprinkle you, who are dear to the altar. *Svāhā* to the fathers who drink the hot offering (*gharma*).
The one dwelling in the lair for Agni. (Note:
The sandhi is irregular; the editor reads *ākhareṣṭhā agnaye*.)
Best dwelling in the pen.
May Pūṣan untie your knot. You are the tuft of Viṣṇu; spread yourself wide! Soft with wool, a good seat for the gods.
You are the Gandharva Viśvāvasu, shrinking away from everyone; you are the enclosure of the sacrificer, worthy of praise, praised by Indra.

You are the right arm of the sacrificer, the enclosing-stick, praised with the *iḍā* invocation. May Mitra and Varuṇa enclose you from the north; you are the enclosing-stick of the sacrificer, praised with the *iḍā* invocation.
O Sage, may we, radiant, kindle you, the eternal Hotṛ-priest.
Upon the highest vault of the earth, may Sūrya protect you from the east with his rays from every curse.
You two are the supporters of all people; you are the seat of the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas. You are the womb of the offering-spoons;
by your birth you are the sky. You are named Juhū (the Sacrificer); you are dear to the gods by your dear name. Sit down upon your firm seat; you are the intermediate space.
By birth you are named Upabhṛt; by your dear name, beloved of the gods, sit in your firm seat! You are Pṛthivī; by birth you are named Dhruvā;
by your dear name, beloved of the gods, sit in your firm seat! You are the Bull, belonging to the Śakvarī verses; I set you down in the measure of the Vaṣaṭ-call.
They have settled firm in the womb of Cosmic Order, in the world of well-performed deeds; protect them, O Viṣṇu!
Protect the sacrifice; protect the lord of the sacrifice; protect me, the performer of the sacrifice.
You are Viṣṇu’s portions; you are Viṣṇu’s abodes; you are Prajāpati’s abodes.

Today the sun has set for me; O Agni and Viṣṇu, you who are well-enclosed and well-sheltered, draw yourselves apart; do not harm me. O makers of the world, create a world for me; do not burn me. Protect my self; be auspicious to us today. This is the station of Viṣṇu; standing here, Indra performed his heroic deed, having taken hold together with the deities.
Upright is the sacrifice, reaching to heaven; unswerving is the worship of the lord of sacrifice—rich in Indra, rich in horses, and possessing great luster.
Of the rice, of the honey, and of the clarified butter, Svāhā! May light be united with light.
With the impulse of strength, with the upward-grasping, he has lifted me up;
then Indra, by the downward-grasping, has cast my rivals beneath me.
The grasping and the seizing have strengthened the divine *brahman*;
now may Indra and Agni scatter my rivals in all directions.
You are Vasu, you are Upāvasu, you are Viśvāvasu; licking with the waters, may the birds go forth. Having become the speckled cow, go to the Maruts; from there, favor us with rain.
The gods who partake of the remnants, the steadfast ones, the great ones, those who stand upon the sacrificial grass (*prastara*), and those who sit upon the sacred grass (*barhis*)—
all of you, welcoming this speech, may the immortal gods rejoice in the *svāhā*!
O gods who know the way, having found the way, go upon the way. O Lord of Mind, place this well-prepared sacrifice in heaven among the gods; Svāhā!
O divine waters, purify me; being full of sweetness, [purify me] for the sacrifice to the gods.
O herb, protect him; O axe, do not harm him.
With that body of yours which is most auspicious, touch him.
O god-hearer, I shave these; may I attain well-being hereafter.
Golden-hued, pure, and purifying, the waters have flowed forth, leaving behind all that is blameworthy;
a hundred filters are spread out within them—by means of these may the divine Savitṛ purify me.
May the Waters, my mothers, purify me; may those who cleanse with ghee purify me with ghee. For the goddesses shall carry away every impurity; from them I emerge bright and purified.

You are Viṣṇu’s protection; grant me protection. For strength, I take you. You are the milk of the great ones, the sap of the waters and the plants. You are the bestower of luster; bestow luster upon me.
You are the pupil of Vṛtra; may you bestow vital strength upon my eye. With you as a great mountain, I place hatred and enmities within [me]. You are the protector of the eye; protect my eye.
May Citpati purify you; may Vācaspati purify you.
May the god Savitṛ purify you with a flawless strainer,
with the rays of the Vasu Sūrya.
O Lord of the Purifier, with your purifier, may I be able to accomplish that for which I purify myself.
To Ākūti, to Prayuj, to Agni, Svāhā! To Medhā, to Manas, to Agni, Svāhā! To Dīkṣā, to Tapas, to Agni, Svāhā! To Sarasvatī, to Pūṣan, to Agni, Svāhā!
The divine waters, vast and bringing all-beneficence; Heaven and Earth, and the wide mid-air; may Bṛhaspati increase us with our oblation. Svāhā!
May every mortal choose the friendship of the divine leader;
everyone strives for wealth, and may he choose glory so that he may prosper. Svāhā!

You two are the artistic forms of the Ṛgveda and Sāmaveda; I take hold of you both until the end of the verse. Protect me! You are the shelter of Viṣṇu; grant me shelter. Homage be to you; do not harm me.
O Varuṇa, as he trains his mind in this way, sharpen his will and skill.
May I board the well-oared ship by which we may cross over all difficulties.
O Sun and Fire, Heaven and Earth, the wide Atmosphere, Waters, and Plants—ye lords of consecration, summon me to the consecration!

O God Savitṛ, you are the lord of consecration for this consecration; protect me while I am thus. You are strength, belonging to Aṅgiras; soft as wool, bestow strength upon me. You are the womb of Indra; guard me! Homage be to you; do not harm me.
Make the cultivation yield good grain; make the plants bear fine fruit.
O Horn, loosen this knot: that which is knotted in his heart, and that thought of his which is knotted within.
Great art thou, O tree-born one; with fair splendor, bestow splendor upon the sacrificer; protect him from the gaze of the stars.
O gods, we seek from you that which is desirable as the sacrifice proceeds;
O worshipful gods, since we call upon you with our prayer.
Svāhā! I take hold of the sacrifice from the mind, svāhā! From heaven, svāhā! From earth, svāhā! From the wide mid-region, svāhā! From the wind, svāhā! Svāhā!
Do not depart from the presence of the constellations; perform the vow.
We meditate upon the divine intellect, most gracious for our aid, bestowing splendor, carrying the sacrifice; may it lead us to a good path under its control.
Those gods who are born of Manu, yoked by mind, highly skillful, and whose father is Dakṣa—may they protect us; may they guard us; to them, svāhā!
O Waters, may you be auspicious and drinkable; may you be very gracious within our womb, our belly.
Rich in nourishment, free from disease, and sinless, be auspicious to us for the sake of life.
O Agni, you are the most gladdening of the oblations; may you be well awake, and may we be well gladdened.
Guard us for our well-being; restore us again for waking.
May mind come back to us, may life come back; may breath come back, and may intention come back.
May Vaiśvānara, the undeceivable protector of the body, drive away all misfortunes.
O Agni, you are the guardian of vows, a god among mortals; you are to be praised at the sacrifices. Maintain the vow among us.

May Pūṣan be master of gains; may Soma, bestowing wealth with bounty, be preeminent through fulfillment. May we not be deprived of life and luster! Grant this much, O Soma; bring more, O God! Savitṛ is the giver of wealth, Vāyu the guardian, Tvaṣṭṛ the overlord, and Pūṣan the receiver.
O divine Waters, that wave of yours which belongs to the waters, which is fit for oblation, powerful, and most intoxicating—may I not step upon it. Those [waves] of yours...
The speech of cattle is in the bull; those [speeches] are bright at the head, the sun is at the head. I send them forth according to your respective portions here.
May they return to us auspiciously. For Vāyu you, for Varuṇa you, for Rudra you, for Nirṛti you, for Indra you, for the Maruts you!

This is your white body, this is your luster; unite with it, go to radiance! You are swift, held by the mind, beloved by Viṣṇu. At the impulse of you, whose impulse is true, may I attain the control of your body. Svāhā! You are the bright one.

Thou art the moon; thou art ambrosia; thou belongest to the All-gods; thou art consciousness; thou art mind; thou art thought; thou art the sacrificial fee; thou art worthy of sacrifice; thou art the ruling power; thou art Aditi, double-headed. As such, be favorable to us when moving forward and favorable when returning. May Mitra bind thee by the foot; may Pūṣan protect thy paths; for Indra, the overseer, let thy mother give her consent, let thy father give his consent, let thy brother give his consent.

With thy kinsman, thy companion, thy fellow-herd, go thou, O Goddess, to the God; for Indra, Rudra shall turn thee back as Soma. Return again with Soma as thy friend. Thou art a Vasu, thou art a Rudra, thou art Aditi, thou art an Āditya, thou art Candrā, thou art Rudrā.
May Bṛhaspati cause thee to rest in bliss; Rudra, together with the Vasus, has looked upon thee. Upon the head of the earth I sprinkle thee.
Worthy of sacrifice, in the place of Iḍā, rich in ghee, Svāhā! Rejoice with us; in us be your wealth, in us your wealth, in us your wealth.
May we not be separated from the abundance of wealth; may we serve you, possessing the skill of Tvaṣṭṛ.
I have mounted the eye of the sun, the pupil of the eye of Agni,
when you go forth shining with your wise steeds.
Moreover, we have entered upon the path that leads to well-being and is free from danger,
by which one avoids all enemies and finds wealth.
Thou art ours; thy cup is bright; Svāhā! thee for the Vicits!
I praise that god Savitar between the two worlds, the one of seer-like wisdom, whose impulse is true, the bestower of jewels, the beloved thought.
Whose lofty splendor has shone forth at his impulsion; the golden-handed one of good intent has measured out the light with his form.

For the sake of offspring, may offspring breathe after you; protect the offspring. O bright one (*śukra*), I purchase your bright [essence] with the bright, your radiant [essence] with the radiant, your immortal [essence] with the immortal, O divine Soma. Whatever power you have in the cow, let that be ours; O radiant one, you are the body of ascetic heat (*tapas*), the color of Prajāpati. Thriving with thousandfold nourishment, be purchased for us with the supreme animal. Our kinship is with you, O fair-voiced one, O cloud-like one (*nabhrāj*).
Aṅghāri, Bambhāri, Astar, Ahasta, Kṛśānu—these are your Soma-purchasers; guard them, let not the evil-eyed one deceive you, and let no evil-sighted one look upon you.
The animals for purchase:
FN *Corrigenda et Conjecturae ad opus integrum* [Page I,15]

Thou art self-born, thou art self-existent; born for our ritual act, I take thee with the *ṛta*, protect us with the *ṛta*. Come to us like Mitra, bestowing good friendship; enter Indra’s right thigh together with the increase of wealth—desiring him who desires thee, gentle one, enter the gentle.
Upward with life, with good life, upward with the sap of the plants;
upward from the domain of Parjanya I have arisen following immortality.
Pervade the wide mid-air; sit upon the seat of Aditi.
The Bull propped up the sky and measured out the expanse of the mid-air;
the Sovereign took his seat over all beings—all these are the ordinances of Varuṇa.
He spread the mid-air across the forests; he placed speed in horses, milk in cows, will in hearts, Varuṇa in the quarters, Agni in heaven, Sūrya in the sky, and Soma upon the mountain.
You are the striker; strike down the striker, whoever shall strike us, and whoever we shall strike—strike him down!
Thou art Varuna's; may Varuna support thee; thou art the pillar of Varuna.
Descend, O Lord of the World, toward all your abodes;
let not those who lie in ambush, nor those who waylay you, nor predatory wolves seeking to do harm, find you.
Becoming a hawk, fly away to the prepared offering in the house of our sacrificer for the sake of the pressing for the gods.
Homage to the eye of Mitra and Varuṇa! Pay worship to that great god;
recite the hymn to Sūrya, the far-seeing, the banner born of the gods, the son of Heaven.
Thou art Varuna’s; may Varuna support thee; thou art Varuna’s pillar-release.
Loosened is the noose of Varuṇa; cast away is the noose of Varuṇa; homage to the noose of Varuṇa!
You are the body of Agni; for Viṣṇu, you! You are the body of Soma; for Viṣṇu, you! You are the hospitality of the guest; for Viṣṇu, you!
For Agni, the giver of increase of wealth, for Viṣṇu, you! For the falcon, the bearer of Soma, for Viṣṇu, you! You belong to Varuṇa; [you are] Varuṇa.
"O you who are firm in your vow, sit upon the seat of Truth for Varuṇa; for Varuṇa, I take you."
Thou art the birthplace of Agni; ye two are the testicles; thou art Urvaśī; thou art Āyu; thou art Purūravas; thou art the Gāyatrī; thou art the Triṣṭubh; thou art the Jagatī.
May you two be of one mind with us, of one dwelling, of one consciousness, and stainless.
Do not harm the sacrifice, nor the lord of the sacrifice, O Jātavedas; be auspicious to us today.
Fire moves within fire, having entered it; he is the son of the seers, this sovereign ruler.
To him let us pay worship with an oblation; may we not fail in our portion of the gods.

I take you for the one who falls upon; I take you for the one who falls around. For Tanūnapāt, for Śakman, for the powerful Śakvara, with power, for the most mighty; you are unassailable, the invincible might of the gods.
The protector from curses, who is himself beyond being cursed.
May the Lord of Vows accept this vow of mine; may the Lord of Consecration accept my consecration. Straightway have I approached the Truth. O Agni, Lord of Vows, establish me in prosperity.
O Agni, Lord of Vows, that body which is mine, let it be in thee; O Agni, Lord of Vows, that body which is thine, let it be in me.
O Lord of Vows, let the vows of us two who observe them be united. O divine Soma, may thy stalk by stalk swell.
For Indra, the finder of the single wealth; swell for Indra! May Indra swell for thee! Make thy friends swell with gain and wisdom!
O divine Soma, may I attain well-being through the pressing; may I attain well-being at the conclusion. Desired is wealth, desired are blessings;
I send them forth for Bhaga. Truth to the speakers of truth; homage to Heaven, homage to Earth!
O Agni, that body of yours which is the seat of the unaging, most exalted, dwelling in the depths—therein you have warded off the flashing word, you have warded off the fierce word. Svāhā!
O Agni, that body of yours which dwells in the dust, that body of yours which dwells in the flames, that body of yours which belongs to Rudra—with that, protect us; for that body of yours, *svāhā*!
Thou art my path to heat; thou art my path to wealth. Protect me when I am distressed; protect me when I am afflicted, O Agni Aṅgiras!

Thou who art upon this earth, come with life and with name! Let the Vasus carry thee hither with the Gāyatrī metre; find that which belongs to the Lord of the Sacrifice! With that unassailable and invincible abode of thine, I establish thee, O Agni Aṅgiras! Thou who art upon the second earth...

Upon the earth, by your life-breath, come with your name! Let the Rudras carry you; recognize [this] with the Triṣṭubh metre. Know that which is your unassailable domain of the Lord of the Sacrifice; with that which is unassailable, I establish you. O Agni Aṅgiras, upon the third earth, by your life-breath, come with your name! Let the Ādityas carry you; recognize [this] with the Jagatī metre. Know that which is your unassailable domain of the Lord of the Sacrifice.
That which is your unassailable domain, your invincible [domain], with that I establish you. O Agni, may you find the name Nabhas, which is yours. You are the lioness; you are the buffalo-cow.
Purify yourself for the gods; beautify yourself for the gods. May Indra’s roar protect you from the east with the Vasus;
may the Fathers, swift as thought, protect you from the south; may the Rudras, the wise ones, protect you from the west; may Viśvakarman [protect you from the north].
May you protect from the north with the Ādityas. You are a lioness, overcoming rivals; svāhā! You are a lioness, winning the increase of wealth;

svāhā! You are a lioness, winning good offspring; svāhā! You are a lioness, winning the Ādityas and winning kinsmen; svāhā! You are a lioness; bring the gods for the god-loving sacrificer; svāhā! For the beings, you! You are the life of all; make firm the earth!
You are the firm foundation; make the intermediate space firm. You are the abode of the immovable; make the sky firm. You are the ash of Agni; you are the soil of Agni; you are the nest of Agni.
May the radiant, great one drink the Soma-mead, bestowing unimpaired life upon the lord of the sacrifice;
impelled by the wind, he who protects by his own power nourishes all creatures and shines forth in many ways.
O you who are renowned among the gods, proclaim this among the gods!

The inspired poets harness their minds and harness their thoughts for the sake of the great, inspired, and wise one. He, the knower of the sacred ordinances, has established the priestly functions; indeed, great is the praise of the divine Savitṛ.
Drive away the fear of men; let not the wheels turn back.
Go to the house of Soma; go to the appointed place of Indra.
Vishnu strode across this [universe]; in three places he planted his foot;
it was gathered together in his dust.
For you two have become possessed of refreshing waters and cows, providing excellent pasture for Manu, O glorious ones;
Viṣṇu has propped apart these two worlds, and you have supported the earth on all sides with your rays.
O God, speak auspiciously for our home; may you remain uninjured while [the enemy] is injured.
May a heroic son be born to us, one capable of action, a protector against curses, himself beyond the reach of curses—
one whom many shall follow and who shall be the master of many.
Thou art Vaiṣṇava; may Viṣṇu support thee from above.
O Viṣṇu, from heaven or from earth, or from the wide and vast mid-air, O Viṣṇu, fill your hands with many riches; bestow them from your right hand and from your left.
I shall now proclaim the heroic deeds of Viṣṇu, who measured out the earthly realms;
he who, striding out threefold with wide-gazing steps, propped up the highest dwelling place.
Thou art the back of Viṣṇu; thou art the forehead of Viṣṇu; ye two are the jaws of Viṣṇu; thou art the needle of Viṣṇu; thou art the fixed point of Viṣṇu; thou belongest to Viṣṇu; for Viṣṇu thee!
For that heroic deed Viṣṇu is praised; like a fearsome beast, roaming and dwelling in the mountains, he in whose three wide strides all beings abide.
At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee up. Thou art a spade; thou art a woman.

Here do I cut off the necks of the Rakṣas. Here do I cut off the necks of him who is my equal and of him who is not my equal, whoever acts as an enemy toward me. Great art thou, of great lineage; utter a great voice for Indra, O slayer of Rakṣases, destroyer of secret spells!

O Vaiṣṇavī, you are the sovereign; I root out those secret spells (*valaga*) which my equal or my unequal has buried—those spells, O Self-Ruling One (*svarāj*), which have been cast away at the height of the ankles, destroyers of the adversary. I root out those secret spells which my kinsman or my non-kinsman has buried—those spells, O Far-Ruling One (*virāj*), which have been cast away at the height of the knees.

O slayer of demons, I now dig up these *valagas* which my kinsman or my stranger has buried—those *valagas* which have been cast down at the height of the navel; you are the all-conquering destroyer of curses. O slayer of demons, I now dig up these *valagas* which my rival or my non-rival has buried—those *valagas* which have been cast down at the height of the shoulders; you are the all-conquering destroyer.
Henceforth, I dig up those spells of the enemy who acts with hostility— those which my kinsman or my stranger has buried—
which are spells cast down to the height of the head.
Touch these for the sake of long life and splendor; you are the treasure-store of the gods, the repeller of hatred.
Drive away from us all hostilities, whatever we have committed.
This which belongs to the gods has been deposited here; now shine forth upon the four quarters, making thy other rivals low.

For the earth thee, for the atmosphere thee, for the sky thee! May the worlds, the seats of the fathers, be purified! Thou art barley; bar away our enemies, bar away the adversary! I strew thee upon the world, the seat of the fathers.
Rise up, O Lord of the Forest, in harmony with the divine sacrificial grass;
let the Maruts, as extenders, strike you down, and let Mitra and Varuṇa do so by their firm law.

[I, 21] I pile thee around, the winner of the Brahman, the winner of the Kṣatra; strengthen the Brahman, strengthen the Kṣatra, strengthen the increase of wealth, strengthen progeny; strengthen the kinsmen for this sacrificer.
Fill heaven and earth with clarified butter; you are the shade for all people.
May these songs encompass you on every side, O lover of song;
may the increasing hymns follow him whose life is increased, and may they be pleasing to him as he delights in them.

For Indra thee! Thou art the needle of Indra; thou art the fixed point of Indra; thou belongest to Indra; for Indra thee! I sprinkle you, the Rakṣas-slayers, the charm-destroyers, belonging to Viṣṇu. I pour out for you, the Rakṣas-slayer, the charm-destroyer, belonging to Viṣṇu. I strew for you, the Rakṣas-slayer, the charm-destroyer, belonging to Viṣṇu. I lay down for you two, the Rakṣas-slayers, the charm-destroyers, belonging to Viṣṇu.
"O you two, I strew around you, who are slayers of demons and destroyers of secret spells, belonging to Viṣṇu; I spread you out, the demon-slayer and spell-destroyer, belonging to Viṣṇu."
You are pervasive, the carrier; you are the bearer of the oblation. You are strengthening, the wise one; you are Tutha, the all-knowing.
You are the seeker of aid, the worshipper; you are Aṅghāri, you are Bambhāri. You are Uśij, the seer; you are Śundhyu, the purifier. You are the sovereign, Kṛśānu;
you are the one to be seated in assembly, the one to be established. You are the cloud, the swift mover; you are the unsullied, the slayer of the oblation.

Thou art Sagara, the knower of all; thou art the abode of Truth, the light of heaven. Thou art the ocean, the all-encompassing; thou art the one-footed goat; thou art the serpent of the deep; thou art the sage, the bearer of the sages. With thy fierce aspect, O Agni, protect me; carry me across;
let there be homage to thee; do not harm me.
O Soma, you are the one who extends wide protection against the hostilities caused by others that seek to harm our bodies; Svāhā!
May the swift one, being pleased, enjoy the clarified butter; Svāhā!
O Agni, lead us by a good path to wealth, O God who knows all ways;
remove from us the sin that leads astray, and we shall offer you the most abundant speech of homage.
O Viṣṇu, stride out widely; make wide room for our dwelling. Drink the clarified butter, O you who love ghee; further and further prolong the life of the lord of the sacrifice. Svāhā!
Thus worship Varuṇa, the lofty one; pay homage to the wise guardian of immortality.
May he grant us a triple-layered shelter; may Heaven and Earth protect us in their lap.
Pervade the wide mid-air; sit upon the seat of Aditi. O God Savitṛ, this is your Soma; protect it.
Let not those of evil sight harm you; let them not look upon you. Here, O divine Soma, I turn back toward the gods;
here I turn back toward men, together with abundance of wealth and progeny. Homage to the gods! Svadhā to the fathers! [I am] released from the noose of Varuṇa.
I have been released; I have manifested the light of Vaiśvānara. O Agni, Lord of Vows, that body of yours which was in me—let it be in you;

O Agni, Lord of Vows, that body of mine which was in you—let it be in me. O Lord of Vows, let us two, who have observed our vows, again [unite] our vows according to their respective places. O Lord of Vows, let us two, who have observed our vows, release our vows from one another.
upāvṛta: FN ⟨ upāvṛtas upāvṛta: FN Corrections and conjectures for the entire work:
read *upāvṛtta* instead of *upāvṛta*.
*upāvṛta*: see 3.9.1:113.14; *upāvṛtā* (sg. nom.). Aorist [Page I,23].

I have passed beyond others; I have not approached others. I have found you, who are beyond those beyond and nearer than those near. We delight in you for the sacrifice to the gods; you are beloved by Viṣṇu; for Viṣṇu, you!
O Viṣṇu, stride out widely; make wide room for our dwelling. O consumer of ghee, drink the ghee; further and further prolong the life of the lord of the sacrifice. Svāhā!
O herb, protect him; O axe, do not harm him.
With that body of yours which is most auspicious, touch him.

You, whom this sharp-edged axe has brought forth for great good fortune—do not harm the sky with your tip, nor the mid-air with your middle; be united with the earth and go to the light. O Lord of the Forest, grow with a hundred shoots; may we grow with a thousand shoots.

For the earth thee, for the atmosphere thee, for the sky thee! May the worlds, the seats of the fathers, be purified! Thou art barley; bar away our enemies, bar away the adversary! I spread thee out as a world, a seat for the fathers.
Easy of access, you are the leader of leaders; he shall stand upon you—be mindful of him.
Fill heaven and earth with clarified butter; may the god Savitṛ anoint you with honey.
You are the cup of Indra; make the plants bear good fruit. With your top, prop up the sky; with your middle, fill the atmosphere; with your base, make firm the earth.
We desire to go to those abodes of yours where the many-horned, tireless cows dwell;
for there, indeed, the highest step of the wide-striding Viṣṇu shines forth abundantly.
Behold the deeds of Viṣṇu, through which he has made his vows manifest;
he is the close-allied friend of Indra.

I pile thee around, the winner of Brahman, the winner of Kṣatra; strengthen the Brahman, strengthen the Kṣatra, strengthen the increase of wealth, strengthen progeny; strengthen the kinsmen for this sacrificer.
The wise behold with power that supreme abode of Viṣṇu,
like an eye stretched across the sky.

Thou art the encircler; may the divine subjects encircle thee; may human beings, together with abundance of wealth and progeny, encircle this sacrificer. Upon the summit of heaven, may thy smoke go to heaven, thy light to the intermediate space, and thy ashes to the earth; Svāhā!

For strength, thee! Thou art the assistant. The divine hosts have come forward to the gods—the eager bearers. O Bṛhaspati, bestow riches; may thy oblations be sweet, O God Tvaṣṭṛ, for the delight of wealth. O wealthy ones, rejoice! At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee. O divine oblation, I bind thee with the noose of Cosmic Order (Ṛta).

For such-and-such [deity], thee, who art acceptable, I sprinkle boldly; for the waters and for the plants, thee, who art acceptable, I sprinkle. May thy mother give her consent, may thy father give his consent, may thy brother born of the same womb give his consent, may thy friend belonging to the same herd give his consent. Bring the gods hither for the god-loving sacrificer. Thou art the drinker of the waters; may the divine waters relish this well-prepared oblation. May Vāyu unite with thee through the wind.
May the limbs come together with the sacrificial offerings; may the lord of the sacrifice come together with his blessing. Anointed with clarified butter, do you two protect the cattle.
O humans: those who,
being bound themselves, looked upon the one being bound with their mind and their eye—
may the god Agni release him first, and Prajāpati, bestowing favor upon his offspring.
O Revatī, enter the lord of the sacrifice with vigor; O Urojas, together with the divine Vāta, enter the intermediate space.
Sacrifice with your own self for this oblation; become one with its body.
Bestow upon the lord of the sacrifice a sacrifice that is ever more exalted than the most exalted.
You are the winner of light; having won the light, go to the light! You are the light for me, the light for my cattle. You are the winner of the world; having won the world, go to the world!
You are the world for me, the world for my cattle. You are the winner of refuge; having won the refuge, go to the refuge! You are the refuge for me, the refuge for my cattle.
You are the winner of the path; having won the path, go to the path! You are the path for me, the path for my cattle.
Verily, you do not die here, nor do you suffer harm; you go to the gods by auspicious paths, where the doers of good deeds go, and not the doers of evil—there may the god Savitṛ place you.
O pacifiers, approach the sacrifice accompanied by the gods;
release the animal from the noose and the lord of the sacrifice from his bond.
May Aditi release these bonds—the bonds of the animal—from Paśupati.
May he who hates us fall low; upon him we fasten these bonds.

Homage to these! O unassailable one, go forth for the sacrificer along the stream of clarified butter, together with the increase of wealth. O divine waters, you who are pure, you have served the gods; being pure ourselves, may we be your well-served servers. [I offer] speech.
Do not harm his breath; do not harm his sight; do not harm his hearing; do not harm his ear.

Whatever in you is cruel, whatever is fixed, purify that with this; beautify it for the gods. Do not harm his limbs; do not harm his feet; do not harm his navel; do not harm his penis; do not harm his anus.
Do not harm this; may there be peace for the waters.
O herb, protect him; O axe, do not harm him.
With that body of yours which is most auspicious, touch him.

For the earth! You are the portion of the Rākṣasas. Here I repel the Rākṣasa; here I lead the Rākṣasa into the lowest darkness. For food you, for strength you! Be purified for the gods; be adorned for the gods!
May Heaven and Earth cover [you] with ghee. For such-and-such, you who are beloved—homage to the sight of the sun!
Pervade the wide mid-air! The Rakṣas is burnt away, the enemy is burnt away! O Vāyu, may the drops of fat be free from hatred! Svāhā! Go to the god Marut, whose path is the upward sky!
The hatreds:
*svāhā* to the upward-moving one, the beloved oblation for the gods, rich in ghee; for such-and-such [deity], thee, the beloved! Thou art the impeller; may Agni cook thee; may the waters [cook thee].
They have sent you forth; for the speed of Vāta, for the rush of Pūṣan, so that you may not falter before the heat. You are the essence of the waters and the plants;
O drinkers of ghee, drink the ghee! O drinkers of fat, drink the fat! You are the oblation of the atmosphere; *svāhā*!
To Vāta, to the quarters, the intermediate quarters, the directed quarters, the sub-quarters, the upward quarters—to the quarters! May Indra’s breath settle within every limb.
Indra’s apāna has settled within every limb; Indra’s vyāna has pervaded every limb.
O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, may your abundant wealth come together, that which has become multiform yet possesses a single mark.
May your friends, your mother, and your father rejoice after you as you go among the gods for their protection.

Go to the ocean, svāhā! Go to the intermediate space, svāhā! Go to the god Savitṛ, svāhā! Go to day and night, svāhā! Go to Mitra and Varuṇa, svāhā! Go to heaven and earth, svāhā! Go to the meters, svāhā! Go to Soma, svāhā! Go to the sacrifice, svāhā! Go to the celestial firmament, svāhā! Go to Agni Vaiśvānara, svāhā!
May the mind bestow heart-strength upon you; I take you from the plants.
From every bond, O King Varuṇa, release us from here; whatever we have sworn by the waters, by the inviolable cows, or by Varuṇa himself—from that, O Varuṇa, release us.
O Varuṇa, loosen the highest bond from us, untie the lowest, and release the middle one.
Then, O Āditya, being under your protection, may we be sinless before Aditi.
May waters and plants be well-disposed toward us;
may they be ill-disposed toward him who hates us and whom we hate.
Rich in oblations are these waters; rich in oblations is the divine sacrifice. Rich in oblations he seeks to win [the gods]; may Sūrya be rich in oblations.
[I,29] "I set you down in the seat of Agni, whose house is unassailable. You are the portions of the gods; you are the portions of Indra and Agni;
you are the portions of Mitra and Varuṇa; you are the portions of all the gods; you are seekers of favor."
Bestow favor upon us for the sake of favor.
For the sake of the favor of all; for the heart thee, for the mind thee, for the sky thee, for the sun thee.
Direct this sacrifice upward to heaven among the gods; perform the office of the Hotṛ.
May Agni hear my call with the fuel; may the Waters and the divine Dhiṣaṇās hear;
O pressing-stones, you who are wise, hear now the sacrifice; may the god Savitṛ hear my call.
The goddesses:

"And the goddess Dhiṣaṇā"—thus [are] the goddesses, the waters. Of the waters, that wave which is fit for oblation, endowed with power, most intoxicating—that [wave] [I offer] to the gods who drink the bright [Soma].

To you who have a share, [I give] the oblation; Svāhā! You are the furrower. For the sake of the ocean’s imperishability, for the pouring out, you are the washing waters of the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas. O Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas, these are your washing waters. Follow the Gandharva dwelling in the ocean, the one praised by the flight of the wind. In your auspicious sight, may I deposit all seed; in accordance with your auspicious sight.
O Agni, that mortal whom you protect in battles and whom you urge on in the contests for booty—
he shall be the master of eternal refreshments.
May I be beloved of speech; may I be beloved of the Lord of Speech. That which is the honeyed essence of speech—to that, Svāhā! Svāhā to Sarasvatī!
You are the Nigrābhyās, heard by the gods; satisfy me! Satisfy my life-span! Satisfy me! Satisfy my out-breath!
Satisfy me! Satisfy my in-breath! Satisfy me! Satisfy my diffused breath! Satisfy me! Satisfy my eye! Satisfy me! Satisfy my ear! Satisfy me! Satisfy my mind! Satisfy me! Satisfy me!
Do not let my speech thirst; satisfy it! Satisfy my self; satisfy it! Satisfy my offspring;
satisfy it! Satisfy my house; satisfy it! Satisfy my cattle; satisfy them! Do not let me thirst along with my groups; satisfy me!

At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee up. Thou art the pressing-stone, the performer of the sacrifice; for the gods, perform this deep sacrifice.
For Indra thee, most well-pressed, honeyed, and milky;
for Indra thee, O slayer of the adversary; for Indra thee, accompanied by the Vasus and the Rudras; for Indra thee, accompanied by the Ādityas.
For Agni, thee, the giver of increase of wealth; for Viṣṇu, thee; for the Falcon, thee, the bearer of Soma; for Viṣṇu, thee.
[Page I,31] You are auspicious, O subduers of Vṛtra; prosper, you praised wives of immortality!
O goddesses, bestow this sacrifice upon the gods; being invited, drink of the Soma.

O Soma, whatever light is yours in heaven, whatever on earth, and whatever in the wide mid-air—with that, create wide space for wealth for this lord of the sacrifice; speak in favor of the Creator. Do not fear, do not tremble; bestow strength, bestow strength upon us.
O two praised ones, be praised; bestow strength, bestow strength upon us. May I not harm you two, nor may I harm us.
For you two must destroy [them].
Flow for Vācaspati, purified by the hands from the stalks of the bull.
O god, you are the purifier of the gods; you are the portion of those [gods] to whom it belongs.
Make our nourishments honey-sweet. You are self-fashioned; enter the wide mid-air. For all divine and earthly powers, may the mind take hold of you!
*Svāhā* to you, O auspicious one, for Sūrya! For the gods who drink the rays of light, for the vital breath (*prāṇa*), I take you!
That invincible, watchful name of yours, O Soma—for that Soma of yours, O Soma, *svāhā*! Eastward, westward, downward.
O Mother, let these quarters run toward you with joy; do not forget us, so that the enemy may be found.
O descendant of Tvaṣṭṛ,
you are taken with a support.
O Maghavan, grant us what is within; protect the Soma, preserve our wealth, and win for us nourishments through sacrifice.
I place you within heaven and earth; I place you within the wide mid-air.
In harmony with the gods, both those below and those above, O Maghavan, rejoice in the Antaryāma cup!
May speech protect thee, Svāhā! To thee, O auspicious one, for Sūrya; to thee for the gods who drink the rays of light; to thee for out-breath! MS_1,3.5.
O Vāyu, drinker of the pure, come to us; a thousand are your teams, O possessor of all boons.
To you this intoxicating juice is offered, of which, O God, you have the first draught.
You are taken with a support; for Vāyu, you!
O Indra and Vāyu, these pressed juices are here; come hither with refreshments, for the drops long for you both.
You are taken with a support; for Vāyu, for Indra and Vāyu, you! This is your womb; for the two who are in harmony, you!
O Mitra and Varuṇa, increasers of cosmic order, this Soma has been pressed for you; hear my invocation here.
[Page I,33] You are taken with a support; for Mitra and Varuṇa you are; this is your womb; for the seekers of Truth (ṛtāyu) you are.
O Aśvins, with that whip of yours which is honeyed and full of pleasant truth,
sprinkle the sacrifice.
You are taken with a support; for the Aśvins you are; this is your womb; for the two Mādhvīs you are.
You are taken with a support; for the gods you are taken with a support; for the Viśvedevas you are taken with a support; for all the gods you are taken with a support.
I have performed the rite for the sons of Diti and Aditi, who provide wide shelter, who are great and possess vast protection—
those whose names are established according to their stations, whom people worship with their thoughts for the sake of the world’s life.
Thou art taken with a support; I take thee in the wide-striding step of Viṣṇu. O Viṣṇu of the wide stride, this is thy Soma;

guard it, let not the evil-eyed ones harm thee. Let not the ill-seeing one look upon thee. This Vasu, Purovasu, the guardian of speech—may he protect my speech. This Vasu, Vidadvasu, the guardian of the eye—may he protect my eye. This Vasu, Saṃyadvasu, the guardian of the ear—[may he protect my ear].
May he protect me.
This Vena impels the Pṛśnigarbhas, whose womb is light, in the measurement of the mid-air;
at the meeting-place of the waters and the sun, the sages lick him with their prayers as if he were an infant.
You are taken with a support; for Śaṇḍa you! This is your womb; for heroism you!

Him, the sovereign of the eldest, seated upon the sacred grass, beholder of heaven, who turns toward us with his strength—him we milk with our song as of old, as in former times, as always, as now; he who is swift and victorious, in whom you grow great.
You are taken with a support; for Marka you are; this is your womb; for progeny you are.
Śaṇḍa and Marka have been driven away along with him whom we hate. O divine Soma, may we be the partakers of this unbroken strength, of the increase of wealth, and of heroic vigor.
Tutha art thou, the progenitor of men; may the gods who drink the *śukra* lead thee forward. Tutha art thou, the progenitor of men; may the gods who drink the *manthin* lead thee forward.
Thou art unassailable; generating heroic offspring, go around; generating offspring with good progeny, go around [them].
With Indra as my ally and with fury, may I drive back those who attack me,
slaying the enemies without opposition.

Meeting together with heaven and earth, you two bright ones of bright luster—O gods Śukra and Manthin, bestow life upon the sacrifice and life upon the lord of the sacrifice; place a male embryo within the two wombs; bestow the vital breaths upon the cattle. You are the station of the Śukra;
you are the station of the Manthin. Śaṇḍas is cast out, Markas is cast out, along with him whom we hate.

That which is the first consecration in this sacrifice, that which is the supreme Bṛhaspati the wise, that which is the middle one—Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni—to that Indra offer the pressed [soma]; to that Sūrya offer the pressed [soma].
O gods who are eleven in heaven, who are eleven upon the earth, and who dwell in the waters as eleven by your greatness— O gods, may you graciously accept this sacrifice.
O gods! You are taken with a support; you are the foremost draught (*āgrayaṇa*), you are the true *āgrayaṇa*. Quicken the sacrifice, quicken the lord of the sacrifice;
protect the libations. Therefore, let Viṣṇu protect you; protect the people with your power. This is your birthplace; for all the gods, you are taken.
You are taken with a support.
For Indra, the possessor of the great, the possessor of vigor, thee who art eager for the hymn;
that which is thy great vigor, O Indra—for that [I take] thee; for Viṣṇu, thee.

This is your womb; for Indra you are taken with a supporting base. For the gods you, who desire the gods, I take you. You are the oblation again; for the gods you, who desire the gods, I fill; for the life of the sacrifice.
The gods generated from their mouth the head of heaven, the steward of earth, Vaiśvānara Agni born in the cosmic order (ṛta)—
the seer, the sovereign, the guest of men— as a vessel for their mouths.
You are taken with a support; for Vaiśvānara, you!
You are firm, of firm abode, the firmest of the firm, the most immovable of the immovable; this is your womb; for Vaiśvānara, you!
With the firm oblation, we lead Soma for you by the firm path,
so that all people may be well-disposed toward us at our gathering.
In heaven, strengthen those things that are celestial; in the intermediate space, those that belong to the intermediate space; on earth, those that are terrestrial.

You are taken with a support: for Madhu you, for Mādhava you, for Śukra you, for Śuci you, for Nabhas you, for Nabhasya you, for Tveṣa you, for Ūrja you, for Sahas you, for Sahasya you, for Tapas you, for Tapasya you.
O Indra and Agni, come to the pressed juice, to the desirable cloud through our songs;
drink of this, impelled by our prayer.
You are taken with a support; for Indra and Agni you are; this is your womb; for Indra and Agni you are.
O protectors of the people, all you gods, come hither;
you who are givers, come to the pressed juice of the donor.
You are taken with a support; for all the gods you are taken. This is your womb; for all the gods you are taken.
O Indra, accompanied by the Maruts, drink the Soma here, just as you drank of the pressed juice at Śāryāta’s sacrifice.
Under your guidance and in your protection, O Hero, the sages who perform fair sacrifices seek to win your favor.
You are taken with a support; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you! This is your womb; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you!
You were born fierce for victorious power, delightful, most mighty, and full of great pride;
even the Maruts strengthened Indra on that occasion when his mother gave birth to the hero—thus you were born.
You are taken with a support; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you! This is your womb; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you!

I invoke here for new protection that Indra, who is accompanied by the Maruts, the bull who has grown great, the one whose enemies are never deficient, the divine ruler, the all-conquering, the fierce giver of victory.
You are taken with a support; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you! This is your birthplace; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you!
Accompanied by the Maruts, O Indra, as a bull for the battle, drink the Soma according to your custom for exhilaration.
Pour the wave of honeyed juice into your belly; you have been the king of the pressed juices from of old.
You are taken with a support; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you! This is your seat: for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you!
O Indra, together with your troop, the Maruts, drink the Soma, O wise hero, slayer of Vṛtra!
Slay the enemies, drive away the adversaries, and then grant us security from every side.
You are taken with a support; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you! This is your seat; for Indra accompanied by the Maruts, you!
Great is Indra through his might, like Parjanya rich in rain;
he has been strengthened by the hymns of Vatsa.
You are taken with a support; for Mahendra you are; this is your womb; for Mahendra you!
Great is Indra, manly, the filler of the people, doubly vast and immeasurable in his powers. He has grown strong for our sake, a hero; broad and wide, he has been made well-fashioned by the makers.
You are taken with a support; for Mahendra you are; this is your womb; for Mahendra you are.
Never art thou barren, O Indra; thou never failest the worshipper.
More and more, O Maghavan, let thy bounty increase; indeed, the gift of thee, the god, is ever being added to.
You are taken with a support; for the Ādityas, you!
Never do you neglect; you guard both worlds.
O Āditya, the fourth libation is your power; you have established immortality in heaven.
You are taken with a support; for the Ādityas, you!
May the sacrifice reach the favor of the gods; O Ādityas, be gracious to us.
May your benevolence turn toward us, which finds wider space even from distress.
I am above, I am below; I am the king of the entire world.
I have beheld the sun on both sides; that which is the intermediate space has become our father.
Raise up the earth; cleave open this celestial firmament.
O Dhātṛ, as the lord, unbind for us the leather bag of the celestial waters.
O Savitṛ, with your unfailing and auspicious protections, guard us today for our prosperity. O golden-tongued one, protect us for ever-new well-being; let no one who speaks evil have power over us.

You are taken with a support; you belong to Savitṛ, the sustainer of people. Enliven the sacrifice, enliven the lord of the sacrifice; protect the libations! From here let Viṣṇu protect you; protect the people with your power.
You are taken with a support.
You are well-protected, you are well-established; homage to the great bull!
This is your womb; for all the gods, you!
You are taken with a support; of you, O Indu, who are pressed by Bṛhaspati and possessed of power, [I take a portion].
May I successfully attain the draught accompanied by its consort.
O Agni, accompanied by the wives, in harmony with Tvaṣṭṛ, drink the Soma.

You are taken with a support; you are the bay one, the yoker of bays, possessed of bays, the rider of the two bays. O divine Soma, you for whom the *stoma* has been praised, the *uktha* recited, and the *yajus* offered.
May I successfully obtain the draught belonging to the one with bay horses, the yoker of bay horses, that which possesses bay horses.
For the two bay horses, the parched grains accompanied by the bay horses; for Indra, together with Soma, thee for wealth, thee for prosperity!
O Agni, purifying yourself, send forth our lifespans; bring us strength and nourishment, and drive misfortune far away.
You are taken with a support; for Agni, the long-lived, you are taken. This is your womb; for Agni, the long-lived, you are taken.
His vital energy blazed forth when Indra rolled together both worlds like a hide.
You are taken with a support; for Indra the powerful, you! This is your resting place; for Indra the powerful, you!
His banners have been seen, his rays extending over the people,
shining like blazing fires.
You are taken with a support; for Sūrya, the radiant, you! This is your birthplace; for Sūrya, the radiant, you!
The two bay steeds carry Indra, whose power is unassailable,
toward the praises of the seers and toward the sacrifice of human beings.
You are taken with a support; for Indra accompanied by the bay horses, you! This is your womb; for Indra accompanied by the bay horses, you!

You are taken with a support; for Prajāpati, the luminous, I take you, the luminous. Given to the gods, the increaser of skill, for the sake of the skillful ones; for you, who are devoted to the *ṛta*, for those whose chief is Indra, whose king is Varuṇa, who have Vāta as their food and Parjanya as their soul; for the earth, for the intermediate space, for the sky, for the waters, for the plants.
For the trees thee; for out-breathing thee, for in-breathing thee, for diffused breathing thee; for what is existent thee, for what is non-existent thee, for the past thee, for the future thee.
For that Prajāpati Viśvakarman, who is all-pervading and the giver of wide abundance, by whom creatures were born without defect—for him I offer this wide portion, Svāhā!
The Uśijs prepared three fuel-sticks for Agni, the encompassing one, so that he might be immortal;
of these, they placed one as sustenance among mortals, while two, as sisters, entered the world.

May Agni protect us from the morning libation—Vaiśvānara, the one who brings glory to all and is the source of well-being for all. May he, the purifier, bestow wealth upon us; may we be long-lived and share in the sacrificial draught together.
I pluck you for Agni with the Gāyatrī metre; I pluck you for Indra with the Triṣṭubh metre;
I pluck you for the Ādityas with the Jagatī metre. I shake you in the flight-path of the gladdening drops; I shake you in the flight-path of the exhilarating drops;
I shake you in the flight-path of the praising drops; I shake you in the flight-path of the purifying drops; [I shake you] in the flight-path of the domestic ones.
I shake thee in the flight of the birds; I shake thee in the flight of the honeyed ones; I shake thee in the flight of the sweet-flowing ones;

I shake thee in the flight of those that go to the gods. Thou art taken with a support; I take thee, the bright one, O bright one, for the sake of the bright, in the form of the day, in the rays of the sun.
The streams from heaven have been poured forth, flowing unceasingly unto the ocean.

The Kakubha-form of the Bull shines forth; at the meditation upon the Vasus, at the ritual act of the Rudras, and in the mind of the Ādityas, I offer you for Indra’s pervading power. O divine Soma, you are the yearning one; with the Gāyatrī metre, go to the abode of Agni.
O divine Soma, you who have mastery, come to the abode of Indra with the Triṣṭubh metre; O divine Soma, our friend, come to the beloved station of all the gods with the Jagatī metre.
His rays bear up that god Jātavedas,
Sūrya, so that everyone may behold him.
The brilliant face of the gods has risen, the eye of Mitra, Varuṇa, and Agni.
Sūrya has filled the heaven, the earth, and the mid-air; he is the soul of all that moves and stands still.
Go to heaven, go to the light; I approach your form with my form, your vitality with my vitality. May Tutha, the all-knowing, distribute you upon the highest vault of the earth.
This gift of yours, O Agni, comes forth, stirred by Soma; lead it along the path of Mitra.
May this Agni create wide space for us; may he go before us, shattering our adversaries.
May he, exulting, conquer the enemies; may he win the prize in the struggle for booty.

Go forth by the path of Truth, O you who give away the moon as a sacrificial fee! May I today prosper through this Brahmin, who is endowed with a father and grandfathers, who is a seer descended from seers, and who is the recipient of a well-bestowed sacrificial fee.
Behold the sun; behold the mid-air. Strive with those in the assembly. O you who are given by us, go to the gods, rich in sweetness.
Enter the giver. Without abandoning us, sit in the world of the doers of good by the path that leads to the gods. May this be prepared for us.
May Dhātṛ, Rāti, and Savitṛ enjoy this; may Prajāpati, Varuṇa, Mitra, and Agni, as well as Viṣṇu and Tvaṣṭṛ, bestowing wealth upon the sacrificer together with progeny, grant him riches.

O Indra, Lord of the Bay Steeds, unite us with our minds, with cattle, with wise patrons, and with well-being; unite us with the sacred prayer that is fashioned by the gods, and with the benevolent favor of the deities worthy of sacrifice.
We have united with splendor, with nourishment, and with our bodies; we have united with a gracious mind.
May Tvaṣṭṛ, the bounteous giver, bestow wealth upon us and mend whatever in our bodies is injured.
O gods, I prepare easy seats for you who have come here, enjoying this libation;
having all eaten and drunk, O Vasus, bestow riches upon us.
O divine Agni, send those gods whom you bring here according to their desire back to their own dwelling place;
carrying and bearing the oblations, may they ascend to heaven along with the vital breath and the heated offering.
Since we have chosen you today here as the Hotṛ priest at this proceeding sacrifice, O Agni—
having sacrificed successfully and having performed the service successfully, come to the sacrifice as one who is wise and all-knowing.

O sacrifice, go to the sacrifice; go to the lord of the sacrifice; go to your own source, svāhā! This is your sacrifice, O lord of the sacrifice, accompanied by the Sūktavāka and rich in heroic sons; through that, come into being; go to splendor! O gods who know the way, having found the way, go upon the way!
O Lord of the Mind, place this well-prepared sacrifice in heaven among the gods, svāhā!
For King Varuṇa has made wide for Sūrya a path to follow;
he has provided feet to set down where there was no place to stand, and he is the remover even of that which pierces the heart.
A hundred physicians are yours, O King, a thousand; may your benevolent thought be vast and deep.
Drive Nirṛti far away to the distance; release from us whatever sin has been committed.
The face of Agni has entered the waters; the Son of the Waters protects the divine powers.
O Agni, sacrifice this fuel in each case; let your tongue rise up toward the clarified butter.
In the ocean is your heart, within the waters; may the plants and the waters enter into you.
O Lord of the Sacrifice, let us pay homage to you with well-spoken words and the utterance of "namas" at this sacrifice.

Svāhā! O Avabhṛtha, you are Nicuṅkuṇa, the gliding one; you are Nicuṅkuṇa, house by house. With the gods, remove from us the sin committed against the gods; with mortals, remove the sin committed against mortals, O wise one. O God, protect us from wide-reaching harm. O divine Soma, of you who are washed in the waters and praised by men—of that portion of yours which wins cattle and that which wins horses—these have been invited.
I partake of that which has been invited; Varuṇa’s noose is loosened, Varuṇa’s noose is cast away. Homage to Varuṇa! O Unnetṛ, raise me up to a better state.
Upward rise to you these most honey-sweet songs, these hymns of praise,
like chariots seeking booty, ever-conquering, winning wealth, and possessing inexhaustible aid.
Like the Kaṇvas, like the Bhṛgus, like the Sūryas, they have attained everything that is beneficial.
May they rise up, bestowing progeny and splendor; through you, may riches and sacrifices flow unceasingly.
Take hold according to the Gāyatrī metre; then may you be fragrant in our homes. You are fuel; may we prosper. You are kindling; may we thrive.
I have followed after the waters today; we have united with their essence.
Rich in milk, O Agni, I have come; unite me with splendor.
O Agni, may splendor be mine in our invocations; kindling you, may we nourish our bodies.
May the four quarters bow down to me; with you as our overseer, may we conquer the hostile armies.
O Agni, Lord of Vows, I shall undertake a vow; we declare it to you; protect it for us; may I be able to fulfill it.
I invoke that Agni, the Hotṛ; may we sacrifice here to the gods worthy of worship.
May the gods partake of this my oblation; may the gods come, being well-disposed.
I yoke you with divine prayer, O Jātavedas, to carry this oblation.
Kindling you, may we live long with good offspring and brave heroes, offering tribute to you.
May Indra bestow power upon us; may wealthy patrons attend to us;
may our prayers be fulfilled.
Yes! Desiring the fulfillment of our blessings, we call upon those accompanied by Indra; may we milk forth offspring and nourishment.
May this my true blessing go to the gods—more pleasing than what is already pleasing, more desirable than what is already desirable.
Go to the gods with a mind free from anger; may the sacrifice go to the gods; may the sacrifice reach the gods.
I loosen your girth-strap, I loosen your reins, I loosen your yokes and the leather thongs.
Grant us here auspicious wealth; declare me a giver of portions among the deities.
The sacrifice was offered by the Bhṛgus as a giver of wealth, by the Yatis as a giver of blessings, and by the Vasus;
the Aṅgirases have offered it for me with the morning recitations of this sacrifice.

May the wealth of that sacrifice which has been offered and consumed come here to me; may the sacrifice be wealthy, may the sacrifice be rich in riches. May the wealth of that sacrifice, of that which is rich in riches, come here to me; may it come from there to me; may it come from there to me.

Thou art united with the blessing of the lord of the sacrifice; be thou present for me. Thou art full; be thou full for me. Thou art all; be thou all for me. Thou art imperishable; be thou imperishable for me. May the gods and the officiating priests purify [us] by the eastern quarter;
may the months and the fathers purify [us] by the southern quarter; may the houses and the cattle purify [us] by the western quarter; by the northern...
May the guardians of the quarters, the herbs, and the trees purify [us]. May the sacrifice and the year purify [us] through the upward direction.

Viṣṇu strode across the earth with the Gāyatrī metre; excluded is he whom we hate. Viṣṇu strode across the intermediate space with the Triṣṭubh metre; excluded is he whom we hate. Viṣṇu strode across the sky...

Excluded by the Jāgata metre, he whom we hate has gone to the light; we have become united with the light. I here bind up the breath of so-and-so. You are brilliance; may I be united with offspring, and may offspring be united with me; may I be united with cattle, and may cattle be united with me.
O Agni, lord of the house, through you as lord of the house, may I be a good lord of the house, a good lord of the house.

May you be with me, O householder; let our household fire shine undisturbed for a hundred winters. May we two, bestowing gifts upon one another, yet not mingling our bodies, remain here. Let not the divine thread be severed after me, nor the human;
may I not be cut off from the divine abode, nor from the human light. For the sake of light and for the sake of the thread, I take you.
Those gods who, as destroyers of the sacrifice, dwell upon the earth—may Agni protect us from them; may we, the doers of good deeds, go forth.
Those gods who sit upon the earth as stealers of the sacrifice—may Agni protect us from them; may we go to the world of those who have performed good deeds.
O Savitṛ, those nights of yours which lead to the gods and have gathered toward the thousandfold sacrifice—
may we, ascending first with all our households and progeny, cross over the regions of the air to the world of light.
Those gods who, slayers of the sacrifice, dwell above in the intermediate space—may Vāyu protect us from them; may we go to those who have performed good deeds.
Those gods who, as stealers of the sacrifice, dwell in the intermediate space—may Vāyu protect us from them; may we go to the world of those who have performed good deeds.
We have come, O Mitra and Varuṇa, by your choice, to that portion of yours which belongs to the nights;
grasping the firmament in the world of the well-done, upon the third ridge in the luminous realm of heaven.
Those gods who sit above in heaven, slayers of the sacrifice—may Sūrya protect us from them; may we go to the world of those who have performed good deeds.
Those gods who sit above in heaven, robbing the sacrifice—may Sūrya protect us from them; may we, as doers of good deeds, go forth.
O Jātavedas, with that same supreme oblation with which they prepared the milks for Indra, with that, O Agni, do thou cause me to prosper; place me in the preeminence among my kinsmen.
You are the Veda; bring the Veda to me. I am satisfied; you are satisfied.
May the Veda grant me strength— rich in ghee, providing a nest, an abundance of wealth, and thousandfold.
Drive away the hater, burn away the enemy; O Rudras, you have grasped him; O Ādityas, you have spread him out.
O Agni, this sacrifice is rich in cattle, rich in horses, and has heroes as its companions; it is ever unassailable.
O Asura, it is provided with sacrificial food, rich in progeny, long-lasting wealth, broad-based, and fit for the assembly hall.

May the wife go with her husband to their good deeds; may they become the two yoke-horses harnessed to the sacrifice. Cherishing one another, may they cast away hostility; may you both grasp the highest light in heaven—Svāhā!
They were [the two wives]: "O wife, this is your world; homage be to you! Do not harm me. To Sarasvatī, who causes one to enter the dwelling, Svāhā!"
Of that Sarasvatī who possesses the fortune of a dwelling, may we be the ones devoted to her.
O Agni, you are *ayās* (unwearied) and free from reproach; truly, you are *ayās*.
Being *ayās*, you have been fashioned by the mind; being *ayās*, you have carried the oblation. As *ayās*, bestow healing upon us—*svāhā*!

The sacrifice has gone to the world of the gods; from there may the blessing of the sacrifice come to me. The sacrifice has gone to the world of the ancestors; from there may the blessing of the sacrifice come to me. The sacrifice has gone to the world of men; from there may the blessing of the sacrifice come to me. The sacrifice has gone to the waters, the plants, and the trees; from there may the blessing of the sacrifice come to me. [The sacrifice has gone] to the world of the five peoples.
The sacrifice has come; may the blessing of the sacrifice come to me from there. I take thee for the support of the five winds;
I take thee for the support of the five directions; I take thee for the support of the five waters;
I take thee for the support of the five ridges; I take thee for the support of the five peoples; [I take] thee for the oblation.
I take [this] for the upholder of the five openings.
Thou art the beloved abode of the gods, the unassailable place of sacrifice for the gods;
I take thee for the feast of the gods.
Bhūḥ! This is our oblation for the gods; may there be blessings for the sacrificer. For the deities, I take you with the deities.

The New and Full Moon sacrifices are indeed a complete sacrifice. To whom do the deities come for the sacrifice when he is about to sacrifice, and to whom do they not? Among many sacrificers on the same day, he who takes up the fire on the previous day worships the deities on the following morning.
He takes up the fire first with the words, "O Agni, may there be splendor for me in the invocations," for the deities are indeed [the ones who attend].

He takes these [vessels] on the previous day; on the following day, he performs the sacrifice with the sacrificial grass (*barhis*). Indeed, they enter upon the vow at the full moon with the grass, and at the new moon with the calves. Before the calves are driven away, the husband and wife should eat. Having washed their hands, they should stand to the south of the fire, [the husband saying]: "O Agni, lord of vows, I shall undertake the vow. For Agni is the lord of vows among the gods, and the Brahmin is [the lord of vows].
Having announced it to the Lord of Vows, the one who maintains the vow takes hold of the vow with the words, "I invoke Agni, the Hotṛ, him toward whom [I call].
He should touch whatever sacrificial oblation he is about to pour out; for this is the seizing of the deities, and by this he has seized the deities.
While the enclosing sticks are being laid around, he should say, "I yoke thee with the divine sacred word"; for this is indeed the yoking of Agni.

With the words, "He yokes the fire; he yokes for him so that it may carry the oblation; may Indra bestow power upon us," he should speak as the *iḍā* is being invoked. This is indeed the milking of the *iḍā*; he thus milks the *iḍā*, and since the *iḍā* is power, he places power within himself.
With the words, "O, [we are] desirous of milking the blessings," they indeed approach the sacrificer desiring to milk the blessings. These [blessings]...

On the south side, he stands worshipping the world of the sacrificer. Just as cows that have not been milked might walk away, so do the blessings (āśis) depart from him who does not know this; but from him who knows this, he milks the very blessings. When the *prastara* is being thrown [into the fire], he should say: "May this my true blessing go to the gods. Having thus caused his true blessing to go to the gods, he then [proceeds].
"One should choose a boon; for indeed Aupāvi Jānaśruteya, having sacrificed with a thousand [cows], said: 'What boon indeed shall we choose beyond this?

[The response was: 'Sacrifice with a thousand! This is what he used to say before that time. When the enclosing-sticks (*paridhi*) are being thrown in, one should recite: 'I loosen your tether, I loosen your reins. For these deities [lead] to the heavenly world."
"Having caused it to go and having established it, the sacrifice was completed by the Bhṛgus"—this is indeed the milking of the sacrifice; he thus milks the sacrifice.
Regarding this, Kāpivana Bhauvāyana used to say: "What use would he have for a sacrifice who does not milk the sacrifice as one would a cow? For the cow is easier to milk."

With the words, "The lord of the sacrifice [attains] his blessing," the sacrificer eats the sacrificer’s portion. The lord of the sacrifice is indeed the sacrificer, and the sacrificer’s portion is the sacrifice.

In that the sacrificer eats the sacrificer’s portion, he establishes the sacrifice in the very lord of the sacrifice. If he should go away on a journey, he should offer it together with the *samiṣṭayajus*; thus he establishes the sacrifice in Agni. As for the oblation...

When about to pour out [the oblation], he heats it over the fire; thus he constructs the sacrifice from Agni itself. And when, about to pour out the sacrificial food, he announces it to the sacrificer, he constructs the sacrifice from the Lord of the Sacrifice himself. Indeed, Agni consumes much;
but when these waters are released, the sacrificer is thereby liberated from this world. The flow must be made continuous.

By means of water, the sacrificer thus interposes himself between himself and the fire. There are two kinds of gods who come to the house of the sacrificer: some are Soma-drinkers and others are non-Soma-drinkers; some are eaters of oblations and others are non-eaters of oblations. Those who are Brāhmaṇas are indeed the gods who do not eat oblations; he who has not previously sacrificed has these as his deities. These [Brāhmaṇas] indeed have power over his offspring and his cattle.

If they are not pleased with him, they depart, taking away his nourishment (*iṣ*) and vigor (*ūrj*). When he brings the *anvāhārya* (the guest-offering), he thereby gratifies them. He says, "Let it be carried around for those seated to the south"; thus he performs the sacrifice with a sacrifice that possesses sacrificial fees (*dakṣiṇā*). By means of the oblations, he gratifies the gods who consume the offerings;
they, being gratified, bestow nourishment and vigor upon him.
"You are existent; may you be existent for me"—these are indeed blessings, and he thus secures them for himself. "You are full;

may you be full for me"—for indeed, one becomes full there in the other world with all one's limbs. "You are everything; may you be everything for me"—for indeed, one becomes everything there in the other world with all one's limbs. "You are undecaying; may you be undecaying for me"—for indeed, one becomes undecaying there in the other world with all one's limbs.

"May the gods, the officiating priests, purify [us] from the eastern direction"—these indeed are the purifications of the sacrifice, these are the pacifications. The Baidavāpayas knew them; for them, the sacrifice became purified and pacified, and Paśupati became harmless toward their cattle.
He who knows thus—his sacrifice becomes purified and pacified, and Paśupati becomes harmless toward his cattle.

"Viṣṇu strode through the earth with the Gāyatrī metre"—for the gods, having Viṣṇu as their leader, drove the Asuras away from these worlds and went to the heavenly world. Thus, the sacrificer, having Viṣṇu as his leader, drives his rival away from these worlds and goes to the heavenly world. With the words, "We have gone to heaven," he indeed goes to the heavenly world.
"United with light, we have become," for the heavenly world is indeed light; "here do I entwine the breath of so-and-so," he says, and thus he entwines his very breath.
He turns around in this manner, for in this manner the sacrifice turns around;
moreover, he turns around following the turning of that sun. "Thou art brilliance," he says, for fire is indeed brilliance. He, having abandoned his offspring...

And he goes to heaven with offspring and cattle when he says, "May I be united with offspring, may offspring be united with me; may I be united with cattle, may cattle be united with me. Thus he finds firm support in offspring and in cattle.
