The deity is the fruit, the wealth; you are the brilliance of Soma, the brilliant one. May my brilliance be like yours.
The head of Namuci has been cast down; the biting serpents have been bound.
Protect me from death, O Shining One; protect me!

Hail to Agni! Hail to Soma! Hail to Savitṛ! Hail to Sarasvatī! Hail to Pūṣan! Hail to Bṛhaspati! Hail to Indra! Hail to Ghoṣa! Hail to Śloka! Hail to Aṃśa! Hail to Bhaga! Hail to the Lord of the Field!
With the splendor of Soma, with the brilliance of Agni, with the power of Indra, and with [the power] of all the gods, I take thee.
I consecrate you with sacred power; you are the womb of Indra; give birth to the days; protect [us].
From below they have turned upward, following after Ahi Budhnya;
like well-pouring voices, those ships spread out from the back of the bull-like mountain.
Thou art Indra’s thunderbolt, the winner of booty; through thee may this man win booty. By the command of Mitra and Varuṇa, the two directors, I yoke thee.

Thou art Viṣṇu’s stride, the slayer of rivals. In the impulse of the Maruts, may we conquer and obtain the mind. May it be united with power; this is the thunderbolt, the best winner of booty; by it may our son win booty.
So great is your life; grant me life. You are a yoke; you are luster; grant me luster. You are vigor; grant me vigor.
You are Mitra; you are Varuṇa; you are the foundation. May I be united with all the gods. Homage to Mother Earth! May Mother Earth not harm me.
That name and sovereignty have been established against [us]; Varuṇa has drawn forth his own body.
We have become observers of the holy laws of the pure Mitra; we have meditated upon the great name of Ṛta.
We have all become the subjects of Varuṇa; the seeker of Mitra has overcome the malevolent spirits.
The worshipful ones have shone forth by means of the eternal Law (ṛta); Trita has brought our old age to an end.
Thou art pleasant, a good seat; sit upon the pleasant one, sit upon the good seat.
Varuṇa, firm in his vows and wise in action, sat down upon the dwellings for the sake of universal sovereignty.
Svāhā to Agni! Svāhā to Soma! Svāhā to the vigor of Indra! Svāhā to the strength of the Maruts!
The swan dwelling in the pure, the Vasu dwelling in the mid-air, the Hotṛ-priest dwelling at the altar, the guest dwelling in the house;
dwelling among men, dwelling in the best, dwelling in Truth, dwelling in the sky; born of the waters, born of the kine, born of Truth, born of the mountains—He is the Eternal Law (Ṛta).

O Brahman, you are the Brahman; you are Savitṛ, whose impulse is truth. O Brahman, you are the Brahman; you are Mitra, the very gracious one. You are the Brahman; you are Indra, whose power is truth. O Brahman, you are the Brahman; you are Varuṇa, whose power is all-encompassing.
This is the thunderbolt; by it may I overcome the quarters; this one has surpassed them.
O Prajāpati, none other than you has encompassed all these created beings;
may that for which we offer sacrifice be ours.
This one is the son of that person; that one is the son of this person.
May we be masters of riches.
Svāhā to the grandson of the waters! Svāhā to the grandson of strength! Svāhā to Agni, the lord of the household!

A cake on eight potsherds for Savitṛ, with a white animal as the sacrificial fee; a pap for Sarasvatī, with a milch cow as the sacrificial fee; a pap for Pūṣan, with a dark-colored animal as the sacrificial fee;

a pap for Bṛhaspati, with a white-backed animal as the sacrificial fee; a cake on eleven potsherds for Indra, with a bull as the sacrificial fee; a cake made of barley on ten potsherds for Varuṇa, with a large, reddish-brown castrated animal as the sacrificial fee;
and a cake on eight potsherds for Tvaṣṭṛ, with a hornless, thick-necked animal as the sacrificial fee.
An oblation on eight potsherds for Agni-Soma with a bull as the sacrificial fee;

a pap for Soma with a brown animal as the sacrificial fee; an oblation on three potsherds for Viṣṇu with a dwarf as the sacrificial fee; an oblation on eight potsherds for Agni with gold as the sacrificial fee;
a pap for Bṛhaspati with a white-backed animal as the sacrificial fee; an oblation on eleven potsherds for Indra with a bull as the sacrificial fee; [and] an oblation for the Viśve Devas.

A brown sacrificial pap is the fee; a curd-mixture for Mitra and Varuṇa is the fee, a barren cow being the fee; a cake on eight potsherds for Agni, a pap for Soma, a cake on twelve potsherds for Savitṛ, a pap for Bṛhaspati, a cake on twelve potsherds for Agni Vaiśvānara, and a cake on eight potsherds for Tvaṣṭṛ—the right-hand draft-ox that draws the chariot-stand is the fee; a pap for Sarasvatī, a pap for Pūṣan, and [a pap] for Mitra.
A pap for Varuṇa, a pap for Aditi, a pap for the Lord of the Field; a left-hand horse that draws the chariot-stand is the sacrificial fee;

a speckled four-year-old cow that is pregnant is for the Maruts; a hornless goat that is pregnant is for Aditi; a cake on eight potsherds for Savitṛ the Impeller; a cake on eleven potsherds for the Aśvins and Pūṣan; a pap for Sarasvatī of True Speech; a staff and sandals [are the fee].
That sacrificial fee is like a dried leather bag.
Malihā: [FN emended. Ed: malhā. cf.
MS.4.4.9:60.20] "Yoking the mind first, Savitṛ, having realized the intentions for the sake of truth, and having perceived Agni as the light, brought him forth from the earth."
With a disciplined mind, we [act] at the impulse of the god Savitṛ, for the sake of power leading to heaven.
Having yoked the gods who travel through the sky with his thought toward heaven,
Savitṛ impels them as they are about to create the great light.
Going toward the light: "They yoke the mind. [Page II,74] *yuñjate manaḥ*.
I yoke for you both an ancient prayer with prostrations; may the hymn go forth like a wise patron on the path.
May all the sons of immortality hear it, they who have taken up their stations in the celestial realms.
After whose departure all other gods have followed, as they sing the praises of the greatness of that god;
he who measured out the earthly regions with his majesty, that god Savitṛ is Etaśa.
O God Savitṛ!

O God Savitṛ, lead this sacrifice of mine forward, which is directed toward the gods, which finds wealth, which conquers all, which wins riches, and which finds the light of heaven. Accomplish the hymn with the verse, and the Rathantara chant with the Gāyatra melody.
The great one, whose path is the Gāyatrī.
At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take thee up. Thou art a woman;

by the Gāyatrī metre, from the seat of the earth, bring hither Agni Purīṣya in the manner of the Aṅgirases. Thou art the spade; thou art a woman; by the Triṣṭubh metre, may we be able to dig for Agni with thee from his seat; [I take thee] by the Jagatī metre.
Taking it in his hand, Savitṛ, bearing a golden spade and perceiving Agni as light, brought him forth from the earth.
With the Ānuṣṭubh metre.
O vigorous steed, run forth swiftly according to the widest course.
Your highest birth is in heaven; your navel is in the mid-air; your womb is upon the earth.
Yoke the donkey, O you two possessors of abundant wealth, for this journey,
bringing Agni who is well-disposed toward us.
In every endeavor, in every contest, we,
as companions, invoke the most powerful Indra for our protection.
Advancing, come hither; trampling down the curses, come as a source of bliss, belonging to the host of Rudra.
Pervade the wide mid-air.
Creating auspicious pastures and security, together with Pūṣan as his companion.
Bring Agni of the soil in the manner of Aṅgiras; let us go to fetch Agni of the soil in the manner of Aṅgiras; we shall carry Agni of the soil in the manner of Aṅgiras.
Agni has followed after.
Having come along the path, the steed shakes off all adversaries;
he seeks to behold Agni with his eye in the great gathering place.
Having stepped upon the earth, O steed, seek Agni with your luster;
having searched the ground, tell us where we may dig him up.
Heaven is your back, the earth your seat, the atmosphere your soul, and the ocean your womb;
having looked abroad with your eye, trample down those who attack you.
Ascend from this place for great good fortune, O bestower of wealth, O vigorous one!
May we abide in the favor of the Earth while we dig for Agni in her lap.
The giver of wealth, the prize-winning steed, has stepped forth toward this world, the well-prepared, goodly place upon the earth.
From there we shall dig up Agni, the fair-faced one, as we ascend to the highest firmament, to heaven.
I sprinkle you with my mind and with clarified butter, you who dwell facing all beings—
broad, vast with horizontal vitality, most expansive, impetuous, and visible as food.
I sprinkle [the oblation] toward him who faces all directions; may you accept it with a mind free from malice.
Agni, possessing the beauty of a youth and a color that inspires longing, exults in his body and cannot be assailed.
The lord of booty goes around.
O Agni, victorious one, we place you around us as a fortress— you, the inspired sage,
of bold appearance, day by day the slayer of those who deal treacherously.
O Agni, you are born from the heavens; you, O seeker of light, are born from the waters, from the stone, from the forests, and from the plants; O Lord of men, you are born pure.
At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan,

I dig for Agni Purīṣya in the lap of the earth, in the manner of the Aṅgirases— Agni, full of light, fair of aspect, shining with undecaying luster, auspicious to creatures, and non-injurious. In the lap of the earth, I dig for Agni Purīṣya in the manner of the Aṅgirases.
The name of the clan. //MS_2,7.2 //
You are the back of the waters, the womb of Agni, swelling around the ocean;
growing great upon the lotus-leaf, spread yourself out with the measure and the width of heaven.
You two are a shelter and you two are a shield; both of you, unbroken and vast, dwell together in wide space, supporting Agni Purīṣya.
May you two, finding your own light, dwell together in harmony, with your breast and your very self, bearing Agni— the radiant and eternal— between the two ends.
You are the one worthy of the sacrificial food, the sustainer of all; Atharvan was the first to churn you forth, O Agni.
From the lotus, O Agni, Atharvan churned you forth from the head of the entire universe, you the worshipper.
The seer Dadhyañc, the son of Atharvan, kindled you,
the slayer of Vṛtra and the shatterer of forts.
The Pāthya bull has kindled you, the greatest slayer of Dasyus, the winner of wealth in every battle.
Sit down, O Hotṛ, in your own place; being wise, establish the sacrifice in the womb of good deeds.
O Agni, as one who pleases the gods, you shall worship the gods with the oblation; bestow great vital strength upon the sacrificer.
The Hotṛ priest, knowing his place on the Hotṛ’s seat, has sat down—resplendent, shining, and most skillful;
Agni, the most excellent one whose wisdom never fails his sacred vows, who brings a thousandfold wealth, and whose tongue is pure.
Sit down, for you are great; shine forth, O best invoker of the gods!
O Agni, worthy of sacrifice, O praised one, emit your ruddy smoke, beautiful to behold.

Be born indeed as the one to be conquered at the beginning of the days, the ruddy one placed among the woods that are themselves placed; bestowing seven treasures in every house, Agni, the most excellent sacrificer, has sat down as the Hotṛ-priest.
This is here.
[Page II,78] Let us fashion this hymn with our intellect for the worthy Jātavedas, as one fashions a chariot;
for his providence is auspicious for us in the assembly. O Agni, in your friendship may we never suffer harm.
This is yours.
Release the divine waters, rich in sweetness, for the health of all creatures;
from their source let herbs with goodly fruit spring forth.
May Vāyu Mātariśvan restore for you the heart that was torn asunder when you lay supine;
O God, you who move among the gods with their breath—O God, may the *vaṣaṭ* call be unto you!
Well-born with light, he has sat down as a protection and a refuge in the sun; O Agni, rich in radiance, clothe yourself in a garment of every form.
Arise, O you of well-performed sacrifice, being praised with divine grace;
with your sight and great radiance, O Agni, you who are well-shining, come hither with excellent hymns of praise.
Stand up erect for our protection like the god Savitṛ;
standing erect as a winner of booty, when we call upon you with ointments and with priests.
Born as the embryo of the two worlds, O Agni, you are lovely, distributed among the plants;
brilliant as a child, you have outshone the darkness, having stepped forth from your mothers with a loud roar.
Be firm, O you of steadfast limbs; be swift, O steed, O courser.
Be broad and well-seated, you who carry the soil of Agni.
Be auspicious toward the human subjects, O Aṅgiras;
do not harm heaven and earth, nor the intermediate space, nor the trees.
Let the vigorous steed go forth, neighing loudly, the braying donkey, the flyer;
bearing Agni Purīṣya, may he not fall before his full span of life.
Bearing the bull Agni, the bull, the offspring of the waters, the son of the ocean— O Agni, come hither for the feast!
Truth is reality, truth is reality; we bring forth Agni Purīṣya in the manner of Aṅgiras.
O plants, receive this Agni as he approaches you here auspiciously;
driving away all misfortunes and diseases, may he sit down among us and strike away evil intent.
O plants, rejoice in him—ye who are flowering and bear fine fruit;
this germ of yours, born in due season, has taken his seat in the ancient dwelling-place.
Flashing forth with your broad radiance, drive away our enemies, the Rākṣasas, and diseases.
May I abide in the protection of the great Agni, who provides excellent refuge, under the guidance of him who is easily invoked.
O Waters, you are indeed sources of bliss; grant us strength for great joy and for the sight [of the divine].
Whatever most auspicious essence you possess, grant us a share of it here,
like longing mothers.
Therefore, come quickly to us, O Waters, for whose dwelling you quicken; and give birth to us as well.
Mitra, having united the earth and the ground with light and heaven—
the well-born Jātavedas— I unite you for the health of all creatures.
Having fashioned the earth, the Rudras kindled the great light;
their unceasing, bright radiance shines among the gods.
May Sinīvālī, having softened with her two hands that clay which is mixed with the Vasus and Rudras and is fit for the ritual work, fashion it into a vessel.
Sinīvālī, with beautiful braided hair, with beautiful ornaments, and with beautiful head-dress—
may she, O Aditi, place the fire-pan into your two hands for me.
May Aditi fashion the fire-pan with her power, her two arms, and her wisdom;
may she bear Agni within her womb, as a mother carries her son upon her lap.
The head of Makha art thou; let the Vasus fashion thee with the Gāyatrī metre, after the manner of Aṅgiras. O fire-pan, thou art firm; thou art the earth;

bestow upon me offspring, abundance of wealth, lordship over cattle, heroic vigor, and kinsmen for this sacrificer. Let the Rudras fashion thee with the Triṣṭubh metre, after the manner of Aṅgiras. O fire-pan, thou art firm; thou art the intermediate space; bestow [upon me].

May the Ādityas fashion you for this sacrificer with the Jāgata metre, after the manner of Aṅgiras—granting him offspring, abundance of wealth, lordship over cattle, heroic strength, and kinsmen; O *ukhā*, you are firm, you are the sky; sustain in me offspring, abundance of wealth, lordship over cattle, heroic strength, and kinsmen for this sacrificer. May all the gods belonging to Vaiśvānara fashion you with the Ānuṣṭubha metre.

By the *chandas* of the Aṅgirases, O *ukhā*, you are firm; you are the quarters. Sustain for me offspring, abundance of wealth, lordship over cattle, heroic vigor, and kinsmen for this sacrificer. O Ādityas, you are the girdle; may Aditi seize your opening.
Having made the earth into a clay cauldron, a womb for Agni,
Aditi gave it to her sons, saying, "Let him cook [him] within it."
May the Vasus fumigate thee after the manner of Aṅgiras; may the Rudras fumigate thee after the manner of Aṅgiras; may the Ādityas fumigate thee after the manner of Aṅgiras;

may Indra fumigate thee after the manner of Aṅgiras; may Varuṇa fumigate thee after the manner of Aṅgiras; may Viṣṇu fumigate thee after the manner of Aṅgiras; may Bṛhaspati fumigate thee after the manner of Aṅgiras; may the goddess Aditi, accompanied by the Viśvedevas, fumigate thee after the manner of Aṅgiras.

In the dwelling-place of the earth, let him dig the pit like Aṅgiras. O Ukhā, may the divine wives of the gods, accompanied by all the gods, place thee in the dwelling-place of the earth like Aṅgiras. O Ukhā, may the divine Dhiṣaṇā, accompanied by all the gods, kindle thee in the dwelling-place of the earth like Aṅgiras.
O Ukhā, may the divine Gnas, accompanied by all the gods, [support] thee in the dwelling-place of the earth.
O Ukha, may they cook thee like Aṅgiras; may the goddess Varutrī, accompanied by all the gods, cook thee on the seat of the earth like Aṅgiras, O Ukha.
May the goddesses Janayas, whose wings are unbroken and who are accompanied by all the gods, cook thee on the seat of the earth like Aṅgiras, O Ukha.
The glory of the divine Mitra, the sustainer of the people, is winning;
his splendor possesses most wondrous renown.
May the god Savitṛ dig you up, he who has beautiful hands, beautiful fingers, and beautiful arms, and who possesses power.
Arise, O great one; stand upright, you who are steadfast. Without wavering, O Earth, fill the regions and the quarters.
O Mitra, I entrust this fire-pan to you; may it not break, for fear of being shattered.

May the Vasus anoint thee with the Gāyatrī metre, like Aṅgiras, O fire-pan! May the Rudras anoint thee with the Triṣṭubh metre, like Aṅgiras, O fire-pan! May the Ādityas anoint thee with the Jagatī metre, like Aṅgiras, O fire-pan! May all the gods belonging to all men anoint thee with the Anuṣṭubh metre, like Aṅgiras, O fire-pan!

To the intention, to Agni the impeller, Svāhā! To the mind, to wisdom, to Agni the impeller, Svāhā! To the thought, to the discerned, to Agni the impeller, Svāhā! To the restraint of speech, to Agni the impeller, Svāhā! To Prajāpati, to Manu, Svāhā! To Agni Vaiśvānara, Svāhā!
May every mortal choose the friendship of the divine Leader;
everyone strives for wealth, and may he choose glory so that he may prosper. Svāhā!
Do not fear, do not be harmed; be firm and show your valor!
O Mother, be bold and show your valor; you and Agni shall accomplish this task together.
Be firm, O Goddess Earth, for our well-being! You have been made by the self-power (*svadhā*) of the Asuras through their creative artifice (*māyā*).
May this oblation be pleasing to the gods; may you rise up unharmed in this sacrifice.
The ancient, excellent Hotṛ-priest, whose food is wood and whose libation is clarified butter,
is the wonderful son of strength.
From the higher distance, come down to the lower;
protect me wherever I may be.
From that furthest distance, O you with ruddy horses, come hither;
O Agni, friend of many, dwelling in the soil, do you overcome our adversaries.
O Agni, whatever pieces of wood we place upon you, may all that be ghee for you; accept it, O youngest one.
What the upajihvikā eats, what the ant crawls over—all that let it be ghee for you; enjoy that, O youngest one!
Bringing fuel night after night without ceasing, like fodder for a standing horse, may we rejoice in the increase of wealth and in nourishment; O Agni, may we, your neighbors, not come to harm.
Kindling Agni at the navel of the earth, we invoke him for the sake of great abundance of wealth—
the one who gladdens with food, the one praised with lofty hymns, the worshipful victor, Agni, the conqueror in battles.
Those armies that are rushing forward, those that pierce, and those that are fierce hordes—
as well as those who are thieves and those who are robbers— these I place within your mouth, O Agni.
Those who among men are defilers, thieves, and robbers in the forest,
those malicious ones in the thickets— I place them within your two jaws to devour.
O Agni, with your two fangs crush the night-pirates, and with your jaws the thief;
O Blessed One, with your two jaws devour those robbers once they have been cast into your mouth.
Whoever acts with hostility toward us, and whatever person hates us,
whoever reviles us and seeks to harm us— reduce them all to dust.
I have extended their arms, and I have increased their luster and strength;
by means of my sacred word (brahman), I destroy the enemies and I raise up my own people.
Sharpened is my sacred knowledge, sharpened is my heroism and strength;
sharpened is my sovereign power, victorious, for whomsoever I am the domestic priest.

The Brahman and the Kṣatra, joined together, do not waver; the Brahman indeed quickens the Kṣatra of the Kṣatriya, and the Kṣatra quickens the Brahman of the Brāhmaṇa, when they both perform heroic deeds in harmony.

Visible like a golden ornament, he shines far and wide; resplendent for glory, he has attained an invincible lifespan. Agni has become undecaying through his powers, since the prolific Heaven brought him forth.
Night and Dawn, of one mind yet different forms, moving together, suckle the single infant;
between heaven and earth the golden disk shines forth; the gods, bestowers of wealth, have sustained Agni.
The Seer puts on all forms; he has sent forth what is auspicious for bipeds and quadrupeds.
Savitar, the one to be chosen, has opened up the firmament; he shines following the departure of the Dawn.

You are Suparṇa, the Garuḍa; the Trivṛt is your head, the Gāyatra your eye, the Bṛhat and Rathantara your wings, the Stoma your body, the meters your limbs, the Yajus formulas your name, the Sāman Vāmadevya your torso, the Yajñāyajñīya your tail, and the Dhiṣṇya hearths your hooves.
You are Suparṇa, the Garuḍa; go to heaven, fly to the light!

Thou art the stride of Viṣṇu, the slayer of rivals; ascend the Gāyatrī metre; stride along the earth. Thou art the stride of Viṣṇu, the slayer of the malevolent; ascend the Triṣṭubh metre; stride along the intermediate space. Thou art the stride of Viṣṇu, the slayer of the hostile;
ascend the Jagatī metre; stride along the sky. Thou art the stride of Viṣṇu, the slayer of those who act as enemies; [ascend] the Anuṣṭubh metre.
O Chandā, ascend; stride along the quarters.
Agni has cried out like the thundering sky; licking the earth, he anoints the plants.
As soon as he is born, he has spread abroad when kindled; he shines with his splendor between the two worlds, heaven and earth.
O Agni, you who turn toward us; O Agni Aṅgiras, come back again with vigor and with wealth.
I have brought you here; you have entered within. Stand firm, unshakable. May all the people desire you; uphold the kingdoms for us.
O Varuṇa, loosen the highest bond from us.
In the forefront of the dawns, the great one has stood up erect; emerging from the darkness, he has come with light.
Agni, with his radiant luster and beautiful limbs, having been born, has filled all dwellings.
The swan dwelling in the pure realm.
Sit down upon the lap of this mother, O Agni, you who know all ways;
do not scorch her with your flame nor with your heat, but shine within her with pure light.
O Agni, with your brilliance within the fire-pan in your own seat,
heating it with your flame, O Jātavedas, be auspicious to it.
Having become auspicious for me, O Agni, sit down as one who is auspicious;
having made all the quarters auspicious, settle here in your own womb.
Agni was first born from the sky; the Jātavedas was born from us a second time;
a third time, he of manly mind, the eternal one, was born in the waters. Kindling him, the pious man brings him to life.
We know your three forms, O Agni, in three ways; we know your dwelling distributed in many places.
We know your supreme name which is hidden in secret; we know that source from which you have come forth.

The manly-minded one kindled you within the waters, in the ocean; the beholder of men kindled you in the udder of heaven. When you were established in the third realm, in the womb of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*), the mighty ones seized you.
Magnificent source of glories, supporter of riches, inspirer of inspired thoughts, guardian of Soma— the Vasu,
the Son of Strength, the King, kindled at the forefront of the dawns, shines resplendent within the waters.
Desirable, purifying, a ministering priest, and wise, the immortal Agni has been established among mortals.
Red-hued, bearing his smoke aloft, he rises up, striving to reach the sky with his bright radiance.
Agni cried out.
He was born as the king of the entire world; being born, he filled the two worlds, heaven and earth.
He split even the firm mountain as he went forth, when the five peoples sacrificed to Agni.
Night and Dawn.
O Agni, of auspicious luster, whoever today prepares for you a cake rich in ghee,
O God— lead him further toward greater wealth, toward the glory ordained by the gods, O most youthful one.
O Agni, grant him a share in glorious deeds; at every hymn being recited, grant him a portion.
May he be dear to Sūrya, dear to Agni; may he prevail with what has been born and with those yet to be born.
O Agni, day after day, the sacrificers, making you their messenger, have worshipped you with oblations;
seeking wealth through you, the desiring ones have opened the stall rich in cattle.
Agni Vaiśvānara, the most gracious guardian of Soma, has been praised by the seers among men.
I invoke the non-hostile Heaven and Earth; O gods, bestow upon us wealth accompanied by heroic sons.
May all the gods lift you up, O Agni, with their thoughts.
Be gracious to us—you who are fair of face and rich in light.
O Agni, come forward as the luminous one with your auspicious flames;
shining with great beams of light, do not harm the offspring with your body.
Agni cried out.
Honor Agni with fuel; awaken the guest with clarified butter;
pour the oblations into him.
Agni has spread far and wide; he is heard of as the Bharata's, shining with great light like the sun.
He who has stood firm against the Pūru in battles, the divine guest, has shone for us auspiciously.
O divine Waters, receive this ash; place it in a pleasant and fragrant place. Let the women of one nest bow down before it; bear it well as a mother bears her son.
O Agni, your seat is in the waters; you follow after the plants;
as their embryo, you are born again.
You are the embryo of the herbs, the embryo of the trees;
you are the embryo of every living being, O Agni, you are the embryo of the waters.
O Agni, having propitiated the womb with ashes, the waters, and the earth,
and having united with your mothers, you have returned, radiant once more.
Having returned again to your seat, O Agni, you lie upon the waters and the earth,
most auspicious within her, as if in the lap of a mother.
Again with vigor, together with wealth.
O youngest one, self-sustaining lord, take note of this my speech, most bountiful and offered to you.
One man censures it, while another has praised it; I, being a singer of praise, praise your body, O Agni.
May that wise sage, Maghavan, the giver of wealth and lord of riches,
drive away from us all hostilities whatsoever we have committed.
Depart, go away, and creep far from here—ye who are here, both those who were of old and those who are recent.
Yama has granted this resting-place on earth; the Fathers have prepared this world for him.
You are the ash of Agni; you are the soil of Agni; you are recognition; you are the fulfillment of desires; may the fulfillment of desires be mine through you.
This is that Agni in whom Indra, longing for it, placed the pressed Soma within his belly;
having won thousandfold booty like a swift horse, O Jātavedas, you are praised.
O Agni, you go toward the flood of heaven; you have spoken to the gods who are worthy of worship.
Toward those waters which are the luminous realms beyond the sun, and those which stand below, you hasten.

O Agni, that splendor of yours which is in heaven, on earth, in the mountains, in the plants, and in the waters— that brilliant, surging light with which you have overspread the wide mid-air, O you who watch over men!
May the fires that dwell in the soil, being of one accord on the downward slope,
enjoy the offered oblation and grant great, disease-free refreshments.
O Agni, bestow upon the one who invokes you the *iḍā*—the gift of cattle that is most abundant and enduring.
May there be to us a son, a progeny that continues the lineage; O Agni, may that benevolence of yours abide with us.
This is yours.

You are the conscious one; by that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras. You are the surrounding conscious one; by that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras. You are the piled ones, you are the surrounding-piled ones; rise up and take your place.
May you two agree together, being well-disposed toward one another, radiant and of good mind; dwelling together for the sake of food and strength.
I have brought together your minds, your vows, and your thoughts.
O Agni Purīṣya, be our protector; bestow food and vigor upon the sacrificer.
O Agni, you who dwell in the soil, you are possessed of wealth and abundance; having made all directions auspicious, sit here upon your own birthplace.
May you two be our protectors.
As a mother carries her son, so has the Earth carried Agni Purīṣya into his own womb, the fire-pan;
may Prajāpati Viśvakarman, in harmony with all the gods and the seasons, release him from it.
Seek out him who does not breathe [the sacrifice], him who does not offer sacrifice; follow the path of the thief, of the robber!
Seek someone other than us—this is your path. O Goddess Nirṛti, let there be homage to you!
Homage be to you, O Nirṛti of piercing splendor! Untie this iron bond.
In agreement with Yama and Yamī, cause him to ascend to the highest firmament.
That which belongs to you today.

The noose which the goddess Nirṛti bound upon your necks, so that it could not be loosened—that I untie for you in the midst of your life; thus, being released, live on as a living man and eat your food.
That wonderful light which was born beyond this great expanse of space—
O Agni Vaiśvānara, may that carry us across our enemies.
Svāhā! Homage to Bhūti!
The abode and gatherer of riches, he beholds all forms with his powers;
like the god Savitṛ whose laws are true, he stands like Indra at the meeting-place of the paths.
By which the gods ascended upward to the light, by which the Ādityas, the Vasus, and the Rudras [went],
by which the Aṅgirases attained greatness— by that may the sacrificers go in well-being.
May Pūṣan yoke you; may Savitṛ yoke you; may Bṛhaspati yoke you, with the splendor of Agni and the radiance of Sūrya.
The seers yoke the plows; the wise, seeking favor among the gods, stretch out the yokes separately.
Yoke the ploughs, stretch out the yokes; sow the seed here in the prepared womb. May our song and our prompt obedience be fruitful together; let the sickle come closer to the ripened grain.
May the plough, sharp-pointed, well-fashioned, with a handle for grasping Soma, dig up the cow and the sheep; may it turn up the fertile soil that yields a wagon-load and the fat earth.
May the well-plowed furrows till the earth auspiciously; may the plowman approach auspiciously with his draft-animals.
O Śuna and Sīra, being gratified by our oblation, make the plants bear fine fruit for us.
Śunāsīrā:
O heroes, may Śuna with the plough and the oxen, Bhaga with the shares, and Marut, the lord of the plough, inspire us;
may Parjanya, setting the seed in motion, prosper us; O Śunāsīrā, provide us with grain.
O Śuna and Sīra, plow well and produce abundant grain;
this earth is fertile according to the seasons; let the plows strike it deep.
Let Sītā be anointed with ghee and honey, authorized by all the gods and the Maruts;
swelling with a honeyed portion of strength, O Sītā, turn toward us with milk.
I yoke the yojana, the antaryāma, the pole, the yoke-pin,
the strength, the goad, the whip, the two covers, and both female frogs.
The winner of cattle, the winner of horses, the winner of gold, surrounded by pleasant speech, Savitṛ has risen; with his single-wheeled chariot, he goes filling the portion of vigor upon the earth.
O Indra, for the sake of this hand-stirring, this vigorous stirring, this stirring from the loins, this productive stirring, this shared enjoyment, this strength, and this drinking, I draw it forth.
Of the two camels, of the two *pīlu* trees, and also of the two binding-ropes—
we know the names of you all, O draft-animals, who are skilled at drinking the sweet juice.
Be released, O inviolable ones, you who go to the gods; you have crossed to the further shore of this darkness.
We have attained the light.
Those herbs which were born first for the gods in the three ages of old—
I now take heed of their hundred and seven abodes, O tawny ones.
A hundred, O mothers, are your abodes, and a thousand are your growths;
therefore, O you of a hundred powers, make this man of mine free from disease.
The plants—those that flower, those that bear fruit, those that are fruitful, and those that are fruitless—are like victorious mares; they are the ones who carry us across.
"O Plants, you mothers— thus I address you, O goddesses—
who strike down afflictions and drive away all disease."
In the *aśvattha* tree is your dwelling; in the *parṇa* leaf is your abode made.
You shall indeed be sharers of cattle when you win back the man.
He who knows how the plants assemble like kings gathered in council— he is called a sage, a seer, a slayer of demons, and a driver away of disease.
Niṣkṛti is your mother, and you are Saṃkṛti;
you are winged streams, for whatever is diseased, you heal it.
I have yoked all the plants— those rich in horses, rich in soma, strengthening, and full of vigor— for his safety and well-being.
When I, seeking strength, take these herbs in my hand,
the self of the wasting disease perishes, as if before one who seizes the living.
The vital breaths of the plants rush forth like cows from the stall, seeking to win wealth for themselves and for you, O man.
They have stepped over all obstacles, as a thief crosses into a pen.
The plants have cast away whatever blemish there was upon the body.
Those [powers] of yours that have entered your self, those that have settled in every joint— may they drive away your consumption, like a fierce man who sits in the midst.
Fly away, O consumption, together with the blue jay and the kingfisher;
vanish together with the blast of the wind and together with the whirlwind.
Let one of you protect another; let each of you assist the other.
All you plants, being in full accord, protect my speech.
Those plants that bear fruit and those that are fruitless, those that are unenclosed and those that are enclosed—
impelled by Bṛhaspati, may they release us from distress.
As they descended from heaven, the plants spoke:
"The living man whom we shall reach, that person shall not come to harm."
We invoke heaven, the stars, the earth, the yakṣas, and the mountains;
the oceans, the rivers, and the ponds—may they deliver us from distress.
We invoke King Varuṇa, Dhātṛ, and Pūṣan;
we invoke Tvaṣṭṛ as the foremost; may they release us from distress.
May he who is the progenitor of the earth not harm us— he, whose laws are true, who has pervaded the heavens,
and who first brought forth the shining waters. To what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
Turn toward us, O Earth, with sacrifice and with milk;
Agni, impelled, has ascended your omentum.
O Agni, that which is bright, that which is radiant, that which is purified, and that which is worthy of sacrifice—
that we bring for the gods.
May I take nourishment and vigor from here, the stream of clarified butter, the womb of the buffalo;
may it enter into our cattle and plants. I cast away exhaustion, lack of food, and disease.
O cow who milks all desires, grant us our wish for the sake of progeny and plants,
and for Indra, Agni, Pūṣan, Mitra, and Varuṇa.
O Agni, yours is fame and vital power; great and radiant are your flames, O Lord of Light.
With your lofty splendor and might, O Sage, you bestow praiseworthy strength upon the donor.
With purifying luster, with bright luster, with undiminished luster, you rise up with your radiance.
Moving between your two mothers as their son, you protect them; you fill both worlds, heaven and earth.
O Agni, ruling over all, spread yourself out among living beings; bestow wealth upon us, O Immortal One! You shine forth with a form worthy of being beheld; you grant us winning riches.
O Son of Strength, Jātavedas, rejoice with our excellent praises and our prayers, being well-disposed toward us.
They have established you here—you who possess manifold forms, wondrous aids, and noble births.
Men have placed before them for their welfare Agni, the observer of the cosmic order (*ṛtāvān*), the mighty one visible to all; you,
the divine one with ears that hear, most far-reaching, men join with their song as a companion.
To the wise ordainer of the sacrifice, who rules over great bounty—
you bestow a fortunate gift of beauty, great nourishment, and winning wisdom.
Swell up, O Soma; let virile strength gather from every side unto you; be present at the gathering of the prize.
May your milks come together, and let your strengths and manly powers that overcome the assailants unite.
Swelling for the sake of immortality, O Soma, place the highest glories in heaven.
Brahman, first born in the east, Vena revealed from the radiant horizon; he disclosed its highest stations in the depths, and the womb of both the existent and the non-existent.
In the beginning, Hiraṇyagarbha came into being; once born, he was the sole lord of all that exists. He supported this earth and yonder sky. To which god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
Gathered from the waters and from the essence of the earth, he came into being from Viśvakarman;
Tvaṣṭṛ, fashioning his form, entered him—that divine birthplace of the Puruṣa in the beginning.
The drop has fallen.
Homage be to the serpents, whichever ones are upon the earth;
to those in the intermediate space and those in heaven— to those serpents, homage!
Homage to those serpents who are the arrows of sorcerers, those who dwell among the trees, and those who lie in holes.
Homage to those serpents who are in the bright realm of heaven, or those who are in the rays of the sun, and those who have made their dwellings in the waters.
Assume your form like a wide-spreading net; go forth like a king with his retinue and his elephant.
Rushing along your swift net, you are an archer; pierce the demons with your most scorching weapons.
Your swift-flying flames fall; touching them with boldness, blaze forth!
O Agni, with your heats and your tongue, release the winged sparks like winged birds on all sides, unrestrained.
Cast forth thy spies; be thou the swiftest, an undeceivable guardian of this people.
Whether he who plots evil against us be far away or near, O Agni, let no affliction from him prevail over thee.
Arise, O Agni! Spread yourself out; burn down the enemy, O you of the sharp weapon!
O kindled one, whoever has directed hostility toward us, him you shall consume downward like dry brushwood.
Stand upright and pierce through [the darkness] toward us; O Agni, make manifest the divine powers.
Slacken the firm [bonds] of those impelled by demons; crush the enemies, both kin and stranger.
This Agni is the lord of thousandfold and hundredfold strength; he is the sage, the head of riches.
With the brilliance of Agni, I settle you; by that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.

Leader of the sacrifice and of the mid-world, where you accompany with your auspicious teams of horses, you place your head in heaven as the winner of light; O Agni, you have made your tongue the bearer of the oblation.

I set thee down with the vigor of Indra; by that deity, sit thou firm like Aṅgiras. Thou art firm, a supporting foundation, spread out and well-sustained by Viśvakarman. Let not the ocean overwhelm thee, nor the Suparṇa; being unshakable, make the earth firm.
Thou art splendor; grant me splendor. Grant the earth; make the earth firm; do not harm the earth. [From] the earth...

Protect me! You are light; grant me light. Support the intermediate space; make firm the intermediate space; do not harm the intermediate space; protect me from the intermediate space. You are heaven; grant me heaven. Support the sky; make firm the sky; do not harm the sky; protect me from the sky.

O Agni, those moist wombs of thine, those that are nest-like, those drops of thine, O Agni, and those navels— with all these, both kinds, being in harmony and knowing [the way], sit down here for thy own body.
Growing from joint to joint, from knot to knot,
even so, O Dūrvā grass, spread for us with a thousandfold and a hundredfold increase.
O divine brick, you who spread yourself out with a hundred and grow forth with a thousand— to you we shall pay worship with an oblation.
O Agni, those splendors of yours which extend across the sky through the sun with their rays—
with all of those, grant us radiance today for the sake of our people.
O Gods, whatever splendors you possess in the sun, and whatever splendors are in the cows and in the horses—
with all those splendors, O Bṛhaspati, Indra, and Agni, bestow radiance upon us.
The Virāj has sustained the light; the Svarāj has sustained the light; the Samrāj has sustained the light. Thou art Bhūḥ, the seed of the world;
thou art a brick, the heavenly world. With my mind I ascend thee. Agni is the light, the light is Agni. By that deity, in the manner of Aṅgiras, sit thou firm.
Thou art Sūḥ, the seed of the world; thou art a brick, the heavenly world. With my speech I ascend thee. Sūrya is the light.

The light is the sun; with that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras. May Bṛhaspati settle you upon the back of the earth, full of light, for the sake of all out-breathing, in-breathing, diffused breathing, and up-breathing, for stability, and for movement.
Bestow universal light! Agni is your overlord; with that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras. May Viśvakarman settle you.

Upon the back of the atmosphere, luminous, for all out-breathing, in-breathing, diffused breathing, and upward breathing, for stability and for movement, bestow universal light! Vāyu is your overlord; by that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras!
May Parameṣṭhin settle you upon the back of heaven, luminous, for all out-breathing, in-breathing, diffused breathing, and upward breathing.
For stability and for conduct, bestow all light, O Sūrya; you have the Sun as your overlord. With that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.
You are Āṣāḍhā, the overcoming; overcome the enemy, overcome those who attack us. You possess a thousandfold power; as such, quicken me.
The winds blow honey for the one who follows the cosmic order; the rivers flow with honey;
may the plants be sweet for us.
May the night be honey-sweet, and may the dawn be honey-sweet; may the earthly realm be honey-sweet, and may our father, heaven, be honey-sweet.
May the tree be full of sweetness for us; may the sun be full of sweetness;
may the cows be sweet for us.

I set thee down in the depth of the waters, in the swelling of the ocean, in the shadow of the well; homage to the ocean, homage to the eye of the ocean! May the rain from heaven attend thee; let not the sun scorch thee, nor Agni Vaiśvānara; with unbroken wings, look upon thy offspring.
He has traversed the three oceans; Svarga, the lord of the waters, the bull among bricks—go there where the ancestors have departed, clothing yourself in the soil, to the world of the well-done.
May Heaven and Earth, the broad and the vast, sprinkle this sacrifice for us; may they fill us with nourishments.
This is Viṣṇu.
Now, O Lord of the Forest, let the wind blow upon your very tip;
and now, O mortar, press out the Soma for Indra to drink.
Night and Dawn.
Sewn by the gods with immortality, the fire-pan has come; as a sister, it has mounted upon the altar.
In agreement with the ancient seers, may Agni, the all-knowing, perform that here according to truth.
O Earth, sit upon the earth; as a mother, sit upon the mother.
Thou art pleasant, thou art a good seat; sit upon the pleasant one, sit upon the good seat.
Varuṇa, firm in his vows and wise in action, sat down upon his dwellings for the sake of universal sovereignty.
We seek the sacrifice of the gods, their majesty— Agni, the wondrous one, in his common dwelling-place and in his seats.
With the sacred word (*brahman*), I establish Vaiśvānara, who is all-pervading, in the abode of the hymn of praise, as the source of the soil.

The sages, bestowers of vitality, have established Agni Vaiśvānara—the all-pervading one, who is firmly seated in his place within the sacrificial seat—in the measure [of the rite] by means of the sacred word; he is the one deposited in the womb of the earth as the very foundation of the hymn of praise.
They kindle with fuel the well-wishing Agni as he is being kindled in his common dwelling-place and in his seats;
Vaiśvānara, the all-pervading, who has been brought forth as the purifying one, the very essence of the hymn, by means of the sacred word.
O Agni, yoke those horses of yours, O God, which are well-trained and swift; they carry you readily.
Yoke, O Agni, the horse most beloved by the gods, like a charioteer; sit down as the ancient Hotṛ-priest.
Together they flow like rivers, our milk-offerings, purified within by the heart and the mind;
I behold the streams of clarified butter, and in the midst of the fire stands the golden reed.

For the *ṛc* thee, for brilliance thee, for luster thee, for light thee! This has become the vigor of the entire world, of Agni Vaiśvānara. May Agni be radiant with radiance; may the golden disk be brilliant with splendor.
Thou art the giver of a thousand; I take thee for a thousand.
Anoint the solar embryo with milk, the image of a thousand, possessing all forms. Encompass it with your heat; do not scorch it. Being piled up, grant him a life of a hundred years.
The impulse of the wind, the navel of Varuṇa, the horse born in the midst of the waters,
the infant of the rivers, the tawny one whose foundation is the mountain— O Agni, do not harm him in the highest heaven.
I praise with prostrations Agni— the eternal, ruddy, and restless one, who is perceived first— may he,
being fashioned according to his joints and seasons, not harm the cow, Aditi, the radiant one.
O Agni, do not harm Tvaṣṭṛ’s Varutrī, the navel of Varuṇa, the ewe born from beyond the mid-region, the great, thousandfold creative power of the Asura, in the highest heaven.
The fire that was born from the heat of Agni, from the fervor of the earth or from the sky—
he who as Viśvakarman begot these creatures— may thy wrath, O Agni, spare him.

Do not harm this two-footed animal, O thousand-eyed one, as you are being piled for the sake of the sacrifice. I assign to you the wild *mayu*; building up your body with that, settle down. Let your heat reach the *mayu*; let your heat reach him whom we hate. Do not harm this one-hoofed animal, the neighing, vigorous steed among the prize-winners; I assign to you the wild *gaura*.
Seeking [this] for yourself, settle down; let your heat reach the wild ox, let your heat reach him whom we hate.
This thousandfold, hundred-streamed fountain, expanding in the midst of the waters, milking out clarified butter for mankind—O Agni, do not harm Aditi in the highest heaven.
I assign to you the wild gavaya; fashioning your body with it, sit down. Let your heat reach the gavaya;

let your heat reach him whom we hate. This woolly one, the navel of Varuṇa, the skin of animals, biped and quadruped—the first birthplace of Tvaṣṭṛ among the gods—O Agni, do not harm it in the highest heaven.
I assign to thee the wild ram; fashioning thy body with him, sit down. Let thy heat reach the ram; let thy heat reach him whom we hate.
For from the heat of Agni the goat was born; in the beginning he beheld his progenitor. Through him the gods attained divinity first;
through him those worthy of sacrifice ascended to the height. I assign to thee the wild śarabha.
Gathering [the fire] for yourself, sit down; let your heat reach the śarabha, let your heat reach him whom we hate.
I settle you in the movement of the waters; I settle you in the rising of the waters; I settle you in the path of the waters; I settle you in the light of the waters;
I settle you in the ashes of the waters; I settle you in the ocean as your seat; I settle you in the flood as your seat;
I settle you in the liquid as your seat; I settle you in the dwelling of the waters; I settle you in the companionships of the waters.
I settle you in the seat of the waters; I settle you in the gathering-place of the waters; I settle you in the womb of the waters; I settle you in the soil of the waters;
I settle you in the domain of the waters. With the Gāyatrī metre I settle you;
with the Triṣṭubh metre I settle you; with the Jagatī metre I settle you; with the Anuṣṭubh metre I settle you.
I settle you with the Pāṅkta metre.

This earth is his breath; from the earth comes the wind, from the wind springtime, from springtime the Gāyatrī, from the Gāyatrī the Gāyatra [chant], from the Gāyatra the Upāṃśu [cup], from the Upāṃśu the Trivṛt [stoma], from the Trivṛt the Rathantara [sāman]; Vasiṣṭha is its seer. With thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take hold of the breath for the sake of offspring. This southern [quarter] is Viśvakarman; his mind belongs to Viśvakarman.

Summer is the *mānasa*, the *triṣṭubh* is the summer [season], from the *triṣṭubh* comes the *svāra* [sāman], from the *svāra* comes the *antaryāma* cup, from the *antaryāma* comes the *pañcadaśa* [stoma], from the *pañcadaśa* comes the *bṛhat* [sāman]. Bharadvāja is the seer. With thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take hold of the mind for the sake of offspring. This one behind is Viśvavyacas; his is the Vaiśvavyacasa eye, the rainy seasons are the visual [spheres], the *jagatī* is the rainy [season], from the *jagatī*...

From the *ṛk-sama* [comes] the *ṛk-sama*, from the *śukra* the *śukra*, from the seventeenfold [stoma] the seventeenfold, from the seventeenfold the *vairūpa*; Jamadagni the seer [received it]. With thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take the eye for offspring. From this northern [direction], the *sva* [belongs to] him; from the *sauva* [comes] the ear, from the *śarat* the *śrautra*, from the *anuṣṭubh* the *śārada*, from the *anuṣṭubh* the *aiḍa*, from the *aiḍa* the *manthin*, from the *manthin* the twenty-onefold [stoma], from the twenty-onefold the *vairāja*.
Viśvāmitra is the seer. With thee, taken by Prajāpati, I take the ear for offspring. This is the higher thought; its speech is mātyā;
the winter season is to be expressed by speech. The *paṅkti* meter belongs to winter; from the *paṅkti* comes that which has a *nidhana*; from that which has a *nidhana* comes the *āgrayaṇa* cup;
from the *āgrayaṇa* come the *triṇava* and *trayastrimśa* stomas; from the *triṇava* and *trayastrimśa* come the *śākvara* and *raivata* sāmans; [the seer is] Viśvakarman.
O Seer, with you who are taken by Prajāpati, I take up speech for the sake of progeny.

The eastern direction, the spring season, Agni as the deity, the Brahman as wealth, the Gāyatrī metre, the Rathantara Sāman, the Trivṛt Stoma—which indeed follows the path of the Pañcadaśa—Sānaga as the seer, the three-year-old calf as the age, the Kṛta age among the ages, the east wind as the wind, the fathers and grandfathers, those who are further and those who are nearer: may they protect us; may they guard us in this sacred formulation (brahman), in this [earth].
In this office of domestic priest, in this ritual act, in this benediction, and in this invocation of the gods.
The southern direction, the summer season, Indra as the deity, the ruling power (*kṣatra*) as wealth, the *triṣṭubh* metre, the *bṛhat* chant, the fifteenfold hymn-form (*pañcadaśa-stoma*),
which follows the path of the seventeenfold hymn-form, the eternal seer, the three-year-old horse,

the south wind, the winds, the fathers, and the grandfathers— those who are further and those who are nearer— may they protect us; may they guard us in this sacred formulation (*brahman*), in this [earth].
In this office of domestic priest, in this rite, in this blessing, and in this invocation of the gods.
The western direction; the rainy season; the Viśvedevas as the deity; the people as the wealth; the Jagatī metre; the Vairūpa Sāman; the seventeenfold Stoma;
that same one with twenty-one turnings; the days as the source; the Trivatsa bull as the seer;

the bird; the Dvāpara age; the wind from behind; the winds; the fathers and grandfathers—those who are further and those who are nearer—may they protect us, may they guard us in this sacred formulation (brahman).
In this office, in this ritual act, in this prayer for blessing, and in this invocation of the gods.

The northern direction, the autumn season, Mitra and Varuṇa as the deities, nourishment as wealth, the Anuṣṭubh metre, the Vairāja Sāman, the twenty-one-fold Stoma—which indeed follows the path of the twenty-seven-fold—Purāṇa as the seer, Turyavāṭ as the age, the overcomer of enemies, the wind blowing from the north, the fathers, the grandfathers, those who are further and those who are nearer: may they protect us; may they guard us in this sacred formulation (brahman).
In this office, in this ritual act, in this prayer for blessing, and in this invocation of the gods.
The upward direction; the winter and cool seasons; Bṛhaspati as the deity; wealth as the fruit; the *paṅkti* metre; the *śākvara* and *raivata* *sāmans*; the twenty-sevenfold hymn-form;
that which has the thirty-threefold hymn-form as its path; Suparṇa as the seer; the five-year-old ox as the age;
the leaping one among those who do not leap; the wind blowing above; the wind; the fathers and grandfathers, those further and those nearer—may they protect us, may they preserve us.
In this sacred formulation, in this office of the priest, in this ritual act, in this benediction, and in this invocation of the gods.
Fill the world, fill the gap; then sit down, you who are firm.
Indra, Agni, and Bṛhaspati have seated you in this womb.
These dappled cows, yielding milk for the preparation, mix the Soma;
they are the clans at the birth of the gods, in the three luminous realms of heaven.
Of firm abode, of firm origin, you are firm; sit upon the firm womb, O Sādhya!
Enjoying the first signal of the fire-pan, may the Aśvins, acting as Adhvaryus, settle you here.
Nest-like, rich in clarity, and all-sustaining, sit upon the pleasant seat of the earth.
May the Rudras and Vasus sing your praise; fulfill this sacred prayer for our well-being.
Let the Aśvins, the Adhvaryu priests, settle you here.
Sit here on your own skillful [seat], O son of Dakṣa, for the great joy and delight of the gods.
Be like a father to his son, you who are most gracious; settle yourself with a body that provides easy access.
Let the Aśvins, the two Adhvaryu priests, establish you here.
The earth's excrement art thou; thy name is Water. May all the gods acclaim thee.
Seated here upon the back of the *stoma*, rich in ghee, bestow upon us wealth accompanied by progeny.
May the Aśvins, the two Adhvaryu priests, settle you here.
I set thee on the back of Aditi, the upholder of the intermediate space, the support of the quarters, the sovereign lady of the world; thou art the wave, the drop of the waters.
May the two Aśvins, the Adhvaryu priests, settle thee here.

In harmony with the seasons, in harmony with the ritual distributions, in harmony with the gods, in harmony with the gods who perceive the sacred ordinances—may the two Aśvins, the Adhvaryu priests, settle you here for Agni Vaiśvānara. In harmony with the seasons, in harmony with the ritual distributions, in harmony with the Vasus;

in harmony with the seasons, in harmony with the ritual distributions, in harmony with the Rudras; in harmony with the seasons, in harmony with the ritual distributions, in harmony with the Ādityas—in harmony with the seasons [I settle you].

In harmony with the [three] forms, in harmony with all the Vaiśvānara gods, in harmony with the gods who possess wisdom—may the two Aśvins, the Adhvaryu priests, settle you here for Agni Vaiśvānara. MS_2,8.1 //
Protect my out-breath; protect my in-breath; protect my diffused breath. Shine forth widely for my sight; make my hearing resonant.

Swell the waters; quicken the plants. Protect the two-footed; protect the four-footed. Send down rain from heaven. Kṣatra is the vigor; Chandas is the support; Vayas is the overlord. Mūrdhan is the vigor; Prajāpati is the Chandas. Viśvakarman [is the Chandas].

Vaya is the *parameṣṭhin*; the *tryavi* is the *triṣṭubh* metre; vaya is the *dityavāṭ*; the *virāj* is the metre; vaya is the *pañcāvi*; the *gāyatrī* is the metre; vaya is the *trivatsa*; the *uṣṇih* is the metre; vaya is the *turyavāṭ*; the *anuṣṭubh* is the metre;
vaya is the *paṣṭhavāṭ*; the *bṛhatī* is the metre; vaya is the bull (*ukṣan*); the *kakubh* is the metre; vaya is the steer (*ṛṣabha*); the *sato-bṛhatī* is the metre.

The *chandas* is the ox, the age is the *paṅkti*; the *chandas* is the cow, the age is the *jagatī*; the *chandas* is the ram, the age is the youth; the *chandas* is the bull, the age is the *viśāla*; the *chandas* is the man, the age is the *tandra*; the *chandas* is the lion, the age is the *chadis*; the *chandas* is the tiger, the age is the unassailable.
O Indra and Agni, do you two firmly establish this unshaking brick;
with its back, may it fill heaven and earth and pervade the intermediate space.

Thou art the Queen, the eastern quarter; thou art the Virāj, the southern quarter; thou art the Samrāj, the western quarter; thou art the Svarāj, the northern quarter; thou art the Sovereign Lady, the upward quarter. Protect my life-span; protect my out-breath;
protect my in-breath; protect my diffused breath; protect my sight; protect my hearing; swell my mind; quicken my speech; protect my self; [grant] light.

Grant me the *me-chandas* meter, the *pramā-chandas* meter, the *pratimā-chandas* meter, the *asrīvīś-chandas* meter, the *paṅkti-chandas* meter, the *uṣṇihā-chandas* meter, the *gāyatrī-chandas* meter, the *triṣṭubh-chandas* meter, the *jagatī-chandas* meter, the *anuṣṭubh-chandas* meter, the *virāṭ-chandas* meter, the *bṛhatī-chandas* meter,
the *pṛthivī-chandas* meter, the *antarikṣa-chandas* meter, the *dyauś-chandas* meter, the *nakṣatra-chandas* meter, and the *samā-chandas* meter.
Agriculture is a meter; speech is a meter; mind is a meter; a cow is a meter; a horse is a meter; a goat is a meter; gold is a meter. Agni is a deity; Vāta is a deity; Sūrya is a deity;

Candramas is a deity; the Vasus are deities; the Rudras are deities; the Ādityas are deities; the Maruts are deities; Indra is a deity; Varuṇa is a deity; Bṛhaspati is a deity; the Viśve [Devas] are deities.

The gods are your divinity; you are the head, the sovereign. You are firm, the supporter, the sustainer, the earth. For long life I take you, for splendor I take you, for agriculture I take you, for security I take you. You are the controller, the sovereign; you are the controller, the restrainer, the sustainer, the upholder.
For food I take you, for strength I take you, for wealth I take you, for prosperity I take you.

Indra: O drop (*indo*), you are firm (*dhruva*). The swift one is the *trivṛt*; the radiant one is the *pañcadaśa*; the sky is the *saptadaśa*; the onset is the *aṣṭādaśa*; and the heat is the *navadaśa*.
The Bhīvarta is the twentyfold; the Dharuṇa is the twenty-onefold; the Varcas is the twenty-twofold; the Saṃbharaṇa is the twenty-threefold;
the Yoni is the twenty-fourfold; the Garbhas are the twenty-fivefold; the Ojas is the twenty-sevenfold; the Virāj is the thirtyfold; the Kratu is the thirty-onefold;
the Vidhṛti is the thirty-two-fold; the Pratiṣṭhā is the thirty-threefold; the summit of the ruddy sun is the thirty-fourfold; the Nāka is the thirty-sixfold.
The Vīvarta is the forty-eighth; the Dhartra is the Catuṣṭoma.

You are the portion of Agni; the overlordship of Dīkṣā; the Brahman is protected; the Trivṛt Stoma. You are the portion of Indra; the overlordship of Viṣṇu; the Kṣatra is protected; the Pañcadaśa Stoma. You are the portion of the Nṛcakṣases; the overlordship of Dhātṛ;
the progeny is protected; the Saptadaśa Stoma. You are the portion of Mitra; the overlordship of Varuṇa; the rain from heaven.

The wind is won; the twenty-onefold hymn-form is won; thou art the portion of Aditi, with Pūṣan as thy overlordship; power is won; the twenty-sevenfold hymn-form is won; thou art the portion of the Vasus, with the Rudras as thy overlordship; the four-footed is won; the twenty-fourfold hymn-form is won;
thou art the portion of the Ādityas, with the Maruts as thy overlordship; embryos are won; the twenty-fivefold hymn-form is won; thou art the portion of Savitṛ, with Bṛhaspati as thy overlordship.

The quarters are the overlordship; the directions are won; the Catuṣṭoma is the hymn-form; thou art the portion of the Yavas; the Ayavas have overlordship; creatures are won; the Catuścatvāriṃśa is the hymn-form; thou art the portion of the Ṛbhus; the Viśvedevas have overlordship;
what has been and what has been pacified is won; the Trayastriṃśa is the hymn-form.

With one [verse] they praised; creatures were produced; Prajāpati was the overlord. With three [verses] they praised; the Brahman was created; Brahmaṇaspati was the overlord. With five [verses] they praised; beings were created; Bhūtānām pati was the overlord.
With seven [verses] they praised; the seven Ṛṣis were created; Dhātṛ was the overlord. With nine [verses]...
They praised with eight; the Fathers were created; Aditi was the overlord. They praised with eleven; the seasons were created;
the seasons were the overlords. They praised with thirteen; the months were created; the year was the overlord.
They praised with fifteen; the kṣatra was created; Indra was the overlord. They praised with seventeen.

Domestic animals were created; Bṛhaspati was the overlord. They praised with nineteen [verses]; the Śūdra and the Ārya were created; Day and Night were the two overlords. They praised with twenty-one [verses]; the one-hoofed [animals] were created; Varuṇa was the overlord. They praised with twenty-three [verses]; small animals were created; Pūṣan was the overlord. They praised with twenty-five [verses]; wild [animals] were created.

Cattle were created; Vāyu was the overlord. They praised with twenty-seven [verses]; the trees were created; Soma was the overlord. They praised with twenty-nine [verses]; heaven and earth went apart; the Vasus and Rudras followed after them, and they indeed were the overlords.
They praised with thirty-one [verses]; creatures were created—the Yavas and Ayavas were the overlords.
They were thirty-three; they praised with hymns; the beings became tranquil; Prajāpati Parameṣṭhin was the overlord.
O Agni, drive away our born enemies; O Jātavedas, repel those yet unborn.
Speak for us with a gracious mind, without anger; may we abide in your triple-layered protection within the light.
O Jātavedas, drive away our enemies who have already been born; repel those yet unborn.
Speak for us with a benevolent mind; may we prevail, and drive our enemies away.
The forty-fourfold hymn-form is splendor as wealth; the sixteenfold hymn-form is vigor as wealth.
You are the soil of Agni, whose name is Apas; may all the gods acclaim you. Seated here upon the back of the Stoma, rich in ghee, bestow upon us wealth accompanied by progeny.
By that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras! The *eva* metre, the *varivas* metre, the *ācha* metre, the *manas* metre,

the *śambhu* metre, the *paribhu* metre, the *sindhu* metre, the *vyacas* metre, the *samudra* metre, the *salila* metre, the *kakubh* metre, the *trikakubh* metre, the *kāvya* metre, the *aṅkupa* metre, the *akṣarapaṅkti* metre.
The *chandas* is the *padapaṅkti*; the *chandas* is the *viṣṭārapaṅkti*; the *chandas* is the *kṣura-bhr̥j*; the *chandas* is the *pakṣa*; the *chandas* is the *pracha*;
the *chandas* is the *saṃyat*; the *chandas* is the *vyat*; the *chandas* is the *bṛhat*; the *chandas* is the *rathantaram*; the *chandas* is the *nikāyam*; the *chandas* is the *vīvadham*;
the *chandas* is the *giraḥ*; the *chandas* is the *bhr̥j*; the *chandas* is the *saṃstobha*; the *chandas* is the *anuṣṭubh*.
Eva is a metre; Varivas is a metre; Vayas is a metre; Vayaskṛt is a metre; Viśāla is a metre; Viṣpardhā is a metre; Chadiḥ is a metre; Dūrohaṇa is a metre; Tandra is a metre; Aṅkāvaṅka is a metre.
With the *raśmi* (beam), quicken the dwelling for the sake of the dwelling; with the *preti*, quicken the law for the sake of the law; with the *anviti*, quicken heaven for the sake of heaven;
with the *saṃdhi*, quicken the intermediate space for the sake of the intermediate space; with the *pratidhi*, quicken the earth for the sake of the earth;

with the *viṣṭambha*, quicken rain for the sake of rain; with the *pravāy*, quicken the day for the sake of the day; with the *anuvāy*, quicken the night for the sake of the night; with the *uśij*, [quicken] the Vasus.
Quicken the Vasus with foreknowledge; for the Rudras, quicken the Rudras with fair splendor; for the Ādityas, quicken the Ādityas with the thread; for offspring, quicken offspring with vigor;
for the fathers, quicken the fathers as the conqueror of armies; for cattle, quicken cattle as the possessor of wealth; for plants, quicken the plants with the two Revatīs;
for Indra, quicken Indra with the Abhijit and the joined pressing-stones; for the vital breath, quicken it with the overlordship.

Quicken the out-breath with the support; quicken the in-breath for the sake of the in-breath with the gliding one; quicken the eye for the sake of the eye with the bestower of vigor; quicken what has been studied for the sake of what has been studied with the threefold one;

quicken the threefold for the sake of the threefold with the threefold; quicken the turning forward for the sake of the turning forward with the turning forward; quicken the turning together for the sake of the turning together with the turning together;

quicken the following-turning for the sake of the following-turning with the following-turning; quicken the upward growth for the sake of the upward growth with the upward growth; [quicken] the forward growth for the sake of the forward growth with the forward growth.

Quicken *praroha* with *saṃroha*, quicken *saṃroha* for the sake of *saṃroha*; quicken *anūroha* with *anūroha*, quicken *anūroha* for the sake of *anūroha*; quicken *vasuka* with *vasuka*, quicken *vasuka* for the sake of *vasuka*;
quicken *veṣaśrī* with *veṣaśrī*, quicken *veṣaśrī* for the sake of *veṣaśrī*; quicken *vasyaṣṭi* with *vasyaṣṭi*, quicken *vasyaṣṭi* for the sake of *vasyaṣṭi*;
quicken *ākrānti* with *ākrānti*, quicken *utkrānti* with *utkrānti*, quicken *ākrānti* with *utkrānti*.

Thou art the queen, the eastern quarter; the Vasus are thy gods as overlords; Agni is the warder-off of missiles. May the threefold hymn (stoma) support thee on earth; may the butter-hymn (ājya-uktha) stabilize thee for steadiness; may the Rathantara-sāman establish thee in the atmosphere. May the first-born seers among the gods extend thee with the measure and width of heaven, and may this Dispenser [do the same].
And may all those overlords, being in agreement, establish you and the sacrificer upon the back of the firmament, in the heavenly world.

You are the Virāj; the southern quarter is yours; the Rudras are your gods; Indra is the warder-off of missiles. May the fifteenfold Stoma support you on earth; may the Praüga Uktha steady you for lack of wavering; may the Bṛhat Sāman provide stability.

May the Ṛṣis, first-born among the gods, spread thee out in the intermediate space with the measure and breadth of heaven. May this Vidhartṛ and the Adhipati, all of them in agreement, establish thee and the sacrificer on the back of the firmament, in the world of heaven.
Thou art the sovereign; the western quarter is thine; the Ādityas are thy gods; Soma is the warder-off of missiles; [the Stoma is] the seventeenfold.

May the *stoma* rest upon you on earth; may the *marutvatīya* hymn support you for stability; may the *vairūpa* chant establish you in the mid-air for firm standing. May the first-born seers among the gods extend you across the sky with its measure and breadth.
And may this Ordainer and this Overlord—may they all, in harmony, place the sacrificer upon the back of the firmament, in the world of heaven.

And may they settle it; the Self-Ruling One is your northern quarter; the Maruts are your divine overlords; Varuṇa is the repeller of weapons. May the twenty-one-fold hymn support you on earth; may the Niṣkevalya litany establish you for steadfastness; may the Vairāja Sāman provide stability in the atmosphere. May the Rishis, the first-born among the gods, extend you with the measure and breadth of heaven.

He is the Ordainer and he is the Overlord; may they all, being in full agreement, establish you and the sacrificer upon the back of the firmament, in the world of heaven. You belong to the Overlord; the upward direction is yours; the All-Gods are your overlords; Bṛhaspati is the warder-off of missiles.
May the Triṇava and Trayastriṃśa Stomas support you on earth, [along with] the Vaiśvadeva and Agnimāruta Śastras.

May the Śākvara and Raivata Sāmans, through the hymn (uktha), support you for non-stumbling; for the sake of stability in the intermediate space, may the first-born seers among the gods extend you with the measure and breadth of heaven. May both this Ordainer and the Overlord, all in harmony, establish you and the sacrificer upon the back of the firmament, in the world of heaven.

Direction: This eastern direction belongs to Harikeśa Sūryaraśmi; his chariot-makers are Rathakṛtsna and Rathaujas; his two leaders of the host are the Apsarases Puñjikasthalā and Kṛtasthalā; the Yātudhānas are his missiles, and the Rākṣasas are his projectiles. Homage to them!

Be gracious to us; may they be merciful to us. Whomsoever we hate and whosoever hates us—him we place within the jaws of these [deities]. This one is Dakṣiṇā Viśvakarman; his are Rathasvana and Rathecitra, the two leaders of the army and the village-clans. Menakā and Sahajanyā are the two Apsarases.
