May they not harm us; him whom we hate and him who hates us—we place him within their jaws.
This one behind is Vidadvasu; his chariot-bearer is Rathaprota and his charioteer is Asamaratha; the two *grāmaṇīs* are Āmlocantī and Pramlocantī, the two Apsarases;
the tiger is the weapon and the snakes are the missile. Homage be to them! May they be gracious to us; him whom we hate and him who hates us—[we place him] there.
We place him who hates us in the jaws of these. Here from the north is Saṃyadvasu;
his two leaders of the army and the hosts are Senajit and Suṣeṇa, and his two Apsarases are Viśvācī and Ghṛtācī. Water is their missile, wind is their weapon.
Let there be homage to them! May they be gracious to us. We place him whom we hate and whoever hates us in the jaws of these. Here from the north... [repeated].
Above is Arvāgvasu; his are Tārkṣya and Ariṣṭanemi, the leaders of the army and the hosts; Urvaśī and Pūrvacitti are the Apsarases;
Avasphūrja is the missile, Vidyut is the hurler. Homage be to them! May they be gracious to us. Whom we hate and whoever hates us—him we place within their jaws.
I settle you with the eastern quarter, with Agni as the deity, with the Gāyatrī metre;

I place the head of Agni with the head of the Gāyatrī metre. With the head of Agni, I place the head of Agni. I settle you with the southern quarter, with Indra as the deity, with the Triṣṭubh metre; I place the wing of Agni with the wing of the Triṣṭubh metre.

With the wing of Agni I lay down the wing of Agni; with the western quarter I settle you; with the Viśvedevas as your deity, with the Jāgata metre, I lay down the tail of Agni; with the tail of the Jāgata metre, with the tail of Agni I lay down the tail of Agni;
with the northern quarter I settle you; with the two gods Mitra and Varuṇa as your deity, with the Anuṣṭubh metre.
With the *chandas* of Agni I lay down the wing; with the wing of Agni belonging to the *anuṣṭubh* *chandas*, I lay down the wing of Agni.

With the upward direction I settle you; with Bṛhaspati as the deity and the *paṅkti* *chandas*, I lay down the back of Agni; with the back of Agni belonging to the *paṅkti* *chandas*, I lay down the back of Agni.
Madhu and Mādhava are the two spring seasons; you are the internal bond of Agni.
May heaven and earth be in harmony; may the waters and the plants be in harmony;
may the fires, acting in concert for my preeminence, be in harmony individually.
Those fires which are of one mind between heaven and earth,
conforming to the spring seasons— may they enter into [this fire] as the gods enter into Indra.

Śukra and Śuci are the two summer seasons; Nabhas and Nabhasya are the two rainy seasons; Iṣa and Ūrja are the two autumnal seasons; Sahas and Sahasya are the two winter seasons; Tapas and Tapasya are the two dewy seasons; you are the internal cohesion of Agni.
May heaven and earth be in harmony; may the waters and the plants be in harmony;
may the fires, acting in concert for my preeminence, be in harmony individually.
The fires that are of one mind between heaven and earth, belonging to the two dewy seasons and striving toward their goal— may they enter into Indra, just as the gods enter him.

Thou art the precursor of the east wind; thou art the precursor of the cloud; thou art the precursor of lightning; thou art the precursor of thunder; thou art the precursor of rain. Thou art the path of Agni; thou art the path of Agni belonging to Agni; thou art the path of Vāyu; thou art the path of Vāyu belonging to Vāyu; thou art the path of the gods;
thou art the path of the gods belonging to the gods; thou art the path of all the gods; thou art the path of all the gods belonging to all the gods.

Thou art the uniter; thou art seated in the intermediate space. Sit down! Ambā, Bulā, Nitatnī, Stanayantī, Abhrayantī, Meghayantī, Cupuṇīkā—[I offer] thee for the sake of water, thee for the sake of softness, thee for the sake of the *satīka* plant, thee for the sake of *ketā*, thee for the sake of *suketā*, thee for the sake of *saketa*, thee for Vivasvat, thee for Heaven, thee for Light, thee for the Ādityas.

Thou art named Udapurā, entered by food; thee I approach with my own self—with men, cattle, horses, life-span, luster, offspring, wealth, gain, wisdom, riches, and nourishment. Men are thy guardians, Agni is thy overlord.
By that deity, as did Aṅgiras, sit thou firm! Thou art named Aparājitā, entered by the sacred word (*brahman*); thee I approach with my own self.

With men, with cattle, with horses, with life-span, with luster, with progeny, with wealth, with gain, with wisdom, with riches, and with nourishment—O Maruts, may you be my guardians; Vāyu is the overlord. By that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras! Your name is Adhidyauḥ (Over-the-Sky); you are pervaded by immortality.
To you I go with my own self—with men, with cattle, with horses, with life-span, with luster, with progeny, and with wealth.

With faith, with wisdom, with wealth, with nourishment—may all the gods be your guardians, Sūrya your overlord. With that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras. May Prajāpati seat you upon the back of the earth. You are *bhūḥ*, you are the earth, you are the wide one, you are the broad one, you are Aditi, the sustainer of all, the upholder of the entire world. Support the earth, support the earth!

Strengthen the earth; do not harm it; protect me from the earth—for the sake of all out-breathing, in-breathing, diffused breathing, and upward breathing, for stability and movement—may Agni protect you with great well-being, with a most peaceful shelter. May Viśvakarman settle you on the back of the mid-region;
uphold the mid-region, strengthen the mid-region, do not harm the mid-region, protect me from the mid-region—for the sake of all.

For out-breathing, for in-breathing, for diffused-breathing, for up-breathing, for stability, for conduct—may Vāyu protect you with great well-being, with a most peaceful shelter. May Parameṣṭhin settle you upon the back of heaven, you who are spacious, far-extending, radiant, and possessed of rays; you who illumine heaven and earth and the wide mid-air; uphold heaven, uphold heaven!

Strengthen the sky; do not harm the sky; protect us from the sky! For the sake of every out-breath, in-breath, diffused breath, and upward breath; for stability and for movement—may Sūrya protect you with great well-being, with a most peaceful shelter.
Like a horse pricking up its ears in a pasture, when he has emerged from the great enclosure, then the wind blows after his flame; and let your path be black.
I set thee down in the seat of life, in the swelling of the ocean, in the shadow of the well. Homage to the ocean! Homage to the eye of the ocean!

Thou art the measure of a thousand, thou art the fore-measure of a thousand, thou art the counter-measure of a thousand, thou art the equal-measure of a thousand, thou art the up-measure of a thousand;
thou art of a thousand, for a thousand thee! May these bricks of mine be milch-cows in Agni—yea, even one.

A hundred and a hundred, a thousand and a thousand, ten thousand and ten thousand, a hundred thousand and a hundred thousand, a million and a million, ten million and ten million, a hundred million and a hundred million,

a billion and a billion, ten billion and ten billion, a hundred billion and a hundred billion, a trillion and a trillion— may these bricks of mine be milch-cows for Agni. Sixty, a thousand, ten thousand, inexhaustible, you abide in the seasons, increasing the seasons, dripping with clarity.

Dripping with honey, full of vigor, full of milk, providing the *svadhā* offering, and possessing nests— may these bricks of mine be milch-cows named Virāj, yielding all desires for me in yonder world, in that other world.
May the well-disposed bay horses bring you here with white, radiant steeds—
fleet as the wind, powerful, and swift as thought— to this sacrifice of mine, O Śarva, for my oblation.
I invoke Mahādeva, the first-born of the gods, the sages, and the asuras, the thousand-eyed Śiva.
Let us know that Puruṣa; let us meditate upon Mahādeva;
may that Rudra inspire us.
We know that [form] of Gāṅgaucya; we meditate upon the Son of the Mountain;
may Gaurī inspire us thereto.
Let us know that Kumāra; let us meditate upon Kārttikeya;
may Skanda inspire us.
Let us know that Karāṭa; let us meditate upon the Elephant-faced one;
may that Dantī inspire us.
We know that four-faced one; we meditate upon him who is seated on the lotus;
may that Brahmā inspire us.
We know that Keśava; we meditate upon Nārāyaṇa;
may that Viṣṇu inspire us.
We know that Bhāskara; we meditate upon Prabhākara;
may that Bhānu inspire us.
We know that Soma, the King; we meditate upon the Great King.
May Candra inspire us with that.
Let us know that [glory] of the Blazing One; let us meditate upon Vaiśvānara;
may Vahni inspire us toward that.
May we know that for the sake of abandoning; may we meditate upon that for the sake of great recitation;
may that meditation impel us.
Let us know that Supreme Self; let us meditate upon the Son of Vinatā;
may that Creation inspire us.
Homage to your wrath, O Rudra, and also to that arrow;
homage be to your bow and homage to your two arms.
O Rudra, that auspicious form of yours which is not terrible and does not appear evil—
with that most peaceful form, O Lord of the Mountain, look upon us with favor.
O Lord of the Mountain, that arrow which you carry in your hand to discharge—
O Lord of the Mountain, make it auspicious; do not harm the person or the world.
We address you with auspicious words, O Giriśa,
so that all people may be well-disposed toward us at our meeting.
The first divine physician, the advocate, has spoken in our favor;
crushing all serpents and all sorceresses, drive them far away to the nether regions.
That one who is copper-colored, ruddy, and even tawny, the most auspicious;
and those Rudras here who are stationed by the thousands in the directions around us—of them all, we implore the removal of wrath.
He who glides along, blue-necked and deep red—
him the cowherds have seen, him the water-carriers have seen,
and all living beings have seen him; may he, being seen, be gracious to us.
Homage to the one with blue matted hair, the thousand-eyed, the bountiful;
and also to those who are his companions—to them I have paid this homage.
Homage to that weapon of yours, the unstrung one, the bold;
homage also to both your arms, and homage to your bow.
Release the string from both ends of your bow;
O Blessed One, cast away those arrows that are in your hand.
O thousand-eyed one, wielder of the hundred quivers, having drawn your bow and blunted the points of your arrows,
be auspicious and well-disposed toward us.
The bow of the one with matted hair is strungless, and his quiver is without arrows;
his arrows have vanished, and his scabbard has disappeared.
May the missile of your bow avoid us on every side;
and whatever arrow is in your quiver, O Atri, place that within this one.
O most bountiful one, with that missile of yours which has become auspicious,
and with that bow of yours, protect us on every side from disease.

Homage to Hiraṇyabāhu, the leader of armies, and to the Lord of the Quarters; homage! Homage to the trees with golden hair, to the Lord of Animals; homage! Homage to the golden-haired one who wears the sacred thread, to the Lord of the Thriving; homage! Homage to the one tawny as young grass, the radiant one, to the Lord of Paths; homage! Homage to the dark-brown one, the piercer, to the Lord of Food; homage to Rudra, the archer!
Homage to the Lord of the Field; homage to the weapon of Bhava; homage to the Lord of the World; homage to the Unslayable Sūta;

homage to the Lord of the Forests; homage to Rohita the Architect; homage to the Lord of Trees; homage to the Counselor, the Merchant; homage to the Lord of the Bushes; homage to the One Who Is Present, the Provider of Water; homage to the Lord of Herbs; homage to the Conqueror.
Homage, homage to the piercer, the lord of those who pierce; homage to the one who cries out with a loud roar, the lord of beings;
homage, homage to the one clad in full armor as he runs, the lord of foot-soldiers; homage, homage to the quiver-bearer, the towering one, the lord of thieves;
homage, homage to the deceiver and the overreacher, the lord of robbers; homage, homage to the prowler and the wanderer, [the lord] of the forests.
Homage, homage to the Lord of thieves, who carries a sword and a quiver; homage, homage to those who roam as hunters, who seek to kill and plunder, homage to their Lord;

homage, homage to those who carry swords and wander by night, who cut down their prey, homage to their Lord; homage, homage to the turbaned one who wanders the mountains, homage to the Lord of those who steal by stealth. Homage, homage!

Homage to you, the makers of arrows and the makers of bows; homage to you, the bearers of arrows and the wielders of bows; homage to you who string them and those who fix the arrow to the string; homage to you who draw the bow and those who release the shaft; homage to you who shoot and those who pierce the mark; homage to you who sleep and those who are awake.
Homage, homage to you who are lying down and to you who are sitting; homage to you who are standing and to you who are running;
homage to the assemblies and to the lords of the assemblies; homage to the horses and to the lords of the horses;
homage to the piercing ones and to those who pierce; homage to the fierce hosts and to those who crush.

Homage, homage to you, the hosts and to you, the lords of the hosts; homage, homage to you, the troops and to you, the lords of the troops; homage, homage to you, the difficulties and to you, the lords of the difficulties; homage, homage to you, the deformed ones and to you, the multiformed ones;
homage, homage to you, the armies and to you, the army-leaders; homage, homage to you, the chariot-warriors and to you, the protectors.

Homage to the charioteers and to you, the collectors; homage, homage! Homage to the great ones and to you, the small; homage, homage! Homage to the young and to you, the aged; homage, homage! MS_2,9.4 //

Homage to the Brahmins and homage to you, the Kshatriyas; homage to the Sutas and homage to you, the Vaishyas; homage to the carpenters and homage to you, the chariot-makers; homage to the potters and homage to you, the smiths; homage to the Niṣādas and homage to you, the Puñjiṣṭhas; homage to the dog-keepers and homage to you, the hunters; homage! Homage to you, the dogs and the lords of dogs; homage to Bhava and Śarva; homage to Rudra and Paśupati;

homage to him with shorn hair and to the one with matted locks; homage to the blue-necked one and to the white-throated one; homage to the thousand-eyed one and to the one with a hundred bows; homage to Giriśa and to Śipiviṣṭa; homage to the most bountiful giver and to the wielder of the arrow.

Homage to the short one and to the dwarf; homage to the large one and to the most massive; homage to the aged one and to the well-grown; homage to the foremost one and to the first; homage to the swift one and to the fleet; homage to the gliding one and to the rapid;
homage to the one of the waves and to the one of the waters; homage to the one of the island and to the one of the stream.

Homage to him who possesses a swift army and to him who possesses a swift chariot; homage to him who wears a helmet and to him who wears armor; homage to him who is clad in mail and to him who has a protective fender; homage to the hero and to the piercer; homage to the renowned and to him whose army is renowned; homage to the elder and to the younger.
And homage to the one born before and to the one born after; homage to the middlemost and to the unassuming; homage to the last-born and to the foundational;
homage to the one belonging to the *sobha* tree and to the *pratisara*; homage to the one belonging to Yama and to the one belonging to peace;

homage to the one belonging to the conclusion and to the one belonging to the verse; homage to the one belonging to the fertile field and to the one belonging to the threshing floor; homage to the one belonging to the forest and to the one belonging to the thicket.
And homage to Śrava and to Pratiśrava; homage to Pathyā and to Sruṭyā; homage to Nādyā and to Vaiśanta; homage to Nīpyā and to Bhidyā; homage to Avaṭyā and to Kūpyā; homage to Sūdyā and to Sarasyā.
Homage to the one who possesses the drum and to the one who strikes it; homage to the bold and to the one who touches; homage to the one with the quiver and to the one with the arrow-case;
homage to the one with the sharp arrows and to the one with weapons; homage to the one with good weapons and to the one with a good bow;

homage to the one who belongs to the clouds and to the one who belongs to lightning; homage to the one who belongs to the rain and to the one who belongs to the drought; homage to the one who belongs to the piercing wind and to the one who belongs to the scorching heat; homage to the one who belongs to the storm.
And salutation to Reṣmaṇya, and salutation to Vāstavya and Vāstupā; salutation to Soma and Rudra; salutation to Tāmra and Aruṇa; salutation to Śaṅgu and Paśupati; salutation to Ugra and Bhīma;
salutation to Agravadha and Dūrevadha; salutation to the Slayer and the More-Slaying; salutation to the trees with green hair.
Homage to Tārā; homage to Śambhu and to Mayobhuva; homage to Śaṅkara and to Mayaskara; homage to Śiva and to Śivatara.
Homage to Śikhaṇḍin and to Pulastin; homage to Kiṃśila and to Kṣeṇa; homage to Iriṇya and to Prapathya;
homage to Gṛhya and to Goṣṭhya; homage to Gehya and to Talpya; homage to Kūlya and to Tīrthya; homage to Pārya and to Avārya; homage to Prataraṇa and to Uttaraṇa; homage to Pravāhya.

And homage to the one of the sand, and to the one of the foam; and homage to the one of the young grass, and to the one dwelling in the depths; and homage to the one of the brushwood, and to the one dwelling in the abyss; and homage to the one of the withered, and to the one of the green; and homage to the one of the dust, and to the one of the mist;
and homage to the one of the erasure, and to the one of the garment; and homage to the one of the wave, and to the one of the rod; and homage to the leaf, and to the one who dwells upon the leaves.

And homage to him who raises his arms in greeting and to him who strikes down; and homage to him who draws out and to him who draws forth; and homage to him who has drawn out and to him who has drawn forth.
Homage to the Girikas, the hearts of the gods; homage to the Vicinvatkas; homage to the Ākṣiṇakas; homage to the Ānṛhatas.
O wearer of the mantle, Lord of the food, O Daridra, blue-and-red one:
do not fear these cattle, do not harm these offspring, and let nothing whatsoever afflict us.
We offer these prayers to Rudra, the powerful one with matted hair, the ruler of heroes,
so that there may be well-being for our bipeds and quadrupeds, and so that everything in this village may be prosperous and free from disease.
O Rudra, that auspicious body of yours which is auspicious with healing remedies every day, and which is auspicious as a remedy for the roar— by means of that, be gracious to us so that we may live.

May the missile of Rudra pass us by, and may the ill-will of the impetuous evildoer avoid us. Unbend your firm [bow] for the sake of our patrons; O bounteous one, be gracious to our children and descendants.
O most bountiful, most auspicious one, be auspicious to us; be well-disposed. Having unbent your bow, be without anger and well-disposed.
Wearing the Pināka, come hither; clothed in a skin, move upward.
O Vyākṛḍa, O Vilohita, homage be unto you, O Blessed One!
May those thousand missiles of yours cast down others than us.
Thousands upon thousands are the missiles in your two arms;
as their master, O Maghavan, turn their points away from us.
Those thousands of Rudras who are upon the earth—
their bows we unstring at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
Those who dwell upon this great ocean in the intermediate space—
for them we unstring our bows at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
Those Rudras who have blue necks and white throats, who have resorted to heaven—
far away, at a distance of a thousand yojanas, we unstring their bows.
Those who have blue necks and dark throats, the Śarvas who roam upon the earth below—
their bows we unstring at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
Those who are tawny like young grass upon the trees, with blue necks and crimson bodies—
we unstring their bows at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
Those who are the lords of beings, with shaven heads or braided hair—
of them we unstring the bows at a distance of a thousand leagues.
Those who are the guardians of the paths, the protectors of the way, the Ailamṛḍas in battle— stretching our bows a thousand leagues away, we bend them over against them.
Those who frequent sacred fords, carrying bows and quivers.
We unstring their bows even at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
Those who pierce others while they drink from their vessels—
we cause their bowstrings to snap at a distance of a thousand yojanas.
As many Rudras as there are, or even more, who have spread out through the quarters—
of them we unstring the bows at a distance of a thousand yojanas.

Homage be to the Rudras who are in heaven, whose arrows are the rain; to them—ten to the east, ten to the south, ten to the west, ten to the north, and ten above—homage be to them! May they be gracious to us! Whomsoever we hate and whosoever hates us, him we place within their jaws. Homage be to the Rudras who are in the intermediate space, whose arrows are the winds.
To them—ten facing east, ten facing south, ten facing west, ten facing north, and ten facing upward—to them let there be homage!

May they be gracious to us; whomsoever we hate and whosoever hates us, him we place within their jaws. Homage to the Rudras who are on earth, whose arrows are food; to them—ten facing east, ten facing south, ten facing west, ten facing north.
Ten are above; let there be homage to them! May they be gracious to us. Whomsoever we hate and whosoever hates us—him we place within their jaws.
To those who are not terrible, and to those who are terrible, and to those more terrible than the terrible;
to all forms of Śarva, O Śarva, salutations to you, O Rudra, salutations to your forms!
O Blessed One, travel by that path which leads to the heavenly world, just as one well-guided follows a path to the land of cows.
These golden-colored ones are entering their own source.

Go, O Blessed One, for a return and for a future meeting, together with Sahadevī, together with Vṛṣa, together with your attendants, and together with your followers; to you who are invoked as "Salutation upon salutation" (namo-nama), to the Auspicious One (Śiva), let there be salutation to you;
do not harm me.
Invoked, invoked; saluted, saluted; dismissed, dismissed: go your way, go your way; go to heaven, go to heaven; go to the light of heaven, go to the light of heaven; homage be to you; do not harm me.

The strength that rests upon the stone, upon the mountain, gathered from the waters, from the plants, and from the trees—O Maruts, bestowing it with favor, grant us that food and strength! Let hunger be in the stone, let that strength be in me; let your heat reach him whom we hate.
O Agni, we envelop you with the moss of the ocean;
be purifying and auspicious for us.
O Agni, we envelop you with the caul of the frost; be purifying and auspicious for us.
Come down to the earth, come to the reed, descend into the rivers, O Agni; you are the bile of the waters. O female frog, come hither with them!
And make this sacrifice of ours auspicious, O you of purifying hue.
This is the gathering place of the waters, the dwelling of the ocean;
may your missiles burn others than us; O Purifier, be auspicious toward us.
O Agni, purifier, with your radiance; O purifier, O shining one, [protect] us.
With his purifying and radiant form, he has shone upon the earth like the banner of the dawn;
he who, like one parched by heat, has come forth ageless, as if speeding on the path in the battle for Etaśa’s prize.
Homage to your consuming flame and to your radiance; homage to you!
May your missiles strike down others than us; O Purifier, be auspicious unto us.

Hail to him who sits on the tree, hail to him who sits among men, hail to him who sits in the waters, hail to him who sits on the sacrificial grass, hail to him who sits in the forest, hail to the finder of heaven!
O Lord of Food, grant us food that is free from disease and full of vigor;
further prolong the life of the giver, and bestow strength upon our bipeds and quadrupeds.
Those gods who among gods are worthy of sacrifice, who among those worthy of sacrifice sit for their annual portion—
those who do not eat the oblation at this sacrifice, let them themselves drink of the honey and the ghee.
Those gods who attained godhead from among the gods, who are the precursors of this Brahman,
without whom no domain whatsoever is purified— they are neither upon the ridges of heaven nor upon those of earth.
Giver of breath, giver of out-breath, giver of diffused breath, bestower of luster, bestower of wide space:
let your missiles burn others than us; O Purifier, be auspicious unto us!
May Agni with his sharp flame strike down every devouring demon;
may Agni win wealth for us.
He who, as the seer and the Hotṛ priest, sat down making oblations to all these worlds— he, our father,
seeking wealth through his prayer and desiring to be the first coverer, entered into the lower [world].
What was the wood and what was that tree from which they fashioned heaven and earth? O wise ones, ask this with your mind: upon what did he stand while supporting the worlds?
What was the foundation, what was the starting point, and how was it? From what did Viśvakarman, the all-seeing, producing the earth, spread out the sky by his greatness—
he who is all-seeing, whose face is on every side, whose hands are on every side, and whose feet are on every side?
The one God, generating heaven and earth, blew them together with his arms and with his wings.

O Viśvakarman, those stations of yours which are highest, which are lowest, and these which are middle—teach them to your friends with the oblation, O self-dependent one; sacrifice for yourself, taking pleasure in your own body.
O Viśvakarman, by means of the strengthening oblation, you made Indra a protector who is invincible;
to him the divine tribes bowed down, so that he might be formidable and worthy of invocation.
O Viśvakarman, increasing by means of the oblation, sacrifice yourself to both the earth and the sky!
Let other people around us be confounded; here, let the bountiful lord be our patron.
Today, for our protection, let us invoke Vācaspati, the all-maker, who yokes his mind at will, in this contest;
may he, the source of all well-being and the performer of righteous deeds, find pleasure in our nearest invocations and grant us aid.
The wise father of the eye begot these two with his mind as they were bowing down;
when their eastern limits were firmly established, then indeed heaven and earth expanded.
Viśvakarman, who is far-reaching, the upholder and the ordainer, the supreme beholder, measured out [the worlds].
Their desires rejoice together with nourishment where they say there is one beyond the seven seers.
Those ancient seers, like singers in great number, offered prayers for wealth in this world.
Seated in the formed realm of the unformed, they are those who fashioned these beings.
He who is our father, our progenitor, he who is the ordainer, he who, being already existent, brought us forth;
he who alone is the giver of names to the gods—to him all other worlds go for instruction.
Beyond the sky, beyond this earth, beyond the gods— whatever exists as the *asura*—
what indeed was that first embryo which the waters held, wherein all the gods came together?
That very first embryo the waters held, wherein all the gods beheld it together.
Upon the navel of the Unborn is fixed that One, upon which all worlds rest.
When Viśvakarman was born as a god, he then became the Gandharva for the second time;
the third was the father who generated the plants—they have distributed the germ of the waters in many places.
You do not know him who generated these [beings], for something else has come between you.
Enveloped by mist and idle talk, the reciters of hymns wander about, seeking only their own sustenance.
Lead him upward, O Agni, you who are invoked with clarified butter;
endow him with splendor and make him abundant with progeny.
O Indra, lead this man further forward; may he be the master over his kinsmen.
Unite us with the increase of wealth; may you be a giver of portions to the gods.
O Agni, cause him to prosper in whose house we perform the oblation;
for him let the gods speak favorably, as does this Brahmaṇaspati.
Swift, sharpening his weapons like a bull eager for battle, the striker, the shaker of the people,
the roaring one, the unblinking sole hero— Indra has conquered a hundred armies at once.
With Indra— the one who thunders, the unblinking, the victorious, the one who stirs up conflict, the one difficult to shake, and the bold—
conquer and prevail in battle, O men, with that bull who holds arrows in his hand.
He, the controller, with bowmen bearing arrows and quivers, is Indra among the hosts in battles where troops clash;
he is the conqueror of those who meet in conflict, the drinker of Soma, strong of arm, with his bow uplifted, shooting with well-aimed shafts.
O Bṛhaspati, fly around with your chariot, slayer of demons, driving away the enemy;
shattering the armies, crushing them in battle, and conquering, be the protector of our chariots!
Piercing through the cow-pens with force, seizing them, the hero Indra, of a hundredfold wrath—
unshakable, the subduer of armies, invincible— may he protect our troops in the battles.

O Indra, discoverer of strength, elder, pre-eminent hero, powerful, vigorous, victorious, fierce, superior hero, superior warrior, winner of power through might, winner of cattle— ascend your victorious chariot!
He who pierces the clans, the winner of cattle, the thunderbolt-armed, who conquers the racecourse and crushes [the foe] with his might—O kinsmen, emulate this hero; O friends, rally after Indra!
May Indra be their leader; may Bṛhaspati, the sacrificial fee, the sacrifice, and Soma go before them.
Let the Maruts march in the midst of the divine armies as they shatter and conquer.
The fierce roar of the gods has arisen—the host of Indra the bull, of King Varuṇa, of the Ādityas, and of the Maruts; the high-minded ones who cause the worlds to tremble, the victorious deities.
May Indra be with us when the banners meet; may our arrows be victorious.
May our heroes be superior; O gods, protect us in the battles!
Upward, indeed, do I raise you.
May the five divine quarters protect the sacrifice, O goddesses, driving away ignorance and ill-will;
bestowing upon the lord of the sacrifice an abundance of wealth, the sacrifice has been established upon that abundance of wealth.
When the fire was kindled, the gods—worthy of praise, grasped, and having the hymns as their wings—honored him greatly;
taking hold of the heated *gharma*, they performed the sacrifice when the gods perfected the rite with vigor.
For the divine Dhātṛ, the Ordainer, the god-glory, the glorious-minded one with a hundred feet,
having taken hold of the sacrifice, has come.
Golden-haired, with rays like the sun, Savitar rises in the east as an eternal light;
at his impulse, the wise Pūṣan goes forth, the guardian who beholds all beings.

The gods stood among the gods, performing the duties of the *adhvaryu*; let the two *śamitṛ* priests enjoy the well-sacrificed victim for the sake of worship. Where the fourth sacrifice goes with the oblation, from there may the prayers and our blessings be graciously accepted.
All songs have magnified Indra, who is as expansive as the ocean,
the best of charioteers among charioteers, the true lord and master of spoils.
This celestial chariot sits in the midst of heaven, filling the two worlds and the intermediate space;
it looks out upon all the ghee-dripping, all-pervading regions between the eastern and the western beacon.
The bull, the ruddy bird in the ocean, has entered the womb of the ancient father;
placed in the midst of heaven as a speckled stone, he has stepped forth and guards the two ends of the space.
May the one who invokes favor bring the sacrifice hither; may Agni, the god, worship and bring the gods hither.
May the one who invokes the gods bring the sacrifice hither; may Agni, the god, worship and bring the gods hither.
"By the impulse of strength," and so on—these two [verses].
Advance with Agni, bearing the fire-pan in your hands, to the vault of heaven;
having gone to the back of the sky, the light of heaven, sit down mingled with the gods.
Along the eastern direction.
O Agni, go forth as the first among those who approach the gods; you are the eye of the gods and of mortals.
May the sacrificers, desiring to perform the sacrifice together with the Bhr̥gus, go safely to the heavenly light.
From the earth I have ascended to the intermediate space; from the intermediate space I have ascended to heaven;
from the back of the celestial vault, I have gone to the light of *svar*.
Ascending to heaven, they do not look back; they rise up to the sky and the two worlds,
they who, being well-knowing, have spread the sacrifice that flows in every direction.
O Agni, thousand-eyed, you are Night and Dawn.
You are Suparṇa, the Garuḍa; sit upon the back of the earth!
Fill the intermediate space with your radiance, prop up the sky with your light, and strengthen the quarters with your splendor!
Being invoked, O Agni of beautiful countenance, sit down in your own womb from the east, O Sādhya. In this higher common dwelling-place, may all the gods and the sacrificer sit together.
I choose that wondrous, all-beneficent favor of the adorable Savitṛ,
which Kaṇva milked from him— the swelling, great cow, flowing with a thousand streams and rich in milk.
Let us worship you in your highest birth, O Agni; let us worship with hymns in your lower dwelling-place.
From whatever womb you have arisen, sacrifice to that; when you are kindled, they have offered oblations unto you.
O Agni, youngest one, shine forth for us, blazing with your tireless flame;
ever-increasing strengths attend upon you.
O Agni, him today; O Agni, those seven of yours.
I offer the oblation upon the altar with my mind, so that the gods, who increase the cosmic order and enjoy the sacrifice, may come hither.
In the course of the ocean, the path of your wisdom, I offer this oblation to Viśvakarman,
which is invincible every day.
Śukrajyotis, Citrajyotis, Satyajyotis, Jyotiṣmat, Satya, Ṛtapā, Atyaṃhas, Ṛtajit, Satyajit, Senajit, Suṣeṇa, Antimitra, Dūremitra, and the host Ṛta.

And Satya, Dhruva, Dharuṇa, Dhartṛ, Vidhartṛ, and Vidhāraya; Īdṛṅ, Etādṛṅ, Sadṛṅ, Pratisadṛṅ, Mita, Saṃmita, and Sabhara—O Maruts, come hither for our aid, you who are suchlike, even so like, similar, and corresponding; you who are measured and well-measured, the sustainers, come to our sacrifice.

Just as the divine hosts, the Maruts, were followers of Indra, and as the divine hosts, the Maruts, became followers of Indra, so may both the divine and human hosts become followers of this sacrificer.
May vigor and my impulse, my exertion and my expansion, my devotion and my will, my tone and my fame,
my hearing and my revelation, my light and my heaven, my out-breath and my in-breath, my diffused breath and my life-force, my thought and my intention, and my speech and my mind [prosper].

And my eye, and my ear, and my dexterity, and my strength, and my vital energy, and my endurance, and my life-span, and my old age, and my self, and my body, and my shelter, and my armor, and my limbs, and my bones, and my joints,
and my physical forms, and my seniority, and my sovereignty, and my wrath.
And my radiance, and my luster, and my water, and my victory, and my greatness, and my width, and my breadth, and my height, and my length, and my growth, and my increase.

Truth is mine, faith is mine, the world is mine, wealth is mine, control is mine, brilliance is mine, play is mine, joy is mine, the well-spoken hymn is mine, the well-done deed is mine, what has been born is mine, what is yet to be born is mine, what is acquired is mine,
what is to be acquired is mine, what has come to be is mine, what is to come to be is mine, prosperity is mine, the power of prosperity is mine, and the good path is mine.

May my good path be mine; may my preparedness be mine; may my preparation be mine; may my thought be mine; may my good thought be mine; may my well-being be mine; may my joy be mine; may my beloved be mine; may my desire be mine; may my wish be mine; may my mental happiness be mine;

may my fortune be mine; may my wealth be mine; may my prosperity be mine; may my excellence be mine; may my superiority be mine; may my glory be mine; may my cosmic order be mine; may my immortality be mine.

And may there be freedom from consumption for me, and freedom from disease for me, and vitality for me, and long life for me, and absence of enemies for me, and fearlessness for me, and happiness for me, and a good bed for me, and fair nights for me, and a fair day for me.

May my controller and my sustainer, my security and my steadfastness, my universe and my greatness, my consciousness and my wisdom, my procreation and my productivity, my plow and my furrow, my vital energy and my truthfulness,
my milk and my sap, my clarified butter and my honey, my shared meal and my shared drink— [may these be mine].
May agriculture be mine, may rain be mine, may victory be mine, may security be mine, may wealth be mine, may riches be mine, may prosperity be mine, may growth be mine,
may the pervasive be mine, may the powerful be mine, may the full be mine, may the fuller be mine,
may the grain-destroyer be mine, may imperishability be mine, may freedom from hunger be mine, may food be mine, may rice be mine, may barley be mine, and may beans be mine.
Sesame seeds are mine, grains are mine, millet is mine, wild rice is mine, uncultivated rice is mine, wheat is mine, lentils are mine, mung beans are mine, and chickpeas are mine.

May the mountains be mine, may the hills be mine, may the sands be mine, may the trees be mine; may the stone be mine, may the clay be mine, may the gold be mine, may the iron be mine, may the lead be mine, may the tin be mine, may the dark metal be mine, may the red metal be mine; may fire be mine, may water be mine, may the herbs be mine, may the creepers be mine, may the crops ripening in tilled soil be mine, and may the crops ripening in untilled soil be mine.
May my domestic animals and my wild animals prosper through sacrifice; may my wealth and my acquisition, my being and my prosperity, my purpose and my attainment, my approach and my movement,
my action and my power, my riches and my dwelling, and Agni and Indra for me, and Soma and Indra for me.

And may Savitṛ and Indra be mine; and Sarasvatī and Indra be mine; and Pūṣan and Indra be mine; and Aditi and Indra be mine; and Dhātṛ and Indra be mine; and Tvaṣṭṛ and Indra be mine; and Mitra and Indra be mine; and Varuṇa and Indra be mine; and Viṣṇu and Indra be mine; and Bṛhaspati [be mine].
And may Indra and the Vasus be mine; and may Indra and the Rudras be mine; and may Indra and the Ādityas be mine; and may Indra and the Maruts be mine; and may Indra and the Earth be mine;
and may Indra and the Atmosphere be mine; and may Indra and the Sky be mine; and may Indra and the Constellations be mine; and may Indra and the Year be mine.

May Indra and my agriculture; may Indra and my rain; may Indra and my quarters; may Indra and all the gods; may Indra and my stalk; may Indra and my ray; may Indra and my overlord; may Indra and my inviolable cup;
may Indra and my *upāṃśu* cup; may Indra and my *antaryāma* cup; may Indra and my *aindravāyava* cup; may Indra and my *maitrāvaruṇa* cup; may Indra and my *āśvina* cup.

And for me the Pratiprasthātṛ, and for me the Śukra cup, and for me the Manthin cup, and for me the Āgrayaṇa cup, and for me the Vaiśvadeva cup, and for me the Aindrāgna cup, and for me the Kṣullakavaiśvadeva cup, and for me the Dhruva cup, and for me the Vaiśvānara cup,
and for me the Marutvatīya cups, and for me the Niṣkevalya cup, and for me the Sāvitra cup, and for me the Sārasvata cup, and for me the Pātnīvata cup.

My *hāriyojana* cup and my offering spoons and my chalices and my *vāyavya* vessels and my *droṇakalaśa* vat and my two pressing-boards and my pressing-stones and my *pūtabhṛt* vessel and my *apūtabhṛt* vessel and my sacrificial grass and my altar and my purificatory bath and my cry of "Svadhā" and my cry of "Svāhā."

May Agni and Gharma and Arka and Sūrya and Prāṇa and Aśvamedha and Aditi and Pṛthivī and Diti and Dyau and the Śakvarī verses and the fingers and the quarters be perfected for me through sacrifice; may the Season and the Vow and the Year and Penance and Day-and-Night and the Urvaṣṭīvas and the Bṛhat and Rathantara be perfected for me through sacrifice; and may the One and the Three [be perfected].

And [the animals] of the Thirty-three are: four and eight, forty-eight, a three-year-old male and a three-year-old female, a two-year-old male and a two-year-old female, a five-year-old male and a five-year-old female, a three-month-old calf and a three-month-old heifer, a four-month-old male and a four-month-old female, a six-month-old male and a six-month-old female, a bull, a cow, a steer, a barren cow, a milch-cow, and a draft-ox.
May the *stoma*, the *yajuḥ*, the *ṛc*, and the *sāman*; may the consecration (*dīkṣā*), austerity (*tapas*), the *bṛhat* and the *rathantara*;

may the plants, the trees, and the quarters be prepared for me through sacrifice. For food thee, for strength thee, for the winning of strength thee; for brilliance thee, for vigor thee, for wealth thee, for prosperity thee!
And: O Viśvedevas, may all the Maruts come to us today with all their aids; may all the fires be well-kindled.
May all the gods come here to us with protection; may all wealth and strength be ours.
May Vāja protect me here— the seven directions, the four distant realms,
and Vāja with all the gods— at the winning of wealth.
May Vāja be before us and in our midst; may Vāja arrange the gods according to the seasons.
For at the impulse of Vāja, all things bend down; may I become a lord of Vāja, master of all quarters.
May Vāja impel my gift today; may Vāja strengthen the gods with the oblation.
For Vāja has made me possessed of all heroes; as lord of Vāja, may I conquer all directions.
I unite myself with the milk of the earth; I unite myself with the waters and the plants.
As such, O Agni, may I win the prize of strength.
Place milk upon the earth, milk in the plants, milk in heaven, and milk in the intermediate space;
may the quarters of the sky be full of milk for me.
Agni, the upholder of cosmic order, whose abode is cosmic order, is the Gandharva; his Apsarases are the plants, named "Joy.
May he protect this our spiritual power (brahman) and our ruling power (kṣatra); may they protect this our spiritual power and our ruling power. To him, Svāhā! Vaṭ! To them, Svāhā! Vaṭ! Saṃhita.

Sūrya Viśvasāman is the Gandharva; his Apsarases are the Marīcis, named Āyus. Candramas Suṣumṇa, the ray of the sun, is the Gandharva; his Apsarases are the Nakṣatras, named Bekurīs. Vāta Iṣira Viśvavyacas is the Gandharva; his Apsarases are the Waters, named Ūrjas. Yajña Suparṇa is the Gandharva; his Apsarases are the Dakṣiṇās.

The *eṣṭayaḥ* are named: Bṛhaspati is the Gandharva, his Apsarases are the Maruts, and their name is Ojas; Prajāpati Parameṣṭhin is [the deity], Manas is the Gandharva, his Apsarases are the Ṛk-sāmans, and their name is Stava; Amṛdayas is [the deity], Dūreheti Mṛtyu is the Gandharva, his Apsarases are the creatures, and their name is Bhīravaḥ. O Lord of the World, may he whose [world] is above us [protect us].
O Lord of the Virāj, grant great protection to this Brahman, to this Kṣatra;
may those whose name is Apsaras, and who pervade all your quarters, protect this our Brahman and Kṣatra—may they protect this our Brahman and Kṣatra!
To him, Svāhā! Vaṭ! To them, Svāhā! Vaṭ!

Thou art the ocean, full of moisture, the giver of moisture; bringing bliss and joy, blow upon me! Svāhā! Thou art the seeker of help, the recipient of worship; bringing bliss and joy, blow upon me! Svāhā! Thou art the Marut, the host of the Maruts; bringing bliss and joy, blow upon me! Svāhā!
United with the waters and the Āyus, united with the Dawn and her ruddy beams, in harmony with the Aśvins and their wondrous deeds, [thou art] united. Svāhā!
O Hero, together with Etaśa, Vaiśvānara, and with the sacrificial food and clarified butter—svāhā!
With the *iḍā*:
"I yoke Agni with power and ghee—the divine, well-winged, vigorous, great one.
By him may we fly to the summit of the radiant sun, ascending to the heavenly vault upon the highest firmament."
These two ageless wings of yours, O Agni, with which you drive away the Rākṣasas—
by means of them may we fly to the world of the doers of good deeds, where the ancient Ṛṣis who were first have gone.
The Moon is skillful, a hawk, a follower of Truth, a golden-winged bird, swift-moving;
he sits firm and great in his dwelling-place. Homage be to you; do not harm me.
You are the head of heaven, the navel of the earth, the vigor of the waters and the plants;
possessing all life, a wide-extending shelter, you stand supported upon the head of the universe on the path of homage.
In the ocean is your heart; within it is life. Give us water, break open the reservoir!
From heaven, from Parjanya, from the intermediate space, and from the earth—therefrom favor us with rain.
I loosen your girth, I loosen your reins, I loosen your yokes and your fastenings.
Grant us here auspicious wealth; declare me a giver of portions among the deities.

May Agni, the giver of wealth, worshipped by the Bhṛgus, the bestower of blessings by the Yatis, and worshipped by the Vasus when invoked with oblations, fulfill our sacrifice; may this well-offered oblation be a source of joy to the gods. Homage!
By means of which [sacrificial] observances the seers performed the sacrificial session with austerity, kindling the fire while bringing forth the light of heaven—
that fire which men call "one for whom the sacred grass is strewn," upon that firmament I have placed the fire.
O gods, may we follow him with our wives, with sons, with brothers, or with gold;
grasping the firmament in the world of the well-done, upon the third ridge in the luminous realm of heaven.
The restless one has ascended to the midst of speech; this Agni, the lord of the virtuous, is far-seeing.
Established upon the back of the earth, he flashes brilliantly; let him cast beneath his feet those who seek to attack us.
May this Agni, the most heroic, the bestower of vitality, shine forth a thousandfold, never failing;
blazing brilliantly from the midst of the waters, proceed toward the celestial abodes.
O Agni, move forward; proceed along together; make manifest the paths that lead to the gods.
Undertake this very good deed, where the ancient seers of old have gone.
Depart together; come forth together! Prepare the paths that lead to the gods.
May we follow these good deeds to where our ancient fathers have passed away.
Awake, O Agni, and watch over him; may you two unite this man with his sacrifices and meritorious works. Making themselves young again, let the fathers follow this thread of yours.
O Agni, by that path by which you carry a thousand, and by which you carry all wealth,
by that same path carry this sacrifice of ours to the light, so that it may go among the gods.
This is yours.
O Agni, may the seasons, the years, the seers, and all that is true increase thee;
shine together with the celestial light and illuminate all four quarters.
O Agni, be kindled and awaken him; arise for great good fortune.
May he who sits near you, O Agni, not come to harm; may your Brahmins be glorious, and not others.
O Agni, these Brahmins choose you; O Agni, be auspicious for us in our dwelling. O Agni, slayer of rivals, conqueror of those who attack, be watchful in your own home, never failing.
Right here, O Agni, bestow wealth upon us; let not those who seek to harm you in their former thoughts overcome you.
May sovereignty be easy for you to govern, O Agni; may your worshipper increase, unsubdued.

O Agni, exert yourself with your own sovereign power; O Agni, strive as a friend in the establishment of friendship. For the sake of presiding over your kinsmen among the kings, O Agni, shine here with joy.
Beyond excessive cold, beyond excessive heat, beyond thoughtlessness, and beyond destruction—O Agni, for you cross over all difficulties; therefore, grant us wealth together with heroic sons.
Invincible, Jātavedas, unsubdued, the far-shining Agni, sustainer of dominion, shine here!
Driving away the maladies of men, protect us today with your auspicious powers for our prosperity.
O Bṛhaspati, O Savitṛ, awaken him; sharpen him further, even though he is already sharpened.
Cause him to grow for great good fortune, and may all the gods rejoice after him.
O Bṛhaspati, since you have released us from the curse of Yama so that we may not come to be there,
may the Aśvins ward off death from us by the powers of the physicians of the gods, O Agni.
Beholding the higher light beyond the darkness,
we have gone from among the gods to Sūrya, the god, the supreme light.
Upward rise his fuel-sticks, upward the bright flames of Agni,
most radiant for the son of beautiful countenance.
May Tanūnapāt, the Asura, the all-knowing god, anoint for the gods the paths leading to them with honey and ghee;
being gratified, he approaches the sacrifice with honey.
Agni, praised by men, the god Savitṛ, doer of good deeds, possessor of all boons—
he approaches this [place] with power and with ghee.
Being praised with reverence, Agni, the bearer, [is served] with ladles as the sacrifices proceed;
may he worship the majesty of this Agni.
May he, the delightful one, [be seated] upon the well-prepared grass.
He who is great as Mitra through the sacrificial grass, the most observant, and the greatest bestower of wealth.
All the goddesses, the doors, submit themselves to his laws— the laws of Agni—
as they preside over their wide-extending domain by his power.
May those two divine maidens, Dawn and Night, like two wives in their own dwelling,
protect this sacrifice and our ritual service.
O two divine Hotars, with the tongues of Agni, graciously accept this our upward-tending sacrifice;
make it well-offered for us.
May the three goddesses— Ṛtī, Sarasvatī, and Mahī Bhāratī— being praised, come to this pleasant sacred grass.
Then, O Tvaṣṭṛ, release for us that wonderful draught of soma, rich in food, abounding in hero-strength, and the very center of the increase of wealth.
O Lord of the Forest, being gracious, release [the victim] yourself for the gods;
may Agni, the immolator, prepare the oblation.
O Agni Jātavedas, perform the *svāhā* offering for Indra and for the gods;
may all the gods enjoy this oblation.
Some flow together, others approach; the rivers fill the same ocean bed.
The pure waters have surrounded him, the pure and radiant Son of the Waters.
Golden-hued is he, golden in appearance; even Apāṃ Napāt is golden-hued.
Having sat down from his golden womb, the givers of gold bestow food upon him.

Golden-colored, pure, and purifying, those waters in which Kaśyapa was born and in which Indra was born—those waters of diverse forms who have held Agni as their embryo; may they be auspicious and pleasant to us.
Those in whose midst King Varuṇa moves, beholding the truth and falsehood of men—
those waters which drip sweetness, which are pure and purifying— may they be auspicious and pleasant to us.

Those waters for which the gods in heaven prepare a draught, those that exist manifoldly in the intermediate space, and those bright ones that flow with milk upon the earth— may those waters be auspicious and pleasant to us.
Behold me with a gracious eye; touch my skin with your gracious body.
I invoke all the Agnis who dwell in the waters: bestow upon me luster, strength, and vigor.
Because when you were flowing together, you roared as you were slain by the Day, therefore you are called "Nadyas" (Roarers); those are your names, O rivers.
When you, O waters, were released by Varuṇa and swiftly surged together, Indra reached you as you were flowing; therefore, O waters, you move in accordance with his will.
Flowing against your will, you indeed closed off your own course; O goddesses, Indra restrained you with his powers, and therefore the name "Vārs" (obstructers) was bestowed upon you.
A single god stood over you as you were flowing according to your will; "the great ones have risen up," he said, and therefore water is called *udaka*.
From the very beginning I see them, or indeed I hear them; now their sound comes unto me.
The potent juice of those who are mixed with honey has come to me; may it come to me together with breath and splendor.
O divine waters, flowing with clarity, you bear Agni and Soma; you are indeed those waters. Thinking thus, I partook of immortality then, when I was satiated by you, O golden-colored ones.
The three verses beginning with "āpo hi ṣṭhā."
Rest in heaven; strive in the intermediate space; arise from the earth; go to radiance.

Thou art the source of austerity; with all holy thoughts I lay thee down, unbroken. The source is the cosmic order (*ṛta*), the source is truth (*satya*), the source is sacred knowledge (*brahman*), the source is sovereignty (*kṣatra*), the source is the earth, the source is the intermediate space, the source is the sky, the source is the quarters.

Continuing from the out-breath (*prāṇa*) to the in-breath (*apāna*), continuing from the in-breath to the diffused breath (*vyāna*), continuing from the diffused breath to sight, continuing from sight to hearing, continuing from hearing to the earth, continuing from the earth to the intermediate space, continuing from the intermediate space to heaven, continuing from heaven to the quarters, continue from the quarters along to the heavenly world.

With the *ṛc* metre I settle you; with the *vaṣaṭ*-call metre I settle you; with the *hiṃ*-call metre I settle you; with the *prastāva* metre I settle you; with the *udgītha* metre I settle you; with the *pratihāra* metre I settle you; with the *stotra* metre I settle you; with the *nidhana* metre I settle you.
I honor with my song your immortal messenger, who belongs to all the gods, the bearer of oblations, the most excellent sacrificer.
We have approached with great reverence the youngest one who has shone forth, well-kindled in his own dwelling—
the one of wondrous luster between the two wide worlds, well-invoked, facing all directions.
This is here.
Whether he has run forth after him or whether he has proclaimed the sacred formulations (*brahmāṇi*),
he encompasses all poetic insights (*kāvyā*) as the felly encompasses the wheel.
O bright one, Lord of the people, you cook both ladles in your mouth;
therefore, O Lord of Strength, fill us up during our hymns and bring nourishment to those who praise you.
With the bones of Dadhyañc, Indra, irresistible, struck down ninety-nine Vṛtras.
Regarding this, it is said: "They recognized the secret name of Tvaṣṭṛ’s cow here in the dwelling of the moon."
They found the horse's head which had been hidden away among the mountains, at Śaryaṇāvat.
To Indra alone have the singers sung aloud; to Indra with hymns have the chanters chanted;
to Indra have the voices cried out.
Indra, with his far-reaching vision, caused the sun to ascend in the sky;
he split the mountain open with the rays of light.
Indra indeed, together with his two bay horses, joined and yoked by a word; Indra is the wielder of the thunderbolt, golden-hued.
O Indra, protect us in battles for booty and in contests for a thousandfold prizes,
you who are fierce with your fierce aids.
We incite that Indra for the sake of great victory, to slay Vṛtra;
may he become the bull, the showerer of blessings.
Indra was made for the act of giving; he is established as the most powerful in strength;
he is resplendent, worthy of praise, and the friend of Soma.
Like a thunderbolt forged by speech, he is powerful and unshakable; fierce and invincible, he has grown great.
This Agni is the possessor of a thousandfold; Agni is the head. O Agni, [I have taken thee] from the lotus-leaf.
Agni has been awakened by the fuel of men, facing the Dawn as she approaches like a cow;
like great birds rising up to a branch, his rays stream forth toward the firmament.
We have spoken a word of praise to the wise, holy one, the bull, the strong;
Gaviṣṭhira has offered with reverence a far-reaching hymn to Agni, like a golden ornament set in the sky.

He has become conscious for the sacrifice to the gods; Agni, upright and well-disposed, has stood up at dawn. The radiant splendor of the kindled one has been seen; the great god has been released from the darkness.
The watchful guardian of the people has been born—Agni, the highly skillful, for new-found prosperity.
With his face anointed with ghee, he shines brilliantly and purely for the Bharatas, reaching to the great heavens with his lofty flame.
O Agni, the Aṅgirases discovered you hidden in secret, dwelling in wood after wood;
being churned, you are born with great might; they call you, O Aṅgiras, the son of strength.
For you, O Agni, let this speech be most sweet; for you, let this inspired thought be a blessing to the heart.
As great rivers fill the ocean, so do our songs fill you and increase you with power.
O bull-like Agni, you gather for yourself all that belongs to the noble;
you are kindled in the place of *iḷā*; as such, bring us riches.
With my song, I praise Agni, the ancient god of you all, the lord of treasures;
O worshipful ones, I laud him who is beloved by many, like Mitra, the establisher of our domain.
O Agni, most rich in wonderful renown, the people among the tribes invoke you—
the one with flaming hair, beloved by many— to carry their oblations.
O Agni, we kindle you—the radiant, unaging god—so that this most praiseworthy fuel of yours may shine in heaven; bring nourishment to those who offer praise.
I meditate upon that Agni who is the Vasu, to whom the milch-cows go home, to whom the swift horses go home, and to whom the constant prize-winners go home; bring nourishment to those who praise you!

He is Agni who is praised as the Vasu, unto whom the milch-cows come together, the swift-running horses come together, and the well-born patrons come together; bring nourishment to those who praise you!
With this homage, I invoke for you Agni, the Son of Strength— the beloved,
most wise steward of the sacrifice, the immortal messenger of all.
O Agni, you are the master of the house; you are our Hotṛ at the sacrifice. You are the Potṛ, O possessor of all boons, the wise one; perform the sacrifice and bring us what is desirable.
The god who bestows wealth desires from you a full ladle;
pour it out or fill it up, for then the god takes heed of you.
O Agni, lord of booty consisting of cattle, young son of strength!
O Jātavedas, bestow upon us great renown.
Blazing here as the benevolent sage, Agni is to be praised with song;
O you of many faces, shine richly upon us.
O King Agni, by yourself, at night and also at the break of dawn,
O you with sharpened fangs, burn against the Rākṣasas.
O Agni, may we today accomplish that [hymn] for you with our praises— like a horse, like an auspicious resolve that touches the heart—
with our offerings.
For indeed, O Agni, you have become the charioteer of auspicious will, of effective and righteous power, and of the lofty cosmic order.
Praising you today with these songs, O Agni, may we serve you; let us offer to you like the thunders of heaven with your mighty powers.
I honor Agni as the Hotṛ-priest, the bountiful, the Vasu, the Son of Strength, Jātavedas—the wise one, like a sage, the Knower of Beings.
He who, performing the sacrifice well, with his upward-turned, god-ward form,
follows the radiant glow of clarified butter, he of the bright luster.
Of the clarified butter being offered.
The swan dwelling in the pure realm; toward that god Savitar; O Agni, you are our closest one.
For thus, O Agni; for thus, O Agni.
Come hither, for we have pressed it well; O Indra, drink this Soma! Sit here upon this sacred grass of mine.
O Indra, may your two long-maned bay horses, yoked by prayer, bring you hither;
listen to our sacred invocations.
O Indra, we Brahmans, possessing Soma and having pressed it, invoke you as our ally, you who drink the Soma.
We cry out to you, O Hero, like unmilked cows;
to you, the lord of this moving world, the beholder of heaven, the lord, O Indra, of all that stands still.
No other like you exists—none from heaven, none from earth; none has been born, nor shall ever be born.
Desiring horses, O Maghavan Indra, and desiring cattle, we, the seekers of strength, invoke you.
For we poets indeed invoke you for the winning of booty;
O Indra, lords of the brave, men invoke you in battles against the Vṛtras, and you in the races of the steed.
As such, O wonderful one, wielder of the thunderbolt, being boldly praised by us, O lord of the pressing-stones,
pour forth for us cattle and chariot-horses, O Indra, like the total prize for a victor.
With what aid has he become manifold for us, the friend who ever prospers? With what most powerful company?
Which true one among the exhilarations, most bountiful, shall intoxicate you with the soma-juice, so that you may break open even the firmest wealth?
Be truly our protector, O friend of us who sing your praises; may you be with us with a hundred aids.
At every sacrifice, with song after song, for the sake of skill toward your Agni—
we, the mortals, shall praise the immortal Jātavedas more and more, like a beloved friend.
To the Son of Strength—him indeed we shall serve with devotion, seeking his favor, for the giving of oblations;
may he be our helper in battles, may he be our increaser, and may he be the protector of our bodies.

The wife of the seasons, she has arrived first; the leader of days and the mother of creatures. Being one, you shine forth in many ways through the dawns; you are undecaying, so cause all else to decay.
Who knows the paired nature of Virāj? Who knows her seasons, and who indeed knows her form?
Who knows her milkings, how many times she is milked, how many are her abodes, and how many are her manifestations?
This is indeed she who shone forth first; she moves within the waters, having entered them. The bride has lowed, the mother of the nine. Three greatnesses attend her.
The two Dawns, full of desire, beautifully adorned, move together toward their common womb;
they wander about as wives of Sūrya, wise, radiant, undecaying, and rich in seed.
Three have followed the path of *ṛta*; three heats have come along with the seed.
One quickens progeny, one nourishment, and one protects the sovereignty of those who seek the gods.
The fourth [verse], which established the Catuṣṭoma and became the wings of the sacrifice for the seers,
brought this light from heaven while yoking the Gāyatrī, Triṣṭubh, Jagatī, Virāj, and the Arka.
The Ordainer, by means of five, has established this; he produced for them five times five tones.
Of these, five go forth in succession, assuming various forms and various intentions.
At the first dawning of the abode of Cosmic Order (*ṛta*), one [of these dawns] bears the majesty of the waters;
one performs the appointed tasks of the sun; one belongs to the heat (*gharma*); and Savitṛ governs the other.

Thinking this to be for my own welfare, I have come to you as a gracious friend. We share a common birth; our creative power (*kratu*) is one and the same. May every one of us move about, fully aware of all things.
May we abide in your benevolent thought, O All-Knowing One; you have established yourself, for you have found a firm footing.
Speaking the truth, we have attained greatness; do not cast me away beyond another of your powers.
Arranging her radiant forms, knowing the path well, Dawn has come from the east;
bringing the enemies of the gods, the haters of prayer, into darkness, she, the possessor of all boons, has shone forth.
Following the five dawns are the five milkings; following the cow with five names are the five seasons.
The five directions are fashioned by the fifteenfold hymn; they share one common summit toward the single world.
Thirty sisters go toward the appointed place, putting on a common luster;
the wise ones, knowing the seasons, extend them and move resplendent in the midst of the sacred meter.
The goddess Night, full of light, releases the sky and the ordinances of the Sun;
the animals being born, of various forms, gaze about within her, their mother’s lap.
The first day indeed dawned; she became a milch-cow for Yama.
May she, rich in milk, yield for us [milk] through each succeeding year.
Questioned in heaven, questioned on earth, Agni has entered all plants;
Vaiśvānara Agni, questioned with power, may he protect us from harm by day and by night.
O youngest one, protect the men who offer oblations; hear our songs;
and guard our offspring with your own self.
O Agni Jātavedas, O divine one, self-sustained lord of immortality, [I know] your abodes and your names;
and all the many powers of the masters of illusion, O all-pervading one whose kinship is sought, you have concentrated within yourself.
Yava, Ayava, Ūma, Eva, Abda, Sagara, Sumeka—O Agni Kahya, O Agni Kiṃśila, O Agni Dudhra, O Agni Vanya, O Agni Kakṣya!
That which is thy arrow, named Yuvā—by that let us worship thee. To it be homage! May we, through its protection, remain alive. Whomever we hate and whoever hates us, him we place within its jaws.
The fire that is within the waters, that which is in Vṛtra, that which is in man, that which is in stone;
that which has entered the plants and the trees—to all those fires, let this offering be made.
That which is within the Soma, that which is within the cows, that which has entered the plants, that which has entered the wild beasts,
that which has entered bipeds and quadrupeds— may this offering be for those fires.
May this oblation be offered to those Agnis: who joined Indra’s chariot, who is Vaiśvānara and the giver of all things, who is wise, powerful, all-encompassing, and invincible.
To Agni, the all-eating, whom they call the one who fulfills desire, whom they call the giver and the receiver;
to him whom I invoke as the conqueror in battles—to those Agnis, let this oblation be offered.
To Agni, the ordainer, whose food is the bull and the cow, who bears Soma upon his back, let us do honor with hymns of praise.
May this be offered to those fires, of whom Agni Vaiśvānara is the eldest.
The Gāyatrī metre; the Earth; Agni the deity—with this metre, with this sacred formulation, with this deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.

The *pramā* metre—its world is the intermediate space, its deity Vāyu; the *pratimā* metre—its world is the sky, its deity Sūrya; the *asrīvī* metre—its world is the quarters, its deity Soma; the *gāyatrī* metre—its world is the goat, its deity Bṛhaspati; the *triṣṭubh* metre—its world is gold, its deity Indra; the *jagatī* metre—its world is the cow, its deity Prajāpati; the *anuṣṭubh* metre...

That is life; Mitra is the deity, the *uṣṇih* is the meter; that is sight; Pūṣan is the deity, the *virāj* is the meter; that is the horse; Varuṇa is the deity, the *bṛhatī* is the meter; that is agriculture; Parjanya is the deity, the *paṅkti* is the meter; that is man; Parameṣṭhin is the deity—with that meter, with that sacred formulation (*brahman*), with that deity—sit firm in the manner of Aṅgiras!
You are the earth by birth, a cow; you have conceived Agni as your embryo—unite with me! You are the intermediate space by birth, a cow;

you have conceived Vāyu as your embryo—unite with me! You are the sky by birth, a cow; you have conceived Āditya as your embryo—unite with me! You are the stars by birth, a cow; you have conceived the moon as your embryo...

You have conceived; come together with me! You are the *ṛc* by birth, a cow; you have conceived the *sāman* as your embryo—come together with me! You are the people (*viś*) by birth, a cow; you have conceived the king as your embryo—come together with me! You are speech (*vāc*) by birth, a cow;
you have conceived the breath (*prāṇa*) as your embryo—come together with me! You are the waters (*āpas*) by birth, a cow; you have conceived the sacrifice (*yajña*)...
You have conceived a fetus; come into being with me.

O Goddess, O Brick, you who are a maiden, fond of reclining—recline here with me, ever like a wife beside her husband. O Goddess, O Brick, you who are a young woman, fond of reclining—recline here with me, ever like a wife beside her husband. O Goddess, O Brick, you who are a youthful maiden, fond of reclining—recline here with me, ever like a wife beside her husband. O Goddess, O Brick, you who are the giver of life, the giver of out-breath, the giver of in-breath, and the giver of diffused breath.
Giver of sight, giver of hearing, you who rest upon the earth, the intermediate space, and the back of heaven— do you lie down near me, as a wife ever lies beside her husband.
O divine bricks, you who are most firm, most gracious, and restful— do you lie down near me, as wives ever lie beside their husband.

Thee for equal age, thee for superior age, thee for upward age, thee for great age, thee for the more powerful, thee for the overcoming, thee for the victorious, thee for the mighty, thee for the subduing,
thee for the overcomer, thee for the slayer of the adversary.
You are the maker of abundance; you are the maker of wide space; you are the eastern quarter; you are the upward direction; you are the intermediate region. I set you, the giver of vigor, in vigor;

I set you, the giver of milk, in milk; I set you, the giver of splendor, in splendor; I set you, the giver of glory, in glory; I set you, the giver of luster, in luster; I set you in the wealth of the earth; I set you in the wealth of the intermediate region.
I set you down in the wealth of heaven; I set you down in the wealth of the quarters; I set you down in the wealth of Draviṇodas.
You sit in the waters; you sit on the vulture; you sit on the falcon; you sit on the eagle; you sit on the vault of heaven.
I settle thee, the luminous; I settle thee, the light-maker; I settle thee, the knower of light; I settle thee, whose light is upward-turned;
I settle thee, whose light is vast; I settle thee, whose light is all-pervading; I settle thee, the unceasing;
I settle thee, the radiant; I settle thee, the shining; I settle thee, the gleaming; I settle thee, the blazing.
I set you down, you who are shimmering; I set you down, you who are wakeful; I set you down, you who are awakening.

The Kṛttikās are the lunar mansion; Agni is the deity. You are the splendors of Agni, of Prajāpati, of Soma, and of Dhātṛ. For the Ṛc you, for splendor you, for light you, for luminosity you—with that meter, with that sacred formulation (brahman), with that deity—sit firm like Aṅgiras!
Rohiṇī is the lunar mansion; Prajāpati is the deity. Anurādhā is the lunar mansion; the Maruts are the deity. Bāhu is the lunar mansion.

Rudra is the deity, Punarvasu the lunar mansion; Aditi is the deity, Tiṣya the lunar mansion; Bṛhaspati is the deity, Āśleṣā the lunar mansion; the Serpents are the deity, Maghā the lunar mansion; the Fathers are the deity, Phalgunīs the lunar mansion; Bhaga is the deity, Phalgunīs the lunar mansion; Aryaman is the deity, Hasta the lunar mansion; Savitṛ is the deity, Citrā the lunar mansion; Tvaṣṭṛ [is the deity].
The deity of the Niṣṭyā constellation is Vāyu; the deity of the Viśākhā constellation is Indra and Agni;

the deity of the Anūrādhā constellation is Mitra; the deity of the Jyeṣṭhā constellation is Varuṇa; the deity of the Mūla constellation is Nirṛti; the deity of the first Āṣāḍhā constellation is the Waters; the deity of the second Āṣāḍhā constellation is the Viśvedevas; the deity of the Abhijit constellation is Brahmā.
The constellation Śroṇā has Viṣṇu as its deity; the constellation Śraviṣṭhā has the Vasus as its deity; the constellation Śatabhiṣaj has Indra as its deity;
the constellation Proṣṭhapadā has Ahibudhnya as its deity;
the constellation Proṣṭhapadā has Aja Ekapād as its deity; the constellation Revatī has Pūṣan as its deity; the constellation Aśvayuj has the Aśvins as its deity; [and] the Bharaṇīs.
The asterism is Yama, its deity; the Brāhmaṇa is the asterism, Soma its deity. You are the splendors of Agni, of Prajāpati, of Soma, and of Dhātṛ.
For the Ṛc you, for splendor you, for radiance you, for light you! With that metre, with that sacred formulation (brahman), with that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras.
Śatabhiṣaj:
You are Śatabhiṣaj, named Samīcī; you are the eastern quarter. Of you, Agni is the overlord, Asita is the protector, and whoever is your overlord—him we invoke.

And he who is the protector of those two—to them be homage! May they be gracious to us; him whom we hate and him who hates us, we place within the jaws of these two. You are the name Ojasvatī; you are the southern quarter. Of that [quarter], Indra is the overlord, and Tiraścīnarājī is the protector.
And he who is your overlord and he who is the protector—to them be homage! May they be gracious to us; him whom...
We hate him who hates us; we place him within the jaws of these two. You are named Prācī, the western direction;
Soma is its overlord, Svaja its protector. To him who is your overlord and him who is your protector, let there be homage!
May they both be gracious to us. We hate him who hates us; we place him within the jaws of these two. You are named Suṣadā.

The northern direction; of it Varuṇa is your overlord, Sṛdākū is your protector. To him who is your overlord and him who is your protector—homage be to them! May they two be gracious to us. Whom we hate and whoever hates us, him we place within the jaws of these two. Your name is "The Support"; the downward direction is yours; Viṣṇu is your overlord, Kalmāṣagrīva is your protector. Whoever... [the text continues].

And he who is your overlord and he who is your protector—to them be homage! May they two be gracious to us; him whom we hate and him who hates us, we place within the jaws of these two. You are the Overlady by name, the upward direction; Bṛhaspati is your overlord, Citra is your protector. And he who is your overlord and he who is your protector—to them be homage! Do not be gracious toward him whom we hate and who hates us; we place both of them within the jaws of this [weapon].
Creating for himself an easy path that does not falter, the sharp-horned bull, blazing brightly,
looking back toward his ancient dwelling place, Agni has stretched out the celestial thread.
O Agni, you are the thread and the bridge; you are the path that leads to the gods.
By you, O Agni, may we ascend to the high ridge, where we may rejoice in communal revelry with the gods.
As they granted permission to the man, looking upward along the path,
the Maruts took pleasure in this sacrifice— immortal, finding the light of heaven, and causing the sky to rain.
Revolving in the midst of the world, creating and generating beings of diverse forms—
may Saṃvatsara, the Parameṣṭhin whose vows are firm, protect our sacrifice from the highest realm.
May the year grant us progeny; may Dhātṛ, being well-disposed, bestow it upon us.
May many [beings], together, manifold, and of all forms, yet united by a single vow, enter into me.
In the beginning, Hiraṇyagarbha arose; once born, he was the sole lord of all that exists.
He supported this earth and yonder heaven. To what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
He who is the King of all that breathes and blinks, the Lord of the entire world;
he who rules over its bipeds and quadrupeds—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
To him who bestows vigor and bestows strength, whose command all the gods revere;
he whose shadow is immortality and whose shadow is death—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
He whose greatness these mountains proclaim, and whose [greatness] they say is the ocean along with the Rasā;
he to whom belong the five divine quarters and intermediate directions—to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?

By whom the formidable heaven and the firm earth were made steadfast, by whom the sun was supported and the firmament, by whom the vast intermediate space was measured out— to what god shall we offer worship with our oblation?
He who propped up these two, heaven and earth, and sustained the two trembling worlds;
he upon whom the sun moves outspread—what god shall we worship with our oblation?
When the great waters came forth, containing the universal germ and generating Agni.
Then the life-force of the gods departed: "To which god shall we offer worship with our oblation?"
May Prajāpati generate offspring for us; may Dhātṛ, being well-disposed, bestow it upon us.
May the Year, in harmony with the seasons, and may the Lord of Prosperity, bestow prosperity upon me.

[Page III,1] First he cleanses the *juhū* ladle. The *juhū* is indeed the mouth of the sacrifice; thus he seizes the sacrifice from the very mouth. By means of the *juhū*, the gods summoned the *virāj*; that is why the *juhū* is called the *juhū*. The *virāj* is food, and the *juhū* is food; Agni is the *arka*.

That which he offers with the *juhū* ladle is for the attainment of food and splendor. He takes eight portions in the *juhū*; the *gāyatrī* consists of eight syllables, and the *gāyatrī* is the mouth of the sacrifice; thus he seizes the very mouth of the sacrifice. When the *sāvitra* oblations are offered, it is for instigation; furthermore, it is for the sake of providing various powers to the *yajus* formulas. Indeed, wherever Agni went, Savitṛ beheld him; that...

The *sāvitrāṇi* oblations are offered; [this is] for the sake of following after Agni. With the words, "Having perceived the light of Agni, he has brought it from the earth," Savitṛ indeed first gathered that light from the earth; therefore he speaks thus. He offers with verses that are both "yoked" (*yuktimat*) and "possessing mind" (*manasvatī*), for with a yoked mind the sacrifice is performed. There are six *ṛgmāṇi* verses; there are six seasons; [it is] in the seasons...

Thus he establishes himself. Indeed, he who approaches another deity before the one belonging to Agni departs from the mouth of the sacrifice. If there were no verses addressed to Savitṛ, he would depart from the impulse of Savitṛ. There are eight of these formulas; the Gāyatrī has eight syllables, and the Gāyatrī is the mouth of the sacrifice. Thus he does not depart from the mouth of the sacrifice. And because they are addressed to Savitṛ, he does not depart from the impulse of Savitṛ.
He does not do so; he offers with the *chandases*. Indeed, by means of the *chandases* he causes this offering to be brought to Agni; many offerings are made for him.

The *ṛc* is closer to the sacrifice, while the *yajus* is closer to the sacrificer.
