the sage has been magnified by the inspired singer.
O Soma, we who are skilled in speech magnify you with our songs; as one who is most gracious, enter into us.
O Agni, you grant glory accompanied by heroic sons; and Savitṛ, the god, Bhaga,
and Diti bestow desirable wealth.
You are our lord, for you bestow wealth; like one who traverses all, you dwell there with wondrous luster.
O Agni, like Mitra, you are the guardian of the great *ṛta* and the dispenser of abundant beauty, O God.
O Agni, you have shone forth.
O Agni, carry these most desirable oblations to the assembly of the gods;
may they accept our fragrant offerings.
O Agni, you purify our lives; Agni is the seer.
For him indeed, the two reciters praise with the ladle dripping with ghee— the god Agni, so that he may carry their oblations.
With invocations, they ever call upon Agni, Agni, the lord of the people,
the bearer of oblations, the one beloved by many.
O Agni, purifier, with your radiance; O purifying, shining one; Agni, whose vows are most pure; O Agni, yours are the pure [flames].
That immortal bearer of oblations, the eager messenger, well-disposed,
Agni brings all things together through our prayer.
Awaken Agni with a hymn, enkindling the immortal one,
so that he may place our oblations among the gods.
What was there in you, O Viṣṇu, that should have been hidden, that you proclaimed, "I am Śipiviṣṭa"?
Do not conceal this form from us, since you appeared in another form in the encounter.
Today, O Śipiviṣṭa, I, an Ārya who knows the sacred ways, proclaim that name of yours.
I, the weak, praise you, the powerful one, who dwells beyond this world-space.
May we ascend for our well-being the protector Earth and the faultless Heaven, Aditi who provides excellent shelter and wise guidance—
the divine ship with good oars, sinless and leakless.

Let us invoke for our protection the Earth, the mother of those who observe sacred vows, the consort of Ṛta— Aditi, the possessor of mighty dominion, the ageless, the far-reaching, the provider of excellent shelter and wise guidance.
O Agni and Soma, you who possess common wealth and are invoked together, accept our songs; you have both become present among the gods.
O Agni and Soma, you two of one mind have placed these luminous realms in heaven;
O Agni and Soma, you released the rivers from reproach and from being seized.
O Agni, come hither for the feast, being praised for the giving of oblations; sit down as the Hotṛ-priest upon the sacred grass.
We choose Agni as our messenger, the invoker, the all-knowing, the one of excellent wisdom for this sacrifice.
By fire is fire kindled— the sage, the master of the house, the youth, the bearer of oblations, whose mouth is the sacrificial ladle.
May Agni strike down the Vṛtras; awaken Agni with a hymn of praise; through Agni you purify our lives; O Agni, [protect] him today; with these [hymns], today [we approach] thee.
Through these our hymns, O Agni, turn toward us as you did toward the light of heaven; be well-disposed toward us with all your faces.
O Agni,
for you are indeed the light of gold.
Desirous of wealth, we meditate today upon the effective hymn of praise for Agni, the god who touches the heavens.
That mortal who, through his prayers and meditations, has taken pleasure in the service of Agni—
may he, being foremost, now enjoy and choose nourishment for our protection.
O Agni, you are far-extending, the beloved and excellent invoker;
through you they spread out the sacrifice.
O Soma, you are a bull, full of splendor; O God, you are a bull whose laws are bull-like; as a bull, you uphold the sacred ordinances.
Agni, once born, shone forth, slaying the Dasyus and dispelling darkness with his light; he found the cattle, the waters, and the sun.
Vast in the forefront.
*agre*: FN emended. Ed: *agne*. Cf. 2.7.8:85.14:
"O Varuṇa, hear this my invocation; be gracious to me today! Seeking your protection, I call upon you."
Hear that; I approach you with Agni, as Agni [approaches] Agni.
For you, O Agni, are kindled by fire; as a sage by a sage, as one who exists by one who exists, as a friend by a friend.

Let that mortal be foremost, O Mitra, who offers you refreshments, O Āditya, and serves you according to your law. He whom you protect is neither slain nor conquered; no distress reaches him, neither from near nor from afar.
Free from disease, rejoicing in our invocation, with measured steps upon the wide expanse of the earth,
and abiding by the ordinance of Āditya, may we remain in the benevolent favor of Mitra.
anāmīvāsāḥ: FN emended. Ed:
anamīmāsā. cf. 4.12.6:197.8 [Page IV,147]

That is the godhead of Sūrya, that is his greatness: in the midst of his work, he withdraws what was spread out. When he has unyoked his bay horses from their station, then Night spreads her garment over all.
He has harnessed the auspicious horses of the Sun— the bay, the dappled, the swift, and the ones worthy of praise.
Paying homage, they have ascended to the back of heaven; in an instant, they traverse heaven and earth.
O Agni, you are the guardian of vows.
O gods, whatever vows of yours we, being more ignorant than the wise, have violated—
may Agni, the knower, satisfy all that through those divine seasons by which he ordains the godhead.
O Agni, lead us.
We have come to the path of the gods, that we may carry out what we are able to do.
Agni, the wise one, shall sacrifice; he is the Hotṛ priest; he shall arrange the rites and the seasons.
Agni, whose vows are most pure; O Agni, you are bright; Agni has roared; Agni [is joined] with Night and Dawn.
Come hither, O Agni; be born through your ascetic heat and with your purifying flame;
come to this my excellent hymn of praise.
Come to us with fervor, O Agni, being born as the purifier, shining brightly;
place our oblations among the gods.
O divine Savitṛ, sovereign lord of all desirable things, O ever-bounteous one, we seek a portion from thee.
May the great heaven and earth protect us; O Agni, you [were born] from the lotus-leaf. You, indeed, was the seer Dadhyañc; you, indeed, was Pāthya Vṛṣan.
And let the people say: "Agni has been born as the slayer of Vṛtra, the winner of wealth in every battle."
They bear him in their hands like a child just born, like one holding a weapon; they bear Agni, who performs the sacrifice well for the people.
Bring forth the god, the best finder of wealth, for the feast of the gods;
let him sit down in his own place.
Sharpen this beloved guest, born from that which is born, in Jātavedas; [sharpen] the master of the house in his pleasant abode.
For you, O Agni, are fire by means of fire, indeed through fire.
They groom him, the one of excellent wisdom, the leader in battles,
the prize-winner in his own dwellings.
With sacrifice the gods sacrificed to the sacrifice; those were the first ordinances.
They reached the heights of heaven, the mighty ones, where the ancient Sādhyas, the gods, abide.

May the fuel-sticks (*samidhaḥ*) enjoy the clarified butter in Agni; may Tanūnapāt enjoy the clarified butter in Agni; may the *iḍas* enjoy the clarified butter in Agni; may the sacrificial grass (*barhiḥ*) enjoy the clarified butter in Agni; may the doors (*duraḥ*) enjoy the clarified butter in Agni; may Dawn and Night (*uṣāsānaktā*) enjoy the clarified butter in Agni; may the two divine Hotṛ-priests enjoy the clarified butter in Agni; may the three goddesses enjoy the clarified butter in Agni. *Svāhā* to Agni! *Svāhā* to Soma! *Svāhā* to Agni! *Svāhā* to Agni!
From the office of the Hotṛ, Svāhā! May the gods who drink the clarified butter, being pleased, partake of the clarified butter in Agni.
O Agni, whatever sacrifice or rite you encompass on every side,
that indeed goes to the gods.
O Soma, you are for us on every side; Agni is the head of the world and of the sacrifice.
O Soma, with those bliss-bestowing aids of yours that exist for the donor,
with those be our protector.

Those abodes of yours which are in heaven, those on earth, those on the mountains, in the plants, and in the waters— with all of them, being well-disposed and free from anger, O Soma, as our sovereign, accept our offerings.
We meditate upon that most excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ;
may he impel our thoughts.
Whatever we have done thoughtlessly toward the divine folk with feeble skill, through our own human nature and arrogance—
O Savitṛ, among both gods and men, do you here impel us to be sinless.
May Sarasvatī, the purifier, come to us from heaven.
May Pūṣan follow after our cows; may Pūṣan protect our horses;
may Pūṣan win us booty.
One of your forms is bright, the other is worthy of sacrifice; like the sky, you possess two days of different forms.
For you, O self-dependent one, protect all wondrous powers; O Pūṣan, may your bounty here be auspicious.
O Maruts, you who are self-strong, poets with sun-like skins, I choose this sacrifice for you here.
Bring forth a brilliant hymn for the swift Marut host, who possess their own inherent power, for they who by force overcome all forces; O Agni, the earth trembles before these mighty ones.
May all the gods, who increase the cosmic order and hear our invocation according to the seasons,
enjoy the appropriate milk.
May all the gods, who are unfailing, possessed of wondrous powers, and free from malice— their bearers— enjoy the sacrifice.
May Heaven and Earth today present this successful sacrifice, which touches the sky, among the gods.
With newest songs, bring hither the two ancient parents to the seat of the Eternal Order.
O Heaven and Earth, come to us with the divine host; great is your protective shelter.
He, the bearer of oblations, [worships] Agni with a hymn of praise.
May the divine *barhis* (sacrificial grass) partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining wealth; may the divine doors partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining wealth;

may the two goddesses Dawn and Night partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining wealth; may the two goddesses who delight [the gods] partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining wealth;

may the two goddesses, the offerings of strength, partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining wealth; may the two divine *hotṛ*s partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of obtaining wealth.
May the three goddesses depart; may the three goddesses partake of the gift of wealth, of the bestowal of riches. May the god Narāśaṃsa partake of the gift of wealth, of the bestowal of riches.

May the god Agni Sviṣṭakṛt—the giver of good wealth, the delightful sage, whose thoughts are true, the sacrificing priest—partake. He who is more skilled at sacrifice than the priest of every priest, O Agni: those gods whom you have sacrificed for, whom you have impelled, those who have rejoiced in your office as Hotṛ—to them, having been satisfied, [give the oblation].

May we send this sacrifice, which goes to the gods, to the gods in heaven; and you, O Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, having become the Hotṛ, accept the invocation for the sake of wealth and the bestowal of riches in the utterance of homage.
In every contest for booty, may they be auspicious to us.
Bring forth the god Jātavedas with divine thought;
may he carry our oblations to him in due order.
This very one, seeking the gods, is led forth as the Hotṛ for the sacrifice; like a well-guarded chariot, he, glowing with heat, takes heed by his own power.
This Agni protects us as if from an immortal birth;
the god, more powerful than power itself, has been made for the sake of life.
We [place] you in the footprint of Iḍā.
O Agni, of beautiful countenance, together with all the gods, sit first upon the wool-lined seat;
lead the sacrifice, which is nest-like and rich in ghee, successfully for Savitṛ and for the sacrificer.
Sit down, O Hotṛ; settle as the Hotṛ.
You are our messenger; you are our protector from afar; you, O Bull, are the leader to greater wealth. O Agni, for the extension of our offspring and our bodies, be a watchful, shining guardian.
Through Agni may one obtain wealth and nourishment day by day—
glorious and most rich in heroic sons.
Increasing our cattle, driving away disease, finding wealth, and increasing prosperity— O Soma, be a good friend to us.
O Indra and Agni, you adorn the luminous realms of heaven for the sake of spoils;
that heroic deed of yours is well known.
You two surpass all people in the calls to battle; you exceed both the earth and the heavens in greatness;
you surpass the rivers and the mountains in majesty; O Indra and Agni, you transcend all other beings.
O Maruts, since we call upon you from heaven seeking your favor, come hither to us quickly!
The protections which you have for the one who exerts himself, grant those threefold gifts to the donor.
Extend them to us, O Maruts; bestow upon us wealth with heroic sons, O bulls.
This [hymn] for me, O Varuṇa; that I entreat of you; by what [means], O Agni, will you satisfy the gods for us today? Since today, O Agni, your seat is in the waters.
Soma has told me that within the waters are all healing remedies, and the waters are the source of all well-being.
O Varuṇa, loosen the highest bond from us.
O Varuṇa, we appease your wrath with prostrations; we seek your favor through sacrifices and oblations.
O wise Asura, O King, as you dwell among us, loosen the bonds of the sins we have committed.

O Agni, you who know, may you ward off from us the wrath of the god Varuṇa; as the best of sacrificers, the most excellent bearer of oblations, and the radiant one, release from us all those who hate us.
As such, O Agni, be our protector; be our nearest helper at the dawning of this morning.
Being gracious, release us from Varuṇa; come to our mercy, and be easy for us to invoke.
May Agni strike down the Vṛtras; you, O Soma, are the lord of the virtuous.
O Agni, with all your hosts and all your aids, crush our hatred; bestow upon us wealth worthy of sacrifice.
With a well-disposed host, may he be gracious toward us—the sacrificer who best attains the gods with auspiciousness;
as our undeceived guardian and protector from afar, O Agni, shine forth with splendor and wealth.
Satisfy the gods; [bring] the gods [hither].
O Maruts, you who consume the enemy, may you graciously accept this oblation of the Sāṃtapanas; [we call upon] you with our prayers.
O Maruts, O Vasus, whoever, being ill-disposed toward us, seeks to strike at our thoughts with malice—may he be caught in the snares of deceit;
slay him with your most scorching blow!
O Agni, with an ancient hymn and with songs, we [worship] you, O Soma, [driving away] malice.
O Maruts, you who dwell in the home, come hither; do not stay away from us.
Enjoy these oblations.
Your great splendors from the depths arise; O most worshipful ones, extend your names.
O Maruts, take pleasure in this thousandfold domestic portion, this offering belonging to the householder.
O Agni, this [oblation] is offered; O Agni, it is kindled.
I praise Agni, the domestic priest, the god of sacrifice, the officiating priest, the invoker,
the bestower of the most excellent treasures.
O Soma, you are a bull, full of splendor.
Sing forth, O Kaṇvas, to your sporting host of Maruts— the unassailable, the chariot-glittering.

The Maruts, who are like swift chargers, moving with their own will, have adorned themselves like youths visible to the seer; established in their mansions, they are bright as children, playing like calves, and bestowing milk.
For all people constantly [worship] that very Agni, Agni.
O Indra and Agni, you two shook down ninety forts belonging to the Dāsas,
together with a single deed.
He shall pierce Vṛtra and win booty—Indra and Agni, the two conquerors, whom one shall worship;
they who rule over abundant wealth, most victorious through their power, striving for strength.
We incite that Indra to win the prize.
I harness the chariot that seeks cattle with the two bay horses; my prayers have reached him who delights in them.
Indra, by his greatness, has forced asunder the two worlds, having struck down the Vṛtras without opposition.
The seeker of cattle;
O Viśvakarman, Lord of Speech!
Desiring you, we invoke you.
O Agni, through your gracious favor, bestow upon us wealth that nourishes all life and grant us compassion so that we may live.
O Soma, you bestow great fortune; you grant skill for living to the youth who follows the eternal law.
O Soma, you are distinguished by your wisdom; you lead us along the straightest path.
Under your guidance, O Indu, our wise ancestors obtained their share of treasure among the gods.
For our ancient fathers, O Soma, performed their rites for you, O Pavamāna, as wise men. Winning [booty] and unassailed, open wide the enclosures; be a bountiful patron to us with heroes and horses.
O Soma, in harmony with the Fathers, you have extended yourself across heaven and earth. To you, O Indu, we pay homage with this oblation; may we be masters of riches.
O Pitṛs who sit upon the sacrificial grass, come hither with your aid; we have prepared these oblations for you, so please accept them.
Having approached us with most auspicious protection, then bestow upon us well-being, health, and freedom from harm.
The Soma-loving ancestors have been invited to their dear treasures upon the sacrificial grass;
may they come, may they hear us here, may they speak for us, and may they protect us.

I have found the benevolent Fathers, and the descendant, and the wide stride of Viṣṇu. Those who sit upon the sacred grass and partake of the pressed juice with the funeral offering (svadhā)—may they be the most ready to come here.
Let this homage be paid today to the fathers— those who went before and those who followed after,
those who have settled in the earthly realm, or those who are now among the well-favored clans.

May the lower, the higher, and the middle ancestors, worthy of Soma, rise up—those who have gone to the life-breath, who are harmless and knowers of the Eternal Order; may those ancestors protect us in our invocations.
O Agniṣvātta Pitṛs, increasers of cosmic order, be gracious to us,
for the sake of long life and living.
We invoke the Agniṣvātta ancestors who follow the seasons and who, in the Narāśaṃsa rite, have attained the drinking of Soma.
May those wise ones, easy to invoke, be gracious to us; may they bring well-being to our bipeds and well-being to our quadrupeds.
O Agniṣvātta Pitṛs, come hither; sit each upon his own seat, O excellent leaders. Eat the oblations presented upon the sacred grass, and then bestow wealth consisting of all heroic sons.
Being born with power as of old, he has immediately assumed all poetic wisdom.
Both the waters and the *dhiṣaṇā* have accomplished their friendship; the gods maintained Agni, the giver of wealth.
By means of his ancient invocation and his wisdom, he generated these offspring of men;
with Vivasvat as his eye, the gods maintained Agni, the giver of wealth, [as the lord] of heaven and the waters.
Those who have thirsted among the gods, exerting themselves, knowing the invocations, fashioning hymns with their chants— O Agni,
come hither with those well-disposed, true, and wise ancestors who sit at the *gharma* vessel!
Toward Vāyu, the possessor of great wealth, the bestower of all boons, and the filler of chariots, let this lofty hymn proceed—
a sage seeking the sage, O most worshipful one, as he comes with his teams of horses whose paths are radiant.
With those teams by which you go toward the donor for our sacrifice in his home, O Vāyu—
bestow upon us wealth that provides excellent enjoyment, and grant us heroic sons and the gift of cattle and horses.
We invoke Indra Śunāsīra at this sacrifice;
may he carry us across our enemies.
Through days and nights, through half-months, through months, and through seasons, he encompassed the sacrifice.
Today we invoke Śunāsīra and Indra, the majesty of this year.
Seven bay horses carry you in your chariot, O divine Sūrya,
whose hair is flame, O beloved of many.
O Sūrya, you are the deliverer, visible to all, the maker of light; you illuminate the entire radiant realm.
O Indra and Agni, [you are] the luminous realms of heaven; for the sake of the people, O Indra and Agni, you shattered the ninety fortresses and struck down Vṛtra.
Welcomed as the domestic friend and guest in the dwelling, come to this our sacrifice, O wise one!
Having struck down all assailants, O Agni, bring hither the possessions of those who act as enemies.
O Agni, be strong for great good fortune; may your splendors be most excellent.
Secure for us a well-governed household lordship, and trample down the powers of those who act as enemies.
The singers who know the ways of praise sing forth hymns to you both; O Indra and Agni, I choose you for nourishment.
When the prize-seeking men, the inspired singers seeking favor with their prayers, have come to the assembly,
they cry out repeatedly to Indra and Agni like horses reaching the goal.
Agni bestows a lord of the virtuous, he who conquers in battle with his men;
Agni [bestows] a swift-gliding steed, a victor unconquered.
Agni bestows upon the worshipper a son who is most highly renowned, a supreme master of sacred prayer, invincible, and a lord who makes his name heard afar.
O Heroes, Indra and Agni, with those many-desired teams of horses that you possess for the donor, come hither!
O Indra and Agni, slayers of Vṛtra, may you today accept this pure, newly-born hymn of praise.
For I invoke both of you, who are easily summoned; you two are most swift to grant strength to the one who desires it.
May Pūṣan follow our cows; one of your [forms] is bright.
Through the Lord of the Field, as through a benefactor, may we conquer;
may he, who nourishes cattle and horses, be gracious to us for such a sight.
May the plants be full of sweetness; may the heavens and the waters be sweet for us; may the mid-air be sweet for us;
may the Lord of the Field be sweet for us, and may we follow him unharmed.
Together indeed.
O friends, bring together for you all— unitedly— refreshment and a hymn of praise for Agni,
the most exalted among the peoples, the son of strength, the mighty one.
May Vaiśvānara come to us with his aid, he who is enthroned in heaven.
We implore Vaiśvānara, the observer of cosmic order, the lord of the light of truth,
the imperishable heat.

O Vaiśvānara, I long for your abodes, by which you became the finder of heaven, O far-seeing one; as soon as you were born, you filled the worlds and the two realms, O Agni—you encompass all these by your own self.
O Agni, [bestow] the nourishment.
O Agni, being praised, make us a glorious singer for the winning of riches;
may we be able to perform our work with new vigor. O Heaven and Earth, together with the gods, protect us!
May we abide in the good favor of Vaiśvānara, for he is the king, the glory over all beings.
Born from here, he beholds this entire universe; Vaiśvānara strives in harmony with the Sun.
O Agni Vaiśvānara, maintain for us among our patrons a sovereign power that is undecaying and rich in heroes;
may we, through your protections, O Agni, win booty in hundreds and thousands.
Like the earth, he has encompassed the entire world with its abundance; he receives one thing after another as it approaches.
By the greatness of the mighty Vaiśvānara, I make my food pleasant and sweet.
Being born in the highest heaven, Agni, the guardian of vows, protected the sacred ordinances;
the wise Vaiśvānara measured out the mid-air and with his greatness touched the firmament.
Just as it was indeed then.
Three are your lifespans, O Jātavedas; three are your births from the dawns, O Agni.
As one who knows, worship the gods with these for their protection, and then become the source of well-being and fortune for the sacrificer.
Establish Agni Jātavedas, the bearer of the oblation, the youngest,
the divine officiating priest.
In the footprint of Iḍā, I have performed this praise for Dadhikrāvan.
Awakening Dadhikrāvan, Agni, Uṣas, and Sūrya,
and the ruddy steed of Varuṇa whom the wise perceive as brown— may they all drive away from us every misfortune.
Agni, the most excellent sacrificer, has sat down as the Hotṛ-priest in the fragrant lap of his mother, in her place;
he is the youthful seer, established in many places, the observer of Truth, the sustainer of the peoples, kindled in their midst.
He has made our divine feast auspicious today; we have found the secret tongue of the sacrifice.
He has come, fragrant and clothed in life; he has made our invocation of the gods auspicious today.
For whatever indeed is yours...
O Agni, great indeed is the danger from sin in the presence of both gods and mortals; may we, your friends, never suffer harm. Grant well-being and prosperity to our children and descendants.
May Heaven and Earth and the broad ground be favorable to us.
Rich in ghee, the glory of all beings, wide and broad, yielding honey, well-adorned—
Heaven and Earth, by the law of Varuṇa, are propped apart, ageless and full of abundant seed.
With broad hips, he is pressed close.
I praise with song Agni the wise, the accomplisher of the sacrifice, who is prompt to hear and who bestows what is intended.
O Agni, may we be able to control the strength of you, the god;
may we overcome all hostilities.
O Agni, son of strength, we who offer nourishment unite our songs with you, whose appearance is delightful.
We have come to you for shelter, as if to shade from the heat,
O Agni, you who are like gold in appearance.
May Agni strike down the Vṛtras; you, O Soma, are the lord of the virtuous; O Agni and Soma, you two are the source of these glories.
O Agni, you have made me the bearer of Soma, the powerful one, so that I may sacrifice in the assembly;
shining toward the god, I harness the pressing-stone. For the sake of well-being, O Agni, take pleasure in this body of mine.
O Soma and Pūṣan, begetters of riches, begetters of heaven, begetters of earth,
born as the guardians of the entire world, the gods have made you the navel of immortality.
These two gods, as they are born, have taken delight; may these two conceal the loathsome darknesses.
Within these raw cows, Indra brought forth the cooked [milk] for Soma and Pūṣan.
And so, O Brahman, most invoked by the gods among our oblations and hymns,
shine auspiciously for us, O Agni, strengthened by the Maruts, as the greatest winner of thousands.
Now bestow upon us, O Agni, wealth consisting of thousands, offspring, and nourishment— splendid, heroic, most excellent, and undecaying.
With you as his ally, O Soma, through that friendship of yours, Indra caused the waters to flow for mankind;
he slew the serpent, released the seven rivers, and opened the channels that were like closed doors.
May I be united with my friend of the soft belly, who, when drunk, shall not harm me, O Lord of the Tawny Horses.
This Soma which has been placed within us—for that sake, O Indra, I come to extend my life-span.
O Agni, you are ours; O Agni, you are ours; we invoke with our song the ancient Agni for you.
Swift is the chariot of the one who favors the gods, like a hero in any battles whatsoever;
he who, as a sacrificer, desires to win the minds of the gods, shall surely prevail over those who do not sacrifice.
No one can destroy him by action, nor can he be driven away;
nor does he remain estranged from those among the gods whose mind the sacrificer seeks to win over, for he prevails even over those who do not sacrifice.
In this [sacrifice] there is excellent heroic power and that very wealth of horses;
he who, as a sacrificer, strives to win the mind of the gods, shall indeed prevail over those who do not sacrifice.
The rivers flow forth as sources of bliss; like milch-cows, they serve both him who has sacrificed and him who is about to sacrifice.
Seeking renown, the streams of clarified butter approach from every side both the one who bestows gifts and the one who fulfills them.
O Soma and Rudra, bestow all these remedies upon our bodies;
grant us protection and release from whatever sin we have committed that remains bound within our persons.
O Soma and Rudra, maintain your divine power; may our offerings reach you sufficiently.
Bestowing the seven treasures in every house, be auspicious to us—be a blessing to our bipeds and a blessing to our quadrupeds.
O Soma and Rudra, tear apart in all directions the disease that has entered our home;
drive far away Destruction, and may auspicious glories attend us.
O Soma and Rudra, wielders of sharp weapons and sharp missiles, most gracious ones, be well-disposed toward us here;
release us from what has seized us in this encounter, and grant us, O Bulls, the most auspicious blessings.
O Agni and Viṣṇu, being of one accord, O Agni and Viṣṇu, your great abode is dear to you both.

O Agni and Viṣṇu, great indeed is that majesty of yours; you enjoy the secret portions of the clarified butter, increasing through fair praises in every house. Now let your tongue move toward the clarified butter.
May Sarasvatī be a purifier for us.
O Sarasvatī, lead us toward greater wealth; do not distance yourself from us, nor consume us with your heat.
Accept our friendship and our domestic presence; may we never depart from you to the desolate wilds.
From the sky, come to us.
O Bṛhaspati, you who belong to all the gods, graciously accept our oblations;
bestow jewels upon the donor.
Thus let us worship the Father, the bull of all the gods, with sacrifices, with homage, and with oblations. O Bṛhaspati, may we, possessing good offspring and heroic sons, be masters of riches.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, you of noble wisdom, sprinkle our pastures with clarified butter and the regions with honey.
Stretch forth your arms that we may live; sprinkle our pastures with clarified butter.
O youthful ones, make us famous among the people; hear these my invocations, O Mitra and Varuṇa.
I invoke the pure Agni, who dwells in the ocean, like Aurva-Bhṛgu and like Apnavāna.
I invoke Agni, who is clothed in the ocean, like the all-bestowing Savitṛ and like the enjoyment of Bhaga.
I have called upon Agni, who has the sound of wind, the sage, whose roar is like Parjanya, the victorious one, whose garment is the ocean.
O Soma, you are a bull, full of splendor.
Those who extend across the billowing ocean with their rays— come hither, O Agni, together with the Maruts.
May your water-bearing steeds come today, all you Maruts who impel the rain;
O wise and youthful ones, take pleasure in this fire which has been kindled for you, O Maruts.
O Agni, whom Devāpi, the son of Ṛṣṭiṣeṇa, the mortal man, has kindled while glowing with fervor—
being celebrated by all the gods, impel Parjanya, the bringer of rain.
O Agni, drive away the adversaries, drive away the difficult passages, and ward off disease and the Rākṣasas.
From this vast ocean of heaven, release for us here an abundance of waters.
I invoke by name the beloved ones of you swift Maruts, so that they may be satisfied as they yearn for us.
For the sake of glory, they have mingled with splendors; they have mingled with rays and with singers, they who are well-armed.
Armed with axes, impetuous, and fearless, they have found the beloved domain of the Marut host.
O Maruts, when [you come] from heaven...
At their onset, the earth trembles as if unsteady during their journeys when they harness themselves for glory;
those playful, roaring ones with glittering spears, the shakers, celebrate their own greatness.
By what [power] have the Maruts, of equal age and dwelling in the same nest, become united as one?
With what thought, from whence have they come? For what purpose do these bulls sing their strength, seeking wealth?
Whose sacred hymns have the youthful Maruts delighted? Who has turned them toward his sacrifice? Like falcons gliding through the atmosphere, by what great spirit may we cause them to pause?

From where do you come alone, O Indra, you who are so mighty, O Lord of the Good? What is it thus that you seek to ask, meeting with those who are radiant? Tell us that, O Lord of the Bay Horses, what you have for us.
The sacred hymns, my thoughts, and the pressed juices are auspicious for me; my strength stirs, and the pressing-stone is set in motion for me.
They look toward you and long for your praise; these two bay steeds carry you toward us.

Therefore, uniting with these our most excellent companions and adorning our bodies with our own powers, we now join together as one through our great splendors; for you, O Indra, have come to us according to our own nature.
Where was your self-power, O Maruts, when you left me alone in the slaying of Ahi?
For I, the fierce, the mighty, the powerful, bent down every enemy with my weapons.
You have performed many deeds with us as your allies, O Bull, through our common manly powers;
for we two, O most mighty Indra, shall accomplish many things together, whatever we may desire, O Maruts.
O Maruts, with my own power and through my own fury, having become mighty, I slew Vṛtra.
With the thunderbolt in my arm, I made these all-glittering waters easy to pass for Manu.
O Maghavan, there is none superior to you; indeed, no one among the gods is known to be your equal.
Neither one being born nor one already born can attain you. O Increaser, perform those deeds which you are yet to do!
May there be abundant power for me alone; whatever I, being bold, shall now accomplish through my inspired thought.
For I am formidable, O Maruts, knowing those things which I, Indra, alone rule over and cause to fall.

O Maruts, you have beautified this hymn here, which you, O heroes, have fashioned for me as a glorious prayer—unto Indra, the bull, the great sacrificer, for my sake; as friends, with your own bodies, for the sake of our common person.
Truly, these Maruts, shining toward me, possessing blameless glory, and appearing with their moon-like luster, have looked upon me; may you now find me pleasing and grant me delight.
Who among you here, O Maruts, has magnified you? Come forth toward your friends, O friends! May you, who inspire brilliant thoughts, be mindful of these my sacred rites.

Since the inspired wisdom of Mānya has brought us here for worship, as a singer brings [oblations] for the sake of service—O Maruts, turn hither to this sage; the singer has recited these prayers for you.

This is your hymn, O Maruts; this is the song of Māndārya, the son of Māna, the poet. May it bring offspring for our own bodies. May we find strengthening food and a community that bestows life-sustaining gifts.
We invoke Indra for you from all sides, away from other people;
may he belong exclusively to us.
O Bull, let your impetuous strength come from behind, from above, from below, and from the front;
let it gather around you from every side, directed hitherward. O Indra, bestow upon us the splendor that shines like the sun.
O Maruts, that which is yours from heaven, and those shelters of yours—
Come hither to us, O Indra, slayer of Vṛtra; come to our side, great one with your mighty aids.
O Indra, you are great; indeed, the earth and heaven have acknowledged your sovereign power with reverence.
Having slain Vṛtra with your might, you released the rivers that had been swallowed by the serpent.
O Maruts, whatever strength you possess, with it you have caused the people to tremble; you have caused the mountains to tremble.

Spears are upon your shoulders, O Maruts; enduring power is in your arms, and strength is placed within you. Manly courage is in your heads, weapons upon your chariots, and all your splendor is adorned upon your bodies.
For you are indeed the same in many places, the lord over all the tribes;
we invoke you in battles.
When the stakes are equal, we who seek strength invoke Agni for protection— him who bestows wonderful wealth in the contests for booty.
O Agni, lead us to the gods; O Agni, you are the guardian of vows for whatever we [have done] toward you.
O Agni, you who uphold the sacred vows, O pure Agni, bring the gods here to our sacrifice and our oblation.
Bearing vows now, the guardian of vows, undeceived, sacrificing, a god, ageless, and rich in heroes—
bestowing jewels, O Agni, be gracious; protect us for life, O Jātavedas!
O youngest Agni, descendant of Bharata, bring us the most excellent, radiant,
and much-desired wealth, O Vasu.

To you, O youngest Agni, the peoples bring tribute from near and from afar; take notice of the prayer of him who praises you best. Great is your greatness, O Agni; your protection is vast and auspicious.
O Agni, the inspired poets magnify you, the best winner of booty, who are well-praised;
as such, grant us heroic strength.
May this Agni with his hosts crush our enemies; with his host [crush] them. This [is] Viṣṇu; forth that [is] Viṣṇu.
Bring hither for your protection Agni, the king of the sacrifice, the Rudra, the Hotṛ-priest who sacrifices truly for both heaven and earth,
the one of golden form, before the unperceived thunderbolt strikes.
What, O Agni, will you say when you have grown strong upon the sacrificial hearths; what to the mighty Vāta who seeks splendor;
what to the Nāsatyas who travel around the earth as its protectors; and what, O Agni, to Rudra, the slayer of men?
To him whose food is bulls, whose food is cows.
Shaken by the wind and impelled according to its will, when you spread abroad through the three foods,
your undecaying hosts, O Agni, strive to burn as if they were separate chariot-horses.
"Kṛṇuṣva pājaḥ"—these five [verses].
He, the youngest one, knows your good intention, he who has prepared a path for such a prayer;
for him, the noble one, may he illuminate all auspicious days, riches, and splendors, opening wide the doors.

But let him, O Agni, be fortunate and a liberal giver who seeks to satisfy you with constant oblation and hymns throughout his own life in his home; for him, every sacrifice shall result in all days being auspicious.
I worship your benevolence; O Roarer, let it resound hitherward. May this song of mine be heard by you as a favorite.
With fine horses and excellent chariots, may we groom you; may you maintain our sovereign powers day after day.
May many a person here attend upon you of their own accord, O radiant one who shines through the nights day after day;
may we, joyful and playing, serve you, while we stand amidst the splendors of the people.
But he who approaches you, O Agni, with good horses and fine gold on a chariot laden with wealth—
of him you are the protector, of him the friend, provided he takes pleasure in offering hospitality to you in due order.

Through kinship and with my words, I break down the great [fortress]; that [song] has followed me from my father Gotama. O most youthful Hotṛ, wise one, master of the house, take heed of this our speech.
Born not from sleep, they are swift-crossing, most gracious, unwearied, non-wolfish, and most tireless. May those protectors, sitting together in unison, O Agni, guard us— O infallible one, yours!

Those reeds, O Agni, which saw and protected the blind son of Mamatā from distress—him, the doer of good deeds, the All-Knowing one has protected; the enemies who sought to harm him could not deceive him.
With you we are fortunate; protected by you, may we obtain spoils through your guidance.
Accomplish both our praises, O upholder of truth; act immediately, O one who is not to be shamed.
With this fuel, O Agni, may we worship you; accept the hymn being recited.
Burn the malicious ones and the Rākṣasas; protect us from the malevolent, from the reviler, and from blame, O you who are great as Mitra.
The immortal Agni, with his bright radiance, drives away the demons; he is pure, purifying, and worthy of praise.
O Soma, protect us from every side.
Yoke, indeed, those who are most invoked by the gods.
And so, O God, speak for us to the God as one who knows best;
grant us full confidence in all desirable things.
Since you, O youngest one, son of strength, when invoked with oblations,
have become the observer of cosmic order and worthy of sacrifice.
This fire [is the master] of thousands.
Bend toward this sacrifice, O Aṅgiras, with our joint invocations, as the Ṛbhus bend the felly of a wheel. Draw near!
O Virūpa, urge forth a well-fashioned hymn of praise for that bull-like one who shines toward heaven, with an eternal voice.
Which Paṇi indeed shall we strike down among the cattle with the missile of this Agni, whose eye looks away?
May the clans of the gods not abandon us, like cows that have bathed,
nor like milch-cows deserting a weakling.
May not the affliction of any malicious hater strike us down,
as a wave strikes a ship.
Homage to you, O Agni; the peoples sing praise to your power, O God; with your flames, crush the enemy.
Accepting this sacrifice and these words, come hither;
O Soma, be for our prosperity.
O Agni, will you not surely bestow wealth upon us for our song? O maker of wide space, make wide space for us!
Do not abandon us in this great contest for wealth, like one who drops his burden;
win the gathered prize, win the wealth!
Whose *śamī* wood the reverent ones have enjoyed, whether it be that of one who has performed the sacrifice or one who has not— it is toward him indeed that Agni hastens.
O Agni, let this misfortune, driven by fear, pursue someone other than us;
increase our impetuous strength.
This oblation is dear to you both in your mouth, O Indra and Bṛhaspati; the hymn and the exhilarating draught are being recited.
O Indra and Bṛhaspati, bestow upon us wealth consisting of hundreds,
abounding in horses, and never-failing.
Come here, O Agni; I shall truly proclaim these other songs to you, so that you may grow strong by means of these drops.
[The word] *gna* is emended; the edition reads *gne*.
[The verse continues: "This sacrifice, this speech."
We now implore those Ādityas for protection, the Kṣatriya, for their great compassion and for our assistance.
From whom the mother Aditi, of mountain-like strength, pours forth honeyed milk and nectar;
she who is strengthened by hymns, whose roar is like a bull’s, and who is full of sleep—may she rejoice in that Āditya for our well-being.
The Ādityas, supporting that which moves and that which stands, are gods and guardians of the entire world;
far-sighted, they protect their divine power, upholding the cosmic order and exacting debts.
They uphold the three divine luminous realms, golden, pure, and purified by their own radiance;
they are straightforward, blameless, undeceived, and far-famed for the sake of the upright mortal.
Those are the auspicious horses of the Sun; he is the Golden Embryo who [sustains] all that breathes.
Bṛhaspati, being born first from the great light in the highest heaven,
seven-mouthed and many-born, blew away the darkness with his roar, he who possesses seven rays.
When he won the prize of every form, and ascended to heaven and the higher dwellings—
strengthening Bṛhaspati, the bull, though being many and bearing the light of these [worlds].
We invoke Bṛhaspati together with his entire host from every side;
may he come to our sacrifice.
With his well-praising, chanting host, Bṛhaspati shattered Vala and the enclosure with a roar; crying out, he drove forth the lowing, milk-yielding cows.
O Brahmanaspati, be the controller of this hymn and prosper our offspring. All that which the gods favor is auspicious. May we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
O Lord of Prayer, may we ever be masters of chariots possessing wealth and vital strength at this pressing;
endow us with hero among our heroes, since you, being the sovereign, come to my invocation through the sacred word.
Arise, O Brahmanaspati! We, seeking the gods, call upon you. May the Maruts, the bounteous givers, come forward; O Indra, be swift with them.
Agni is the domestic priest at the hymn; the pressing-stones and the sacrificial grass are at the rite.
With a verse I seek the Maruts and Brahmaṇaspati, the god, for desirable protection.
Homage to you, O Rudra, to your wrath; these [oblations] for Rudra.
Who truly knows? Who here has declared it? Whence was it born, and whence came this creation?
The gods are later than this world's manifestation; then who indeed knows whence it first arose?
From whom this emission has come into being— whether he fashioned it or whether he did not—
he who is its overseer in the highest heaven, he indeed knows it, or perhaps even he does not know.
Vishnu strode across this [universe].
May I attain that beloved domain of his, where the god-seeking heroes rejoice;
for there, in the highest step of Viṣṇu, the wide-striding one, is the kinsman and the spring of honey.
All the gods, the increasers of cosmic order.
O All-Gods, hear this my invocation—ye who are in the mid-air and ye who dwell in heaven;
ye whose tongue is Agni, or who are worthy of sacrifice, sit upon this sacred grass and rejoice.
Indrāṇī has won the well-won prize with her husband; she is indeed named Senā (the Army), the Earth, the winner of wealth, the all-encompassing Aditi, and she whose skin is like the sun.
To that Indrāṇī, the victorious and overpowering one, let us do honor with this oblation.
Come near, O Lord of Speech, together with the divine mind;
O Lord of Wealth, withdraw my body into myself alone.
May the Lord of Speech today bestow upon me the strength of those who move in thrice-seven groups, bearing all forms.
May Agni, the first, protect us with the Vasus; may Soma guard us by his own self with the Rudras;
may Indra with the Maruts act according to the seasons, and may Varuṇa with the Ādityas grant us shelter.
May Agni protect us together with the Vasus; may Soma [protect us] together with his Rudra-like forms;
may Indra, to whom oblations are offered, [protect us] together with the Maruts; and may Varuṇa, the possessor of all wealth, [protect us] together with the Ādityas.
O Agni, grant wealth consisting of heroic sons and abundance to the donor; sharpen us so that we may be rich in offspring.
O Agni, give us hundreds, give us thousands! Open wide for us the doors of strength like those of fame.
Make Heaven and Earth favorable through our sacred prayer; let the Dawns flash forth the bright light of heaven.
I invoke Savitṛ, the golden-handed, for protection;
he, as the deity, knows the path.
O Savitṛ, grant us what is auspicious today, and what is auspicious tomorrow; day by day, grant us what is auspicious.
O God, through this prayer, may we become partakers of the lovely and abundant dwelling.
Praise Vāyu with those [hymns] by which...
O Earth, be pleasant, free from thorns, and a place of rest for us;
grant us wide-extending shelter.
Truly, O Earth, you bear the very weight of the mountains;
you who, possessing great slopes, impel the earth forward by your greatness, O Mighty One.
Moving back and forth by means of their creative power (*māyā*), these two children pass around the sacrifice while playing;
one of them beholds all beings, while the other, ordaining the seasons, is born again.
Ever new as he is born, the banner of the days goes forth at the head of the dawns;
arriving, he ordains the portion for the gods, and the moon extends long life.
Just as the suns cause the ray to swell, and just as the imperishable ones drink from the imperishable,
even so may Indra, Varuṇa, and Bṛhaspati— the guardians of the world— cause us to swell.
In the eastern direction you are King Indra; in the northern direction, O slayer of Vṛtra, you are the destroyer of hosts.
Wherever the rivers flow, that is your conquest. Be a bull, worthy of oblations, from the south.
His greatness has surpassed even this: from heaven, from earth, and from the mid-air.
Indra, the self-ruling lord praised by all, the celestial, the unassailable, has grown mighty for the sake of battle within his own home.
You, O Indra, are the sovereign king; you have become the overlord of the people. You are the ruler of the divine clans and of men; may your dominion be powerful, undecaying, and majestic.
In whom the seven Vasus ascend as ancient plants—
there the Rishi, most renowned for his hearing, is the guest of Indra, the Gharma-vessel.
The exhilaration is not that which comes from Soma, nor is it the intoxication of the wind; rather, O Indu, it is the sight of thee.
Thou art like a glowing sun for one who purifies himself, and like a seething cauldron when thou art heated, causing sweat to flow.
O Śatakratu, those senses of yours which are among the five peoples— O Indra, I choose them for me.
To you was granted [all] for your great power; all was entirely yours in the slaying of Vṛtra.
To you, O worshipful Indra, were granted dominion and might by the gods in the contest for men.
The Anus fashioned a chariot for your horse; Tvaṣṭṛ, O much-invoked one, forged the radiant thunderbolt.
Exalting Indra with prayers and hymns, they strengthened him for the slaying of the serpent.
When the strong ones sang their hymn for you, the strong one, O Indra—the pressing-stones and Aditi in harmony;
those wheel-rims, horseless and chariotless, sent forth by Indra, rolled against the Dasyus.
The inspiration that has entered me and given me birth—before the decisive day, I shall praise Indra, so that he may carry us across distress;
for him both sides invoke as he goes, like those on a ship.
To the deliverer from distress, let us offer this inspired hymn, seeking his favor as the one who bestows most abundantly.
O Indra, graciously accept this oblation; may the desires of the sacrificer come true.
I invoke Indra the protector, Indra the helper, the hero Indra who is easily invoked at every call; I now invoke the mighty Indra, invoked by many. May the bounteous Indra bestow well-being upon us.

O powerful Lord of the bay horses, let us not fall into misfortune in this your assembly; do not deliver us over to the wicked. Protect us with your safe defenses, and may we remain dear to you among the patrons.
Then, O God, all the gods rejoiced after you, the wisest among sages, at the slaying of the dragon,
when you, being praised, created wide space for the oppressed heaven, for the people, and for yourself.
Heaven and Earth have yielded that power, O immortal gods; O Indra, doer of deeds, perform what remains undone for you. Generate a new hymn through sacrifices.
Boldly strike out, O you of bold mind; let your fame be lofty indeed.
Let the waters flow forth with speed like mothers; slay Vṛtra and win the light of heaven!

For him, indeed, let the lord, however great he may be, swiftly brandish the thunderbolt against Vṛtra; may he rend him as one splits the joints of an ox, and desiring to release the floods, let him flow across the waters so that they may move.
O Indra, strike down our enemies; cast those who attack us low.
Place beneath our feet him who seeks to harm us.

Like a fearsome wild beast that roams the mountains, you have come from the furthest distance. O Indra, whetting your sharp bolt and your keen blade, strike down the enemies and drive away the adversaries.
In the mine of wealth, the singer is praised; Indra, free from fault, is honored by the one who lauds him.
He has indeed taken pleasure in the dwellings of Vivasvat; praise him, the ever-conquering slayer of the arrogant foe!

Victorious over your rivals in battles, O Indra, subduing and striking down those who oppose us—drink the Soma, O wielder of the thunderbolt! Having overcome them, bestow the Paṇis upon us for our enjoyment.
With a hundred names of the one praised by many, we magnify Indra, the subduer of the peoples.
Of the one praised by many:
FN emended. Ed. ṚV 3.37.4: *puruṣṭutasya*.
O Śatakratu, we invoke all your names with every song for the sake of overcoming our adversaries, O Indra.
Come to us from near at hand and from afar, O slayer of Vṛtra;
take pleasure in these our songs.
Since you are invoked between the far distance and the near, O Indra, come here from there!
O Indra, bring for our protection that most excellent wealth which is winning, ever-conquering, and victorious.
O Much-invoked One, you have overcome the enemies; your strength is supreme here, let there be bounty for you.
O Indra, bring us riches with your right hand; you are the lord of the wealthy rivers.
Men invoke Indra in the contest for the prize, when they harness those prayers that lead across [to the goal].
O Hero, desiring glory in the battle for men, grant us a share in the stall rich in cattle.
For the waves do not overwhelm you, O Indra, even though there are sacred prayers that are your strengtheners;
Tvaṣṭṛ himself increased your fitting power and fashioned the thunderbolt of overwhelming might.
Toward his own rain-shower, as he fights in the exhilaration of this [soma], his aids have sped forth like swift mares down a slope;
when Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, boldly aided by the plant, shattered the enclosures of Vala as Trita did.
We impel that Indra; I yoke the chariot.
The lofty songs have celebrated Indra, the subduer of Vṛtra, the bounteous lord of Śacī;
him who is magnified by well-fashioned hymns, the much-invoked immortal, being praised day after day.
vṛtraturam:
FN Corrections and Conjectures for the entire work. Ed. (VC): vṛtrataram.
Indra slew Vṛtra, the worst of Vṛtras, the shoulderless one, with his great thunderbolt, his deadly weapon;
like trunks of trees hewn down by an axe, the serpent lies prostrate, pressed against the earth.
vṛtrataram:
FN emended. Ed:
vṛṃtrataram.
Tread down those who attack; let the enemies be beneath you.
Like Indra, be a slayer of the Dasyus; win back the waters and the fields.
May he grant us blessings, vigor, good offspring, nourishment, and resplendent wealth;
may Indra, conquering lands with his might, subjugate all other rivals.
You, O Indra, are the sovereign ruler.
Indra conquers; he is never defeated. As sovereign lord among kings, he shines as king.
With all his protections, he conquers hostile armies, so that he may be worthy of approach and worthy of homage.

O Indra, your greatness is indeed exalted, O fierce one; when the armies, sharing a common purpose, clash together, let the lightning fall from the arms of the hero, and let not your mind wander away in every direction.
He who, as soon as born, was the first wise god and surpassed the gods by his power;
at whose breath the two worlds trembled through the greatness of his manly might—he, O people, is Indra.
Indra is fury; he was indeed a god, fury; fury is the Hotṛ, Varuṇa, the all-knowing.
The human tribes that exist worship fury. O Manyu, being in harmony with us through our fervor, protect us!

For you, O Manyu, are of overwhelming power, self-born, brilliant, and the subduer of adversaries; you are the observer of all people, victorious, and mighty. Being invoked, you go toward immortality.
O Agni, [accept] the *iḍā*; O Agni, you for us; O Viṣṇu, what indeed is yours? That of yours today.
May your goad be long, with which you bestow wealth upon the sacrificer who presses the soma.
Auspicious are your hands and well-fashioned your palms, O Indra, which bestow bounty upon the one who praises you.
What is your intent? Why do you not exhilarate us? Why do you not take delight in giving to us?
niṣattiḥ: FN emended. Ed: niṣatriḥ. cf. ṚV.4.21.9. [Page IV,187]
O Indra and Varuṇa, grant great protection for our sacrifice to our people and our kin;
may we conquer in battles the evil-minded who seek to overcome us, even those who persistently attack us.
One of you is called the Universal Sovereign, the other the Self-Ruling Lord; O Indra and Varuṇa, you two are great, possessors of great wealth.
All the gods in the highest heaven have bestowed upon you both, O bulls, vigor and strength.
May Indra be our advocate at all times; unassailed, may we win the prize.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
May we, accompanied by Indra, draw this wind toward us with our mouths for all our aid in the assembly.
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this.
In whose prosperity some men find delight in the assembly of heroes;
him whom even those worthy of honor kindle, and whom living beings bring forth together.
When we gather together the offerings of men and the oblations,
he takes hold of the ray of light, the strength of splendor, and the truth.
O Sūrya, as you rise today, proclaiming us sinless as truth to Mitra and Varuṇa— may we, O Aditi, be dear to you among the gods, O Aryaman, as we sing your praises.
Up have risen for you both the nourishing, honey-sweet offerings; Sūrya has ascended the bright ocean, for him the Ādityas—Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa acting in harmony—prepare his paths.
Desiring booty, I have offered this eloquent speech; may the Eater accept my songs with pleasure.
Will not the Son of the Waters, whose course is swift, make them well-adorned? For he indeed shall take delight in them.
The others go together.
For the Son of Waters has indeed taken his seat in the lap of the prostrate ones, standing upright and clothed in lightning;
carrying his supreme majesty, the swift, golden-hued rivers flow around him.
The smiling young women, the waters, go around that youth, cleansing him;
with his bright, skillful flames, Agni shines forth richly in the waters, without fuel, clothed in ghee.
O Agni, you purify our lives.
O God Agni, bestowing long life, choosing old age, with a face of ghee and a back of ghee—
drinking the ghee, the lovely nectar of the cow— bring this man to old age for me, as a father brings his son.
Increasing the cattle-pen, the dispeller of disease.
Those abodes of yours which they worship with oblation—may all those encompass this sacrifice.
Increasing the household, furthering us, rich in heroes, not slaying our men, O Soma, enter the dwellings.
To Sutrāman, to the Great One—this [hymn] for me; O Varuṇa, that [favor]; to you I go; Vaiśvānara, with your help; touched by heaven; toward you, O Hero, we cry out; indeed, we invoke you alone.
O Bull, most powerful one, you have pervaded all things with your greatness, your virility, and your might. O Maghavan,
wielder of the thunderbolt, protect us with your wondrous aids in the enclosure rich in cattle.
O Maghavan, graciously accept this speech of mine, this hymn of praise which Vasiṣṭha recites for you; take pleasure in these prayers at our shared feast.
May the Revatīs be our companions in revelry with Indra, providing abundant strength; may we, possessing food, rejoice through them.

Sing forth this strengthening hymn for this Indra, whose chariot is foremost—for him who creates wide space even in close combat, the slayer of Vṛtra in the clash of battles. Be our inspirer! May the bowstrings of our enemies snap upon their bows.
O Agni, come to us with your gracious favor.
O Agni, bring to us wealth that is all-conquering, most excellent,
and invincible in all battles.
Indra, the slayer of Vṛtra, has been strengthened by men for exhilaration and for power;
him indeed we invoke in great battles and even in small ones—may he further us in the contests for booty.
For in his every intoxication, he of straightforward intent has given us herds of cattle; gather up with both hands many hundreds of riches, sharpen us, and bring wealth hither!
With reverence, those wise ones honor his conquering might; they follow his many ordinances for the sake of primordial awareness, as auspicious ones according to his self-sovereignty.
These dappled cows, longing for him, mix the Soma;
Indra’s dear milch-cows urge on his bolt, the missile, according to their own excellent sovereignty.
Like clarified butter purified, stainless in body, pure like gold— so does that shine upon you, O self-dependent one, like a golden ornament.
Both [of them], O resplendent Lord of the People.
The noble Māya comes, the bull, the swift conqueror; the giver, he bestows wealth as the protector of our bodies.
The thousand-eyed god, the breaker of enclosures with the thunderbolt in his arm, may he grant us riches.
O Āryaman, O King, those many paths leading to the gods that traverse the sky—by them, O God, grant us great protection; be a source of well-being for our bipeds and well-being for our quadrupeds.
Upward, O Agni, [rise] thy pure flames; this Agni is the most heroic. Those auspicious horses of Sūrya—the seven bay steeds—are in thy chariot; thou art the swift one, visible to all.
Bestow sight upon our eye, sight for our bodies to see clearly; may we behold this world both together and apart.
O Sūrya, may we behold you who are so beautiful to look upon; may we, with the eyes of men, see clearly.
O Aśvins, you two [drink] the surā liquor.

Let the Hotṛ worship the Aśvins and Sarasvatī; let Indra drink of the Soma juices mixed with *surā*, and may they rejoice. Let them partake, O Hotṛ, perform the sacrifice—just as parents [rejoice] in their son.
May Indra, the good protector, the possessor of wealth, with his aids, be very gracious, he who is all-knowing.
May he drive away hostility and grant us fearlessness; may we be masters of heroic vigor.
May we abide in the good-will of that one worthy of sacrifice, and in his auspicious favor. May he, the good protector and self-strong Indra, drive far away from us all hatred.
O Agni, [grant] us strength consisting of cattle.
May Agni, when invoked, be auspicious to us; may the gift be auspicious, O blessed one, may the sacrifice be auspicious, and may our praises also be auspicious.
Together with these, we kindle Agni for you; O Agni, may we kindle thee with fuel. O Agni, three are thy powers, and three are thy abodes.
Three times Agni, the breaker of strength, having shattered the force, brought forth a thousand [men]—
the hero, the conqueror, the unconquered.
Three times a day the bull Soma flows with bright aids, the prize-winner who best wins a thousandfold.

Together with this rite and together with food we impel you both, O Indra and Viṣṇu, at the completion of this work. May you enjoy the sacrifice and bestow wealth upon us, carrying us across by paths that are free from harm.
Both of you have conquered.
O Indra and Viṣṇu, you shattered the ninety-nine strong fortresses of Śambara;
together you struck down a hundred and a thousand of the Asura Varcin’s heroes without resistance.
Then the Mother lamented for the buffalo: "O son, these gods are abandoning you.
Then Indra, about to slay Vṛtra, said: "O friend Viṣṇu, stride out even further!"
Three are your lifespans, O Jātavedas.
I am Agni, by birth Jātavedas; clarified butter is my eye, the immortal is in my mouth. I am the threefold light, the measurer of the mid-world; I am the unaging heat, the oblation—this is my name.
We know, O Agni, your three things in a threefold way.
We implore you, O Agni— the showerer of benefits, three-peaked, three-headed, and visible from three directions— to carry our oblations across the height of the earth.
One should indeed pierce it through this very [opening].
O gods,
sing forth to Parjanya, the bounteous son of Heaven;
may he seek out pasture for us.
The winds blow forth, lightnings fall, the plants shoot up, and the sky swells with rain.
Nourishment is born for every living being when Parjanya protects the earth with his seed.
Bṛhaspati, who with his roar has suddenly propped apart the ends of the earth, standing in his threefold seat— him,
the one with the pleasant tongue, the ancient seers, inspired sages, have placed before them with meditative vision.
Having split the fortress, he laid it low toward the west; Bṛhaspati cut through the three together from the ocean. He found the dawn, the sun, the cow, and the light, like the thundering sky.
The bay, well-winged steeds, clothed in the waters, fly up toward heaven along the black path;
they have returned from the seat of Cosmic Order, and from there the earth is moistened with clarified butter.
Your well-winged birds have followed your ways; when this occurred, the black bull bellowed aloud. He has come with the auspicious, smiling [waters]; the mists fall and the clouds thunder.
Like a lowing cow, the lightning bellows; it follows them like a mother follows her calf when their rain has been released.
Even the great, fully grown mountain was afraid; even the ridge of heaven trembled at your roar, when you Maruts, armed with spears, sport and rush together like waters flowing in one direction.
They create a ray with their might, a path for the sun to travel;
they have spread themselves out with their beams.
Moving outward, you go weaving the thread, O God, spreading out the black garment. The rays of the Sun, quivering, have driven away the darkness within the waters like a hide.
The Sun, most effective in winning booty, plunges into the waters with his rays;
awakening through our hymns, he bestows vital strength.
Turn toward us today, O worshipful ones; fearing, I would enter into your very heart.
Save us, O gods, from the devouring wolf; save us, O worshipful ones, from falling into the pit.
One has indeed provoked many offenses against you, since you have chastised me like a father chastises a gambler.
O Gods, let your snares be far away, let misfortunes be far away; do not seize me as one seizes a bird for its young.
Truly, those who kindle Agni and spread the sacrificial grass in due order—
those whose youthful Indra is their friend.
Those two by whom they generated the light in the very beginning, those who have taken their stand over all worlds—
let us invoke Agni and Indra, the bulls of the people, with thunderbolt in arm, the slayers of Vṛtra.
O Agni and Indra, come here to the sacrifice in the house of the donor who has pressed the Soma; O Gods, do not fail us, come for the drinking of the Soma.
May Anumati follow us today; indeed, O Anumati, may you follow us.
I invoke Rākā, who is easily summoned, with a beautiful hymn; may the fortunate one hear us and take note of us herself.
May she sew together our works with a needle that does not break, and may she grant us a heroic son, a giver of hundreds, worthy of praise.
O Rākā, those benevolent thoughts of yours which are well-formed, by which you bestow riches upon the donor—
with those, come to us today with a gracious mind, O fortunate one, granting us thousandfold prosperity.

O Sinīvālī, broad-tressed one, you who are the sister of the gods, accept the offered oblation and, O goddess, grant us progeny. (Ṛgveda 2.32.5) *rarāṇā* is emended; the edition reads *rarāṇa*. Cf. Ṛgveda 2.32.5.
She who has beautiful hands, beautiful fingers, who is prolific and bears many sons—
to her, to Sinīvālī, the mistress of the people, offer the oblation.
I repeatedly invoke at this sacrifice Kuhū, who performs good deeds and acts with wisdom, she who is easy to call upon;
may she grant us the renown of our ancestors. To you, O Goddess, we shall pay homage with an oblation.
May Kuhū, the goddess and consort of the immortal gods, hear our invocation of this oblation.
May she bestow abundant wealth upon the donor; may she grant increase of riches to the one who possesses true knowledge.
May Dhātṛ grant us wealth and unending, forward-reaching life;
may we obtain the favor of the god whose laws are true.
May Dhātṛ grant riches to the donor who desires offspring within his home, O bounteous one;
may all the immortal gods, the Viśve Devās, and Aditi, acting in harmony, bestow them upon him.

Worship the Aśvins in the morning; urge them forward. In the evening there is no sacrifice that goes to the gods, for it is disliked by them. Moreover, another besides us sacrifices and gains favor; each sacrificer who comes first is more successful.

Worship first those who come early in the morning; let them drink before the greedy and hostile one. For the Aśvins establish the sacrifice at dawn; the sages praise them as those who receive the first portion.
Now let us invoke Indra and Pūṣan for friendship, for well-being, and for the winning of booty.
With that which is purified.
O Agni, you, the wise, youthful master of the house, bestow great vital strength upon the donor, O god.

Agni, the bearer of oblations, ageless, our father, all-pervading, radiant, and beautiful to behold among us—shine forth with abundant nourishment from a well-maintained household; bestow upon us glorious renown.
And you, O Soma, being our will, let us not die, that we may live; you are the Lord of the Forest, whose hymns are dear.
Brahmā among the gods, the pathfinder among poets, the sage among the wise, the buffalo among wild beasts,
the hawk among vultures, the axe among the forests— Soma goes forth singing across the filter.
Today we choose with hymns Savitṛ, the lord of the good, who belongs to all the gods, the one whose impulse is truth.
Advancing through the dark expanse, establishing both the immortal and the mortal,
the god Savitṛ comes on his golden chariot, beholding all beings.
Like birds plunging into water, guarding themselves, like the thunderous roars of a cloud,
like waves breaking from the mountains, the jubilant hymns have resounded toward Bṛhaspati.
Like swans, with his speaking friends, Bṛhaspati cast off his stone-made bonds; he bellowed toward the cows, and knowing them, he praised and sang aloud.
O Indra, you who are of skillful wisdom, having grown great at once, you were born for the drinking of the son [Soma] and for supreme sovereignty.

You have become great, O Indra, through the sacred word; you have become worthy of sacrifice at all libations. You have become the shaker of men in every battle; you are the supreme mantra for all people, O Lord of all.
Forward, O friends, those who are free from disease!
Mitra: Corrections and conjectures for the entire work.
For whatever transgression of yours, O God Varuṇa, we commit day by day, as people do against your law—
Whatever offense we humans commit against the divine host, O Varuṇa—
whether through thoughtlessness or by violating your laws— do not harm us for that sin, O God.
So that Aditi may grant us the power of Rudra for our cattle, for our men, for our kine, and for our offspring.
Do not harm us in our children or grandchildren, nor in our own life-span; do not harm us in our cattle or our horses.
O Rudra, do not slay our heroes in your wrath; bearing oblations, we shall worship you with reverence.
He who makes all these creatures hear by means of a verse,
Savitṛ impels them forward.
All forms.
O Aśvins, performers of many wonders, come to the sacrifice of the donor;
may Pūṣan protect our wealth.
O Aśvins, strengthening this sacrifice, may these two bestow heroic power upon the sacrificer;
may these two protect our cattle on every side, and may Pūṣan ever protect us without fail.
O great Sarasvatī, auspicious one, rich in sacrificial food,
I bring this prayer to you whose speech is truth.
This oblation rich in ghee is for you, O Sarasvatī of true speech; may these offerings be presented to you.
May these most auspicious words addressed to you bring us good fortune.
"pra devaṃ devyā dhiyā"— these are eight verses.
The seekers of the gods anoint you with divine honey, O Lord of the Forest, at the sacrifice. Whether you stand upright, bestow wealth here, or whether you dwell in the lap of this mother earth.
O Lord of the Forest, rise up upon the height of the earth;
being well-measured with perfect skill, bestow splendor upon the one who bears the sacrifice.
Rising up before the kindled fire, winning for us the imperishable, heroic sacred word (*brahman*),
and driving far away from us all lack of understanding, rise up for our great good fortune!
Upward indeed, for our protection!
Standing upright, protect us from distress with your banner; burn up every devouring demon.
Raise us up so that we may move and live; find for us honor among the gods.
Born, he is born again on the auspiciousness of days, increasing at the assembly and the sacrifice.
The wise, skillful ones purify him with their inspired thought; the seers seeking the gods raise up their voice.
The youth, well-attired and enveloped in his garment, has come; he becomes even more excellent as he is born.
Wise poets, seeking the gods with their minds and devoted to sacred study, lead him upward.

"O God Savitṛ, toward you..."—with these thirteen verses, let the Hotṛ worship Agni, well-kindled with excellent fuel, at the navel of the earth, at the meeting-place of the lovely, on the height of heaven, at the station of *iḍ*. Let him partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
Let the Hotṛ worship Tanūnapāt, the offspring of Aditi, the guardian of the world, who today, as a god, [prepares] for the gods the paths leading to the gods.

May the path be anointed; may he partake of the clarified butter. Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Narāśaṃsa, the one praised by men, the leader of men, who may be rich in fatness through cattle, powerful with heroes, foremost in chariots, and radiant with gold; may he partake of the clarified butter.
Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ worship Agni; praised with the *iḍā*-hymn, may the god bring hither the gods as a messenger, the bearer of oblations, the unerring one.

Approach this sacrifice; may the god favor and partake of this invocation of the gods. O Hotṛ, sacrifice with the clarified butter! Let the Hotṛ worship the sacrificial grass (*barhis*), which is well-spread and softens the woolen covering. May it spread out wide and far in this sacrifice, providing a good seat for the gods.
May the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas today find it palatable; may it be dear to Indra. O Hotṛ, sacrifice with the clarified butter! O Hotṛ, worship!
O Yakṣas, let the lofty, hollowed-out ones that carry the vessels rise up with their mouths; let them lean out with their wings.
Let those easy of access lean out for this sacrifice; let the increasers of *ṛta* lean out. Let them partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Dawn and Night, the two great and well-adorned ones, who prepare a womb for men for their husbands, smiling together with Indra and the gods.

"Sit upon this sacred grass; let them partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to the two divine Hotṛs, the delightful, the two Potṛs, the sages, the wise. May one today perform the well-sacrificed rite with food, and may the other, with strength, approve it.
May they place this sacrifice in heaven among the gods; let them partake of the clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to the three goddesses, the most skillful of workers."
"May these waters now spread out this opening; may the divine waters go forth for the gods, toward the divine [oblation] of clarified butter. Hotṛ, sacrifice!

Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Tvaṣṭṛ—the most brilliant, the one who does not turn away, the bestower of seed, the far-famed, the bestower of glory, the multiform, who does not weary with desire—may he be well-nourished with nourishments, possessed of good heroes through his heroes. Let him partake of the clarified butter. Hotṛ, sacrifice! Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Vanaspati."
For he has let loose his inspired thoughts; the men, seeking to please him, have performed the rites. May the divine axe, according to the seasons, taste the offering;
may the god who carries the oblations to the gods partake of the clarified butter. O Hotṛ, sacrifice! MS_4,13.2 //
Devahūti: Emended; Ed: devahatim.

Kindled today in the dwelling of man, O Jātavedas, you, a god, worship the gods. And bring them hither, O you of Mitra-like majesty, you who are full of wisdom; for you are the messenger, the seer, and the far-seeing one.
O Tanūnapāt, fair-tongued one, anointing the paths that lead along the way of Truth with honey, make them savory;
fulfilling our prayers through our meditations and the sacrifice, bring our ritual to the gods.
With sacrifices, let us praise the greatness of these worthy of human praise, of the worshipful one;
may the gods, who are wise, pure, and the sustainers of prayer, enjoy both kinds of oblations.
Being invoked, worthy of praise and adoration, come hither, O Agni, in harmony with the Vasus!
You are the youthful Hotṛ of the gods; as such, being impelled, perform the sacrifice for them as the most skilled sacrificer.
The sacrificial grass is strewn toward the east according to the direction of the earth; at the beginning of the days, it is gathered for her dwelling.
It spreads itself out further and wider, a pleasant seat for the gods and for Aditi.
Let the spacious doors open wide, like well-adorned wives for their husbands; O divine, lofty, all-impelling doors, become easy of access for the gods.
Let the two worshipful ones, Dawn and Night, flowing with sweetness, sit down close together in their place;
let the two celestial maidens, lofty and richly adorned, wearing brilliant and radiant ornaments, bestow splendor upon us.
The two divine Hotṛ-priests, the first, eloquent ones, measuring out the sacrifice for man to worship;
the two poets who impel [the rites] at the assemblies, pointing toward the eastern light with their direction.
May Bhāratī come quickly to our sacrifice; may Iḷā, like Manu, be mindful here. May the three goddesses—Sarasvatī and the others, skilled in their work—sit upon this pleasant sacrificial grass.

O Hotṛ, being impelled and more skilled in sacrifice, do you, the wise one, worship here today that god Tvaṣṭṛ, who fashioned these two, Heaven and Earth, the parents, and adorned all beings with forms.
Release [the victim] by yourself, anointing the oblations for the gods in their proper season;
let Vanaspati, the divine immolator Agni, sweeten the offering with honey and clarified butter.
Agni, our Hotṛ at the sacrifice, being a prize-winning steed, is led around—
the god worthy of worship among the gods.
Agni goes around the threefold sacrifice like a charioteer,
bestowing nourishment upon the gods.
The lord of strength, the sage, goes around.

Agni has conquered; the god has won the prize, carrying the oblation to the gods. Urged forward by the *prāñjas*, being prepared with the *dhenā* (milk-streams), prolonging the life of the sacrifice—O Hotṛ, give the command! O divine immolators and you mortals, take hold of the offerings for the gods! Bring forward the sacrificial doors; desiring the sacrificial offering for the Lord of the Sacrifice, bring Agni toward him!
Strew the sacrificial grass; let the mother approve of him, let the father approve, let the brother born of the same womb approve, and let the friend of the same herd approve.

Place his feet toward the north; let him go to the sun with his eye, let him release his breath after the wind, let his life-force go to the intermediate space, and his body to the earth. Strip off his skin in one piece; before the navel is reached, extract the omentum from the fleshless part.

Hold back the internal heat; make his breast like a hawk’s, his forearms with the *praśas* knife, his upper arms like *śalā* sticks, his shoulders like *kaśyapa* birds, his hips without holes, his thighs like *kavaṣa* vessels, and his knee-caps like *srekaparṇa* leaves. There are twenty-six ribs in him; pull them out one by one in order. Make every limb of his complete. Dig a pit in the earth for the receptacle of the undigested food. With the fat, join together the *rakṣas*.
Do not cause the rectum of this [sacrificial animal] to cry out, thinking it to be a mere urinator; lest you, O Adhrigu, cause it to cry out for our children and grandchildren.
Perform the service well, perform the service perfectly, perform the service, O Adhrigu!
The Adhrigu and the Vipāpa are the two preparers for the gods;
as experts, prepare him in such a manner that his cooking is perfect.
Be pleased with that which is most extensive.
Place this sacrifice of ours among the immortals; O Jātavedas, enjoy these oblations.
O Agni, Hotṛ, having sat down as the first carrier, partake of the drops of fat and ghee.
O Purifier, these drops of fat mixed with ghee drip for thee;
