according to thy own law, grant us the most excellent treasure for the feast of the gods.
For you, O Agni, the true one, the inspired sage, the drops of ghee drip;
you are kindled as the best of seers; be the protector of the sacrifice.
For you, O Agni, the powerful one who is free from want, the drops of fat and ghee drip down.
Praised by the seers, come with your lofty luster; O wise one, graciously accept the offerings.
The most potent medicinal fat has been extracted from your center; we offer it to you.
O Vasu, the drops drip upon your skin; accept them, O God, according to the divine order.

Let the Hotṛ worship Agni: Svāhā to the clarified butter, Svāhā to the fat, Svāhā to the drops, Svāhā to the consecrations with Svāhā, Svāhā to the hymns of oblation! May the gods who drink the clarified butter, being pleased, enjoy the clarified butter in Agni.
O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
As soon as he was born, Agni measured out the sacrifice; he became the leader of the gods.
At the command of this Hotṛ, according to the direction of Truth, let the gods eat the oblation consecrated with Svāhā.
May Agni strike down the Vṛtras.
Let the Hotṛ worship Agni; may he enjoy the oblation of clarified butter; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
O Soma, you are the lord of the virtuous.
Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Soma; may he enjoy the oblation of clarified butter; O Hotṛ, perform the sacrifice!
Truly, this hymn of praise is pure.
Let the Hotṛ worship Indra and Agni; may they enjoy the fat of the omentum of the goat, the oblation; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
He pierced Vṛtra; O Indra and Agni, you two together [have done so].
Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Indra and Agni; may they enjoy the oblation of the sacrificial cake; O Hotṛ, perform the sacrifice!
O Agni, as the Hotṛ, sacrifice the *iḍā* for the sake of the people; may Agni enjoy the oblation of the cake; O Hotṛ, perform the sacrifice!

Praising Agni, the radiant and beautiful to behold, we pay homage to thee, O Jātavedas, who art worthy of praise. The gods have made thee their messenger, their steward, and the bearer of oblations—the navel of immortality.
Iḍā has been invoked; O invoked Iḍā, may she invoke us! Iḍā has been invoked—she who is of human descent, whose foot is dripping with ghee, and who belongs to Mitra and Varuṇa.

The Brahman created by the gods has been invited; the divine *adhvaryu*s have been invited; the human ones who protect this sacrifice and those who increase the lord of the sacrifice have been invited; Heaven and Earth, the first-born, the observers of *ṛta*, the goddesses whose sons are gods, have been invited;
this sacrificer has been invited to the higher worship of the gods, invited to the greater performance of the oblation in the divine abode.
"May the gods, being invited, enjoy this oblation of mine"—thus he is invited therein.
Invited are [the gods] for the sacrifice to the gods.
FN emended. Ed: In the *devayājyā* [verse]:
"For you, O Agni, were the first *manotā* of this prayer; you became the wondrous *hotṛ*."
O Bull, you have made us invincible; you have given us conquering power to overcome every force that would oppose us.
Then you sat down as the Hotṛ, the most excellent sacrificer, at the place of the libation, seeking nourishment, worthy of praise;
toward you, O God, the men seeking the divine first approached, intent upon great wealth.
As if surrounded by many riches, those who are watchful have followed after you for wealth—
the bright, beautiful, and lofty Agni, who is rich in fatness and shines forever.
Seeking glory, they have attained unimpaired glory as they approach the station of the god with homage;
they have even assumed names worthy of sacrifice, and they rejoice in your auspicious appearance.
The peoples on earth increase thee; both kinds of wealth of men belong to thee.
Thou hast become a protector, worthy to be known in the crossing over; thou art forever the father and mother of human beings.

Worthy of worship, beloved among the people, Agni has sat down as the joyous Hotṛ-priest, the most excellent sacrificer. As such, we, seeking refuge, would sit near you who shine within our home, paying homage with reverence.
Seeking your favor, we, the pious ones longing for the gods, implore you, O Agni, as the new one.
You, O Agni, have led the people, shining with the great light of heaven.
The sage of the people, the lord of the eternal tribes, the subduer, the bull among men,
the one who seeks the advance of those seeking him, the one who impels, the purifier, Agni who reigns as the worshipful master of riches.
Thus, O Agni, the mortal has sacrificed and labored who has accomplished the offering of oblations with fuel;
he who understands the invocation with prostrations, protected by you, shall possess all desirable things.
To you, the great one, we shall offer great worship with prostrations, O Agni, with fuel and with oblations;
on the altar, O Son of Strength, with songs and hymns, may we strive to abide in your auspicious favor.
O Agni, you who have extended heaven and earth with your light and with glories— you, the seeker of fame and the deliverer— shine forth far and wide for us with great, enduring, and wealthy spoils.

O Vasu, bestow upon us always, as if upon a man, abundant cattle for our children and progeny; grant us many great and mighty nourishments that drive away evil. May auspicious glories of renown attend us!

O King Agni, through my devotion to you, may I obtain many riches in manifold ways from your wealth-giving power; for many treasures, O Agni, rich in boons, reside in you, the king, for the one who serves you.
O slayers of Vṛtra, come hither with your Vṛtra-slaying powers, O Indra and Agni, through our prostrations. O Indra and Agni, be present with us with your most excellent and ungrudging gifts.

Let the Hotṛ sacrifice to Indra and Agni; let them both partake today of the goat-offering—the fat extracted from the midst, before the onset of hatred, before the seizure by men. Let them now devour [the portions] of those who graze in the fields, who are foremost in pasture, who flow with abundance, who belong to the hundred Rudras, who are consumed by Agni, whose garments are fat, from the ribs, from the haunches, from the sinews, and from the marrow.
May Indra and Agni enjoy the oblation cut from limb after limb, right from the hand; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
Seeking wisdom with his hymns, the inspired singer prays for glorious wealth that brings the first share;
O Indra and Agni, slayers of Vṛtra, wielders of the fair thunderbolt, further us with new gifts.
O Vanaspati with golden leaves, carry the oblations to the gods from of old for your purpose;
having bound them with a cord from left to right, convey them by the straightest paths of Truth.
Let the Hotṛ worship Vanaspati, for he has bound him with a most finely ground and most powerful cord—at the place where are the dear abodes of Agni’s oblation of clarified butter;
where are the dear abodes of Soma’s oblation of clarified butter; where are the dear abodes of the oblation of the goat for Indra and Agni;
where are the dear paths of Vanaspati; and where are the dear abodes of the gods who drink the clarified butter.

Wherever are the beloved abodes of Agni the Hotṛ, there he has lowered this [wooden vessel] as if having praised it, as if having extolled it; having made it as if more effective, may the divine Vanaspati accept the oblation—O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
O Lord of the Forest, having bound it with a cord made of the finest flour, you who know the sacred ways,
carry the oblations to the gods; and do thou proclaim the giver among the immortals.
Satisfy the gods.
Let the Hotṛ worship Agni Sviṣṭakṛt. Agni has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Agni; he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of Soma’s oblation of clarified butter;
he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of the oblation of the goat for Indra and Agni; he has sacrificed to the dear paths of Vanaspati;
he has sacrificed to the dear abodes of the gods who drink clarified butter. Let him sacrifice to the dear abodes of Agni the Hotṛ; let him sacrifice.
May Jātavedas perform the worship for those who offer their own greatness; may he provide nourishing food and accept the oblations at the sacrifices; O Hotṛ, sacrifice!
O Agni, that which has been invited today with the *iḍā*.
May the divine *barhis* be well-favored by the gods; may it be rich in heroes through the heroes. At dawn it should be spread, at night it should be gathered;
may it surpass others in wealth. May we rejoice with those who possess the *barhis*. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of treasure, let him enjoy the sacrifice.

For the winning of wealth, for the granting of treasure, let the divine *barhis* enjoy it. O divine doors, you who are strong in your closing, yet supple in your going, firm at the invocation of the gods—O Child!
May the youthful one measure this out; may the newborn boy, or the horse with its dusty mane, come forward.

May they go forth for the winning of wealth, for the granting of riches; O Sacrificer, worship! May the divine Doors go forth for the winning of wealth, for the granting of riches! May the two goddesses Dawn and Night, who have been invoked at this proceeding sacrifice, now surely approach; may the divine clans come forward, well-pleased and well-disposed, for the winning of wealth.
Sacrifice to the two goddesses Dawn and Night; may they partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of winning wealth. Sacrifice to the two goddesses who take pleasure, the bestowers of wealth;

of whom one drives away hostilities and the other brings desirable riches to the sacrificer—may they partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of winning wealth. Sacrifice to the two goddesses who take pleasure; may they partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of winning wealth. Sacrifice to the two goddesses, the offerings of strength; one brings nourishment and the other brings vigor.
May one enjoy the shared meal and the shared drink; may we, showing compassion, be united with the new through the old, and with the old through the new.

May those two, the invokers of strength, bestowing vigor, grant us that nourishment for the sake of wealth and the distribution of riches. Sacrifice to the two goddesses, the invokers of strength; may they partake of the offering for the sake of wealth and the distribution of riches. May the divine Hotṛs, Potṛs, and Neṣṭṛs, who have struck down the malevolent, bringers of wealth, partake for the sake of wealth and the distribution of riches.
May they partake of the gift of wealth; sacrifice to the divine Hotṛs, O gods, may they partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of gaining riches.

May the three goddesses—the three goddesses Iḍā, Sarasvatī, and Bhāratī—partake. Bhāratī has touched the sky with the Ādityas; Sarasvatī has protected this sacrifice here with the Rudras. May we rejoice here in the shared banquet with the wealthy Iḍā. May they partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of gaining riches; sacrifice!
May the three goddesses—the three goddesses—partake of the gift of wealth for the sake of bestowing wealth. May the god Narāśaṃsa, three-headed and six-eyed, receive him;
a hundred white-backed ones support him, and a thousand carry him forward. O Mitra and Varuṇa, he is worthy of this office of the Hotṛ;
Bṛhaspati is worthy of the Stotra, and the Aśvins of the Adhvaryu’s work. For the sake of bestowing wealth, may he partake of the gift of wealth. Sacrifice to the god Narāśaṃsa.

May the divine Vanaspati, the bestower of wealth, enjoy the gift of wealth; clothed in rain, dripping with clarity, he has touched the sky with his summit, filled the mid-air with his middle, and made firm the earth with his base. May he enjoy the gift of wealth. Sacrifice! May the divine Vanaspati enjoy the gift of wealth. May the divine Barhis, the establisher of the waters and the mover of those that flow, enjoy the gift of wealth. Sacrifice! May the divine Vanaspati enjoy the gift of wealth. May the divine Barhis, the establisher of
Unfallen, sustaining [the sacrifice] at will, worthy of man, and glorious—by means of this sacrificial grass (*barhis*), may we surpass other sacrificial grasses.
For the winning of wealth, for the granting of treasure, let it partake; sacrifice to the god Barhis among the waters. For the winning of wealth, for the granting of treasure, let it partake.
May the god Agni Sviṣṭakṛt sacrifice; may the god Agni Sviṣṭakṛt [sacrifice].

Today this sacrificer has chosen Agni as the Hotṛ; cooking the cooked offerings, cooking the sacrificial cake, taking the clarified butter for Agni, taking the clarified butter for Soma, and binding the goat for Indra and Agni—today the divine Vanaspati has become well-disposed toward us;
with the clarified butter for Agni, with the clarified butter for Soma, and with the goat for Indra and Agni, they have offered it from below, and they have grasped it from the fat.
They two have been magnified by the sacrificial cake. O seer, descendant of seers, grandson of seers, this sacrificer has chosen you today from among many who have assembled, saying:

"May he sacrifice for me among the gods for desirable wealth. Whatever divine gifts the gods have given, declare them to us and proclaim them; you, O Hotṛ, are impelled for the auspicious recitation, sent as a human being for the Sūktavāka.
Speak the well-spoken words; may this be auspicious for Heaven and Earth. We have accomplished the *sūktavāka* and the *namovāka*;
may we succeed in the recitation of the hymn. O Agni, you are the speaker of the hymn. Listen from heaven and from earth!

May Heaven and Earth be full of favor for us at this sacrifice, O sacrificer—those two who provide pleasant cows, who grant life-sustaining gifts, who are fearless, who do not fail, who are unconfined, and whose pastures are wide.

The two who grant fearlessness, whose heaven rains, whose waters flow, who are sources of well-being, who bring delight, who are full of vigor and full of milk, who are easy to approach and excellent to dwell with—may Agni, having partaken of these two, have enjoyed this oblation; he has grown strong and made it greater and more mighty.
Soma, having partaken of this oblation, has grown strong and made it greater and more mighty. Indra and Agni, having partaken of this oblation, have grown strong and made it greater and more mighty.

The two have attained greater greatness; the Lord of the Forest has accepted this oblation and has increased it; they have attained greater greatness. The butter-drinking gods have accepted the clarified butter and have increased it; they have attained greater greatness. Agni, through his office as *hotṛ*, has accepted this oblation and has increased it; he has attained greater greatness.
In this successful *hotṛ*-office, which leads to the gods, this sacrificer hopes for prosperity; he hopes for long life.
He prays for good offspring; he prays for everything dear. Whatever he prays for with this oblation, may he attain it, may he accomplish it;
may the gods grant it to him. May the god Agni win it from the gods, and we, the men, [win] from Agni the sacrifice and the enjoyment.
May both Heaven and Earth protect us from distress. Here is the resort of what is desirable; here is homage to the gods.
Hotṛ:
We choose that auspicious path for the sacrifice, the path for the lord of the sacrifice; may there be divine well-being for us, and well-being for human beings.
May the healing medicine rise upward; may it be well with our bipeds and well with our quadrupeds.
Swell up; may your milks be gathered together.
Here I invoke Tvaṣṭṛ, the foremost, who possesses all forms;
may he be ours alone.
Then, O divine Tvaṣṭṛ, being well-disposed, release the generative drop for nourishment,
from which is born a hero— skillful in action, highly dexterous, one who sets the pressing-stones in motion, and a lover of the gods.

May the longing wives of the gods protect us; may they aid us for the impulse of victory and for the winning of booty—those who dwell upon the earth and those who abide in the domain of the waters; may those goddesses, who are swift to hear our call, grant us shelter.
And let the divine wives, the consorts of the gods, come hither—Indrāṇī, Agnāyī, Aśvinī the queen;
let Rodasī and Varuṇānī hear us; let the goddesses come, they who are the season of women.
I invoke Rākā, who is yours, O Rākā; Sinīvālī, who has beautiful hands; and I invoke Kuhū, the Kuhū of the gods.
Agni is the invoker, the lord of the household, he is the king; as Jātavedas, he knows all births.
He who is the most excellent sacrificer among both gods and mortals, he, the upholder of cosmic order, performs the sacrifice.
Agni is the bearer of oblations; Iḍā has been invoked.

Soma gives a milch-cow; Soma gives a swift steed; Soma gives a hero who is skillful in action—one who is capable in the household, fit for the assembly, worthy of the council, and a glory to his father—to him who offers oblations to him.

O Soma, may we rejoice after you— you who are invincible in battles, the bringer across in hostilities, the winner of light, the winner of waters, the guardian of the stronghold, born for the fray, providing secure dwellings, highly renowned, and ever victorious.
O Soma, through your mental powers you have become one of excellent intellect; through your skills you have become one of great skill, the knower of all.
As a bull, by means of your bull-like qualities and your greatness, you have become resplendent with splendors, O beholder of men.
Those abodes of yours which are in heaven and those which are on earth.
O Soma, you have generated all these plants; you have generated the waters and the cows;
you have stretched out the wide mid-air, and with light you have dispelled the darkness.
O Soma and Pūṣan, these two gods—those abodes of yours which they worship with oblation.

O Soma and Pūṣan, you two, O Bulls, quicken that seven-wheeled chariot which measures out the mid-region, which never fails, which turns in all directions, and which is yoked by thought— [the chariot] with five reins.
One has made his dwelling in heaven, the other high upon the earth; one is in the mid-air.
May those two release for us an abundance of wealth, rich in desirable things and rich in food—may they open for us the navel of prosperity.
May Pūṣan, the impeller of all, quicken our intellect; may Soma, the lord of wealth, bestow riches upon us.
May the goddess Aditi, who is free from enemies, protect us; may we, blessed with brave sons, speak aloud at the assembly.
One has generated all beings; the other moves along beholding everything.
O Soma and Pūṣan, favor my prayer; with you two may we conquer all hostile armies.
O Prajāpati, none other than you has encompassed all these created beings.
May that for which we offer sacrifice be ours; may we be masters of riches.
Let us worship the Lord of riches, the adorable, the great, the most heroic in this battle for the winning of booty;
let us worship Prajāpati, the first-born of Ṛta, the god; may he speak in our favor.

O Prajāpati, you are the ancient guardian of the treasure, the father and progenitor of the gods, the lord and supreme protector of the entire world; O God, graciously accept our oblation at this invocation.
These worlds belong to you—the quarters, the intermediate directions, the distant realms, the hollows, and the heights.
O Prajāpati, creator of all, source of life’s prosperity, O God, graciously accept this our oblation.

Worship Prajāpati first among those worthy of sacrifice, the one to be worshipped at the head of the gods; may he grant us the renown of our fathers. To him, O God, let us do honor with this oblation.
He who rules over wealth, the giver of hundreds, worthy of praise; he who is the guardian of animals scattered abroad;
Prajāpati, the first-born of Cosmic Order (Ṛta), whose abode is the thousandfold—he shall enjoy our oblation.
O Vāyu, harness a hundred bay steeds that are well-fed;
or let your chariots, numbering in the thousands, come hither with their full splendor.
O Vāyu, drinker of the pure Soma, to you who belongs to Īśāna, he who has offered that oblation—him you make famous among mortals; every son born to him is born as a victor.
Yoke, O Vasu, the chariot-drawing steeds; harness the well-fed ones.
O Vāyu, drink our honeyed mead; come to our libations.
Surely those blameless gods who of old were strengthened by our homage—
they, for the sake of Vāyu and for the oppressed Manu, caused the Dawn to shine with the Sun.
Come to us, O Vāyu, for our great extension, for the sacrifice, and for splendor;
for we have performed much for you to give, even so as to give greatly at once.
May Vāyu be with you.
The wise, white one, the glory of his teams, who increases wealth and possesses abundant food, attends upon them.
They have stood forth with one mind for Vāyu; all these men have secured good offspring.
For wealth indeed these two worlds, Heaven and Earth, brought him forth; for wealth the divine Dhiṣaṇā establishes the god.
And may his teams attend Vāyu, as well as the white one who holds treasures in abundance.
Come, O Vāyu; [I call] forth Vāyu with those [hymns].
Come to our sacrifice with your teams of horses, by the hundreds and by the thousands, O Vāyu; rejoice at this libation. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
May the auspicious favor of the gods, who are upright in their striving, be ours; may the bounty of the gods turn toward us.
We have approached the friendship of the gods; may the gods extend our life-span that we may live.
O Gods, may we hear with our ears what is auspicious; O Holy Ones, may we see with our eyes what is auspicious.
With firm limbs and bodies, having offered praise, may we attain the lifespan ordained by the Gods.
A hundred autumns are before us, O gods, within which you have ordained the aging of our bodies;
wherein sons become fathers—do not harm our life-span in its middle course.
O gods, we implore you.
O gods, raise up again the one who has been cast down;
O gods, restore to life again even the one who has committed sin.
By means of sacrifice, the gods sacrificed to the sacrifice.
O Agni, lead us.
Bring forth an offering and a most purified hymn for your Agni, for his bright luster—
he who moves by his wisdom between all divine and human generations.
O Agni, do you carry us across.
Excellent songs and god-seeking prayers go forth to Agni, begging for wealth—
to him who is beautiful to behold, of fair countenance, swift-moving, the bearer of oblations, and the steward of men.
O Agni, drive away from us all disease; let the tribes that do not protect with fire fall upon us.
O worshipful God, together with all the immortals, grant us the earth once more for our well-being.
O singers, being urged by your thoughts and seeking the gods, lead her who is directed toward the gods;
carrying the sacrificial oblation for Agni, the vigorous, butter-sprinkling ladle goes forward to the east, bearing the gift.
He propped up the highest heaven; he has supported this prayer.
Whatever the gamblers have cheated at play, or whatever we know to be true, or whatever we do not know—all that, O God, loosen like something slack; then, O Varuṇa, may we be dear to you.
O Varuṇa, let thy wrath depart; for that I entreat thee.
May the daughter of the lightning, Sarasvatī, of wondrous life, the wife of heroes, bestow inspired thought.
In harmony with the divine dames, may she grant the singer an unassailable refuge and a flawless shelter.
Come to us from heaven!

O Sarasvatī, accepting these offerings from us with our salutations, graciously accept this hymn of praise. Placing ourselves within your most beloved protection, may we take refuge in you as if under a tree.

O Sarasvatī, that breast of yours which is inexhaustible, which is refreshing, by which you nourish all desirable things— that breast which bestows jewels, finds wealth, and grants good gifts— bring it here for him to suck.
O Sarasvatī, lead us toward greater prosperity; this is your oblation.
Seat in the sacred place the ordainer, the blue-backed, the great Bṛhaspati;
let us honor him who shines in his own dwelling, the golden-hued, the ruddy one.
For he is pure, the hundred-winged; he is the cleanser, wielding the golden axe, impetuous, and winner of the light.
Bṛhaspati is the one who grants easy access, the lofty one, most skilled at providing abundant nourishment for his friends.
He is Bṛhaspati with the well-praised hymn.
O Bṛhaspati, that which surpasses the worthy rival, which shines brilliantly and powerfully among the people,
which glows with strength, O you who are born of the *ṛta*— bestow that wonderful wealth upon us.
Thus [we offer] to the Father, the one belonging to all the gods, the bull.
The Sun follows the radiant goddess Uṣas from behind, as a youth follows a maiden,
while men seeking the gods extend their generations toward auspiciousness for the sake of the auspicious.
The auspicious horses belong to that Sun.
In the lap of heaven, the Sun assumes that form for the beholding of Mitra and Varuṇa;
one part of his luster is endless and radiant, while the other is black, which the bay steeds bring together.
Today, O gods, at the rising of the sun, deliver us from distress and from reproach!
May Mitra, Varuṇa, Aditi, Sindhu, Earth, and Heaven grant us this!
The brilliant face of the gods has risen; may the great Aditi loosen the bonds of Sutrāman.
Aditi is the sky, Aditi is the mid-air; Aditi is the mother, she is the father, she is the son.
All the gods are Aditi, the five peoples are Aditi; Aditi is all that has been born, Aditi is all that is to be born.
The support of heaven; the strewn sacrificial grass.
Now, what of Viṣṇu? That [is] his; that Viṣṇu [has stepped].
Increasing thy body beyond measure, they do not attain to the full extent of thy greatness.
We know both thy realms upon the earth, O Viṣṇu; as a god, thou alone knowest the highest.
Viṣṇu strode across this earth, bestowing it upon man for his domain;
steadfast are his people, the singers of praise, and he of noble birth has made wide room for them.
Three times this god strode across this earth, which possesses a hundred powers, by means of his greatness.
May Viṣṇu be preeminent, for he is mightier than the mighty; for the name of this steadfast one is truly brilliant.
The men, at the turning of the wheel, have yoked Indra’s chariot.
We have grasped your right hand, O Indra, seeking wealth, O Lord of treasures.
For we know you, O Hero, as the master of cattle; grant us wonderful, virile riches.
This entire world of cattle belongs to you on every side, which you behold with the eye of Sūrya;
you are the sole lord of the kine, O Indra. May we enjoy the wealth that you have extended to us.
O Indra, be united with us!
Drive the enemy far away with your terrible *śamba*, O you who are invoked by many!
Bestow upon us wealth consisting of barley and cattle, O Indra; grant the singer a prayer rich in booty.

Indra, with a roar like the hand of one milking cows, split apart Bala, the guardian of the milk-cows; seeking the milk-mixture with those whose hands were anointed with sweat, he made Paṇi weep and stole away the cows.
O Adhvaryus, he who slew Dṛbhīka and who drove forth the cows—verily, that is your strength.
For him, for Indra, clothe this one with Soma-offerings as the wind is in the mid-air, and with garments as a swift steed.
Indra won the plants and the days; he won the forest trees and the mid-air.
He shattered Vala and drove away the contending voices; thus he became the tamer of those who act with hostile intent.
He who, having slain the serpent, set the seven rivers free; he who drove out the cows from the lair of Vala;
he who generated Agni between the two stones; he who is the destroyer in battles—he, O people, is Indra.
Toward his own rain.
Praised by the Aṅgirases, he split Vala and tore apart the firm foundations of the mountain;
he released their artificial enclosures. Indra performed these deeds through the exhilarating draughts of Soma.
Worship the god Viṣṇu, Varuṇa for our protection, and Bhaga with the fat; O gods, sacrifice with the omentum.
May they come to our sacrifice with all-sustaining nourishment, and bestow upon us here wealth accompanied by progeny.
With the fat, O gods, worship with the omentum Viṣṇu the god and Varuṇa the giver;
driving away disease from us and enjoying this sacrifice, come hither.

O Viṣṇu and Varuṇa, grant great protection to our people and our subjects for the sake of the sacrifice; you who are long-extending in worship and strengthened by the oblation, burn away hostilities with light as you consume the darkness.
By whose power the regions were fixed, who are most heroic with heroes and most mighty, who rule as unconquered through their strengths— O Viṣṇu and Varuṇa, you have come to the first invocation.
O Viṣṇu and Varuṇa, you who protect from curses, O gods, worship with oblation and clarified butter;
drive away disease and the demons, and then bestow well-being and prosperity upon the sacrificer.
O bulls who release from distress, swift victors, most divine among the gods,
most powerful Viṣṇu and Varuṇa, take pleasure in this oblation presented by us, O heroes, for our protection.
The god Savitṛ, possessor of beautiful jewels, goes through the mid-air, borne by his horses; holding many treasures for men in his hand, he causes the world to settle and impels it forth.
Enveloped in pearls, multiform, with golden pins, vast and worthy of sacrifice—
Savitar, of wondrous luster, has mounted his chariot, bestowing power upon the dark regions.
May that god Savitṛ, the powerful lord of treasures, pour forth riches for us;
spreading his far-reaching luster, may he grant us the food that sustains mortals.
With the black dust, bring hither the desirable today.
Seeking fortune, wisdom, and abundance, may Narāśaṃsa and Gnāspati protect us;
may we be dear to the god Savitṛ at the gathering of all desirable wealth.
The plants that are rich in horses—those plants which are mothers, all those that stand around—when the plants come together, one of you after another.
O Heaven and Earth, you two, the greatest here, become manifest with your splendor through pure hymns,
when the bull, building up the two most extensive and lofty [worlds], bellows with his far-reaching movements.
To the two first-born ones.

He indeed was the skillful craftsman among the worlds, he who brought forth these two, heaven and earth—the wide, deep, well-established regions; the wise one, by his power, joined them together where there was no supporting pillar.
The two vast, footless ones bear as their moving embryo the many-footed one who moves;
like an eternal son in the lap of his parents, O Heaven and Earth, protect us from the monstrous.
O Heaven and Earth, O Father and Mother, let this which I address to you here be true. Be present with your protections, O lowest of the gods; may we find strengthening food that bestows long life.
The broad, vast earth, far-extending and boundless, I invoke with reverence at this sacrifice—
those two who are auspicious and victorious; O Heaven and Earth, protect us from evil.
Indra is the king of all that has been and all that is to be; Indra has supported this earth and the heavens. In Indra all worlds are established; I consider Indra to be both father and mother.

Indra bestows [wealth] upon the one who gives, Indra upon the one who fills; Indra, the powerful one, places the giver of praise and the one who praises in the world of the righteous. I consider Indra to be both my father and my mother.
Indra is the vast sky and Indra is the earth; Indra became the deep ocean. He is the wide mid-air; he is the father and mother of all people. I consider Indra to be both my father and my mother.
Indra slew Vṛtra with his thunderbolt; Indra [slew] Vyansa and Śuṣṇa; Indra shattered the fortresses of Śambara. Indeed, I consider Indra to be both my father and my mother.
Indra has become profound through his sacred power; Indra is that which has been, Indra is that which surrounds us.
Indra is the future and Indra is the past; I consider Indra to be both my father and my mother.
May Indra, whose arm wields the thunderbolt, protect us; in Indra are all beings and all worlds.
May Indra be our victorious helper; I regard Indra as both father and mother.

And may Sarasvatī, the fortunate one, being pleased, listen to us at this sacrifice; coming with radiant splendors and worthy of homage, she is superior to her friends through wealth as her companion.
With her surging, nourishing flood, this Sarasvatī has flowed forth as a supporting fortress of iron.
Driving away all other rivers by her greatness, the Sindhu moves forward like a chariot.
Sarasvatī is the sole one among rivers, pure as she flows from the mountains to the ocean;
perceiving the wealth of the vast world, she has yielded for the son of Nahuṣa both clarified butter and milk.

He gave this Divodāsa, who swiftly paid off his debts, to the worshipper Vadhrīyaśva. You, O Sarasvatī, who devoured the greedy Paṇi who consumed the one who offered praise—those are your mighty gifts, O Sarasvatī.

O auspicious Sarasvatī, this Vasiṣṭha has opened for you the doors of the Eternal Order (ṛta). O radiant one, increase [us] and grant spoils of war to the one who praises you. Do you all protect us always with your blessings.
With her surges she has shattered the ridges of the mountains like one digging for lotus-stalks with her powerful waves.
With well-fashioned hymns and prayers, let us invoke Sarasvatī, the slayer of Pārāvata, for our protection.

May he now strike down Vṛtra with our pure hymn; O Indra and Agni, you two who are the slayers of Vṛtra, [protect] us from all people. May the inspired singer, Tvaṣṭṛ, bestow upon us through his songs that which is fourfold, and Tvaṣṭṛ [bestow] a hero.
Tawny-hued, easy to support, bestowing vital strength, the hero is born obedient and longing for the gods.
May Tvaṣṭṛ release offspring for us from the navel; then may he go to the path of the gods.
O divine Tvaṣṭṛ!
The lovely one, entered by all, grows within these [waters]; rising upright in their lap with his own glory, he is the lord of those who lie prostrate.
Both [worlds] are afraid of Tvaṣṭṛ as he is being born; facing him, they bring the lion to consciousness.
I have grasped your right hand, O Indra.

O Indra, grant us wonderful, bull-like wealth— wealth accompanied by the Subrahmaṇyā, possessed of gods, great, wide, profound, with a broad base, renowned among seers, fierce, and overcoming adversaries.
My messengers, the yearning hymns, go forth to Indra, seeking his favor;
touching the heart and uttered by the mind, O Bull, grant us wondrous wealth.
O you who possess excellent weapons, excellent wealth, and excellent guidance, the upholder of the four oceans and of riches—
the one worthy of praise, worthy of hymns, possessing many boons, the fierce one— grant us wonderful, bull-like wealth.
O Indra, grant us wealth consisting of horses, chariots, and heroes—hundredfold or thousandfold booty;
a splendid host of inspired singers, winners of the light, wonderful and virile riches.

O Indra, grant us wealth that wins the prize, heroic through inspired song, victorious, piercing the bowstrings, ever-increasing, most skillful, the slayer of Dasyus, the breaker of forts, true, wonderful, and virile.
May Tvaṣṭṛ, the god, here in harmony with his wives— the goddesses— enjoying our oblation,
open up for us abundant wealth. O you who are worthy of sacrifice, hear our prayer and grant us your favor.
The god who is the placer of seed for this world, the progenitor, has taken his seat in the womb;
creating forms and bestowing beautiful features, Tvaṣṭṛ moves about with his wives, knowing all things.
Like Tvaṣṭṛ with his wives, he is followed by the two bowls (Dhiṣaṇās) as they bestow gifts;
holding all treasures in his hands, he moves between the two great worlds, accomplishing his purpose.
May he, the progenitor of our hymns, come to us with heroes, with cattle, with horses, and with riches, seeking wealth;
Tvaṣṭṛ, anointing himself with his all-formed domains, moves about with his wives, knowing all things.

May Tvaṣṭṛ, the Lord of the world, and the wives [of the gods], fashioning their offspring and abundant cattle—may the divine Rodasī, the Gnas, hear you; may they bestow upon us wealth that contains all boons.
May Tvaṣṭṛ generate for us sacrifice, body, progeny, and wealth of every form; may he now place seed within our womb, and may he cause the divine wives to procreate us so that we may live.

O Varuṇa, loosen our offense like a girdle; may we succeed in reaching the fount of your cosmic order. Let not the thread break as I weave my prayer; let not the measure of my work be shattered before the time of fulfillment.
Discharge the debts that I have incurred; O King, let me not suffer for what has been done by another. There are yet many dawns that have not dawned; O Varuṇa, ordain our heroes to live through them.
O Varuṇa, let fear sink deep into the waters; O sovereign lord of Truth, hold us in your favor.
Release us from distress as one releases a calf from its tether; for not even for a moment can anyone exist far away from you.
Release [me] from [this].
(FN emended. Ed: vimumugdhy.)
O King, whoever—whether an ally or a friend—has spoken fear to me who am afraid in my dream; or whoever, like a thief or a wolf, seeks to harm us—O Varuṇa, protect us from that!

O Varuṇa, let us not suffer the punishments you inflict upon the one who commits sin; O ruddy one, let them not strike him down. May we not go forth from the light into exile; loosen our enemies far away so that we may live.
Where have those friendships of ours gone, when we once wandered together in safety?
O self-dependent Varuṇa, I have come to your lofty dwelling, your house with a thousand doors.

The head of heaven, he who is asked about in the sky—may we abide in the good favor of Vaiśvānara. O Agni, shining brightly with your flame, as Agni you have pervaded everything from the morning libation.
May your golden chariot, pressing against heaven and earth, come with its stallions;
gleaming with its fellies, having a path of ghee, it is the bearer of refreshments, the lord of men, and rich in vigor.
Spreading over the five worlds, let the three-seated chariot come harnessed by thought—
the one by which you go to the people who long for the gods, O Aśvins, as you take your course wherever it may be.
Come hither with your famous horse; O wonder-workers, drink the honeyed treasure.
Your chariot, driven by the bride, strikes against the ends of heaven as it moves along its two paths.

O chariot-borne ones, whatever chariot of yours comes circling its course at the break of dawn, with that bring us well-being and security at the dawning of the Uṣas; O Aśvins, come to this sacrifice.
The daughter of the Sun chose your splendor for herself during the final night;
when you two protect the one seeking the gods with your powers, your bird comes around the heat by means of its protection.

O Aśvins, you two carried Bhujyu, who was cast down into the ocean, out from the waters with winged steeds that do not fail, that are unwearied and unswerving, as you brought him across by means of your wondrous powers.
O Lord of Prayer, may you be its controller.
With his true, radiant companions who seek the wealth of cattle, he split it open;
Brahmaṇaspati, with his bull-like boars that sweat with heat, attained the treasure.
The wrath of Brahmaṇaspati became truly effective according to his will as he was about to perform great deeds;
he who drove forth the cows distributed them across the sky, and like a mighty stream, he flowed apart with his might.

Kindling the fire, he shall conquer those who attack him; having performed sacred prayers and offered oblations, he shall prosper. He surpasses every born being with his own birth—whomever Brahmaṇaspati makes his ally.
O Lord of Prayer, [be present] at this pressing for all time.
He, together with his people, his clan, his kin, and his sons, wins booty and wealth through his men—
he who, with a mind full of faith, seeks to win over Brahmaṇaspati, the father of the gods, with an oblation.

O Mitra and Varuṇa, come with a fair hymn, being invoked with love and homage—ye who, like laborers at their work, stand together for the sake of men; even those who listen, ye restrain by your greatness.
You two wear garments of fatness; your thoughts and your outpourings are unbroken.
You have struck down all falsehoods; O Mitra and Varuṇa, you two adhere to the Eternal Law (ṛta).
Who indeed, O Mitra and Varuna, seeking the cosmic order (*ṛta*), shall bring you from the great heaven or from the earth?
Or in the seat of the cosmic order, may you protect us; and for the one who performs sacrifice, may you grant strengths that win cattle.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, that greatness of yours has been milked day by day from the standing waters;
you cause all the streams of the stall to swell, and the single wheel of yours has rolled along after you.
O Bounteous Givers, Guardians of the world, with that most extensive and flawless protection which is not easily pierced, favor us, O Mitra and Varuṇa; may we, seeking to win, be victorious.
O Gopas, stretch forth your arms! [Page IV,232] MS 4.14.10.
May all the gods come to us, united—Mitra, Aryaman, and Varuṇa;
so that they may all be our strengtheners and make our power easily victorious, not wavering like a weak force.

May the gods, the Viśvedevas, be auspicious to us; may Sarasvatī, together with our prayers, be auspicious. May those who accompany us be auspicious, and may those who grant gifts be auspicious; may the celestial ones, the terrestrial ones, and those of the waters be auspicious to us.
O all you gods who abide in the ordinance of Savitṛ of true impulse, of Mitra, and of Varuṇa—
bestow upon us that auspicious wealth consisting of heroes and cattle, and grant us manifold riches.
May all the gods be easy for you to approach; may all the gods [be gracious].
O Father Heaven, O guileless Mother Earth, O Brother Agni, O Vasus, have mercy on us! O all you Ādityas and Aditi, being of one accord, grant us abundant protection.

I praise Agni, the self-luminous, with prostrations; seated here, may he discern what we have prepared for him. Like chariots seeking booty, may I bring forth my offering; may I attain the hymn of the Maruts by circling to the right.
Radiant like the flash of a sacrifice, like the tongues of Agni flickering in three directions, singing praises like roaring heroes, the Maruts are of brilliant birth and invincible.
O Agni, go on your mission as messenger; do not fail, but proceed toward the god with the company of those who have prepared the sacred prayer.
Sacrifice to Sarasvatī, to the Maruts, to the Aśvins, and to the Waters—worship all the gods so that they may bestow jewels upon us.
Sing forth a brilliant hymn for the swift one who bestows gifts.
Those fires which, when kindled, have shone forth like the Maruts who have grown strong twice and thrice;
they have become dustless and golden, endowed with their manly vigor and heroic powers.
May your water-bearers come hither today.
Truth, the vast, the formidable cosmic order, consecration, austerity, sacred formulation, and sacrifices sustain the earth.
May she, the mistress of all that has been and is to be, the earth, grant us a wide world.
Unconstricted in her midst for human beings, she whose heights, slopes, and great level plains support plants of manifold forms— may that Earth spread out for us and be propitious to us.
May she whom the gods, ever vigilant and sleepless, protect at all times— the earth, the broad ground—
may she yield for us honey and clarified butter, and may she sprinkle us with splendor.
In whom the people of old strode forth, in whom the gods overcame the Asuras;
she who bears that which breathes and moves in many ways—may that Earth grant us the first draught.
Those eastern quarters of yours, those northern ones, those which are below the earth, and those behind—may they be auspicious for me as I move about; may I not fall while resting upon this world.
The all-sustaining, the supporter of wealth, rich in food, golden-hued, the foundation of the world—
the Earth, bearing Vaiśvānara Agni, and Indra the bull, may they bestow wealth upon us.

O gods Mitra and Varuṇa, may I turn you both toward the offering of the oblation with reverence and for our protection; may our sacred prayer be victorious in battles, and may we have divine rain that brings us safely across.
O guardians of Truth, you whose laws are true, you mount the chariot in the highest heaven;
for him whom you protect here, O Mitra and Varuṇa, the rain of heaven pours forth sweetness.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, Parjanya speaks the truthful, wondrous, and brilliant speech;
the Maruts clothe themselves in clouds through their great power; you two cause the ruddy, stainless sky to rain.
Dwell ye here; O sovereign kings, you two rule over this world, O Mitra and Varuṇa, you who behold the light at the assembly.
We pray for your rain, your bounty, and immortality; the thunderers move across heaven and earth.
O Mitra and Varuṇa, sprinkle our sacrificial offering with clarified butter and with nourishing foods;
for our sake here, grant us the boon of a pasture and bestow the lovely water of heaven.

Sovereign kings, fierce bulls, lords of heaven and earth, Mitra and Varuṇa, the all-beholding, they attend to the roar with wondrous clouds; by the magic power of the Asura, they cause the sky to rain.
O you who are great as soon as born, [you] overwhelm the cattle-pens.
With these, O Indra, unharmed, do thou agitate the fury of the enemy and his contending rivals;
with these, do thou scatter all attacking forces in every direction and bring down the Dāsa tribes for the Ārya.
This one is heard of as winning and slaying; he also wins the cattle by battle.
When Indra makes his wrath true, everything firm and everything moving fears him.
The waters flowed according to their own nature; he grew great in the midst of the navigable rivers.
With a concentrated mind, Indra struck him down for all time with his most powerful blow.
Indra is swift, the overcomer, fierce, golden-hued, vigorous, and the winner of light;
may we abide in the favor of that worshipful one, and in his auspicious goodwill.
May the golden-hued Indra, the conqueror in battles, grant us fearlessness from our adversaries.
May he extend to us a triple-layered protection; and may you all protect us always with your blessings.
Praise Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, whose back is drenched with Soma; may he enjoy our oblation of sacrificial cake.
Having slain our adversaries and hostile armies, O victorious one, grant us security from every side.

Praise the heroic wielder of the thunderbolt, the peerless slayer of Vṛtra, Indra who is invoked by many—he who alone is the lord over hundreds among the people; to that Indra, offer oblation with the sacrificial gift.
Indra became the overlord of the gods, the domestic priest, and the lord of the people, possessing abundant wealth;
the slayer of the arrogant, powerful and mighty, may he grant us wonderful, virile riches.

Indra, who by his greatness and power has firmly established these two, heaven and earth, against the assailant—may he accept our oblation for the sake of bounty; may the divine guardian of the treasures protect us among the gods.
Indra overcame Vṛtra in the battle with Vṛtra; the invincible Maghavan, the hero Indra.
The many subjects rejoiced after him: "This one is the king of the moving world and of the peoples."
He alone is the hero, he indeed is the possessor of valor; he is the sole sovereign, the protector of the world from afar.
When the heroic Indra overcame Vṛtra, then he became the sole sovereign of all people.
May Indra, the all-knowing, increasing the sacrifice, enjoy our oblation of the sacrificial cake (*puroḍāśa*).
Having slain the Dānava Vṛtra with his thunderbolt-arm, he made firm the quarters of space which had been made firm by his own strengthening power.
May Indra, the all-knowing, increasing this sacrifice, accept the sacrificial cake;
when the heroic Indra overcame Vṛtra, he became the subduer of those with hostile intent.
I have slain Vṛtra.
Indra aided the gods in the slaying of Śambara; Indra became the leader of the gods.
May Indra, strengthened by the oblation at the sacrifice, the subduer of Vṛtra, grant us protection and security from fear.
O fierce Indra, you were born as the bull of the gods; Indra, you have become their leader and have performed many deeds.
O Indra, together with the Maruts, bestow upon us for the sake of all people honors that bring wealth, headed by cattle;
being praised along with the gods, O Indra, may we find strengthening food and a community that grants life-sustaining gifts.
He who established the seven rivers upon the earth, who created the seven worlds and the quarters;
may Indra, accompanied by his troop of Maruts and possessing the oblation, come here to our sacrifice as the overcomer of Vṛtra.
Kindled are these thy steeds, O Indra.
I shall now proclaim the heroic deeds of Indra, those which the wielder of the thunderbolt performed for the first time:
he slew the serpent, he pierced the waters, and he split open the bellies of the mountains.
He slew the serpent as it lay coiled upon the mountain; Tvaṣṭṛ fashioned for him the thunderbolt that roars like heaven.
Like lowing cows, the flowing waters went straight down to the ocean.
Indra, the wielder of the thunderbolt, is the king of what has been set in motion and of the horned beast that brings peace;
he alone rules as the king of the peoples, encompassing them all as the felly encompasses the spokes.
Successful, he has driven away his enemies; with his sharp bull, Indra has shattered the fortresses. He struck Vṛtra down with his thunderbolt; exulting, Indra furthered his own purpose.
O Indra, you split the waters and the doors in all directions; you shattered the firmness of the mountain.
You became the king of the moving world and of the peoples, generating at once the sun, the sky, and the dawn.

Indra is the king of the moving world and of the peoples upon the earth; from that which exists in manifold forms, he bestows riches upon the donor. May he, being praised, send forth bounty even toward us.
The Gauri cows drink thus of the sweet, all-pervading honey;
they who move together with Indra, O wonder-workers, rejoice for the sake of splendor—being excellent, they follow their own sovereignty.
The heroic deeds of you, the warrior, the bull, the self-ruling lord, the fierce, the young, the ancient, the impetuous,
the undecaying wielder of the thunderbolt— the great exploits of the renowned and mighty Indra.
This homage has been spoken to the bull, the self-ruling king, whose strength is the hymn, the powerful one.
O Indra, in this assembly, may we, with all our heroes, together with the patrons, abide in your protection.
May Indra be with us when our banners meet in battle.

Through the newest favor of the Ādityas, may we be united with their most auspicious protection; may the swift ones, listening to us, establish this sacrifice in sinlessness and in the state of Aditi.
Neither the right nor the left is in doubt, neither in front, O Ādityas, nor behind.
Whether I am simple-minded or wise, O Vasus, may I, led by you, attain the light that is free from fear.
[Page IV,239] Holding [it].
Supporting the three earths and the three heavens, you maintain the three laws within their assembly.
By the Eternal Order (ṛta), O Ādityas, your greatness is mighty; this is your beautiful majesty, O Aryaman, Varuṇa, and Mitra.
May the sacrifice attain the favor of the gods.
Pure, with good pastures, undeceived, and possessing excellent heroes, he dwells among them even as his age grows old;
no one slays him, neither from near nor from afar, who abides under the guidance of the Ādityas.
The divine Āditya has risen in the east, gladdening all beings;
all the gods follow his impulse, for they know his supreme name hidden in the secret cave.
Whose banners shine, whose rays [shine], and to whom all these entire worlds belong—
we meditate upon the impulse of that Āditya, who shines as the first-born through his splendor.
The ruddy banner shines in the east; the Āditya, the all-knowing Asura and father of the gods, illumines all beings and follows the path that leads to well-being.
We meditate upon the impulsion of that Āditya, who shines as the first-born through his splendor— he whom all the gods, humans, and ancestors strengthen by means of their vow.
The bright Āditya has risen in the east, creating light and driving away the darkness;
shining forth toward all the quarters, the radiant maker of auspiciousness has come.
When the worshipful gods placed him, Sūrya, the son of Aditi, in heaven;
when the two moving ones became a pair, then indeed all beings beheld him.
O Agni, Lord of the House among men, we have made thee great with fuel.
May our household duties not be deficient; sharpen us with thy keen splendor.

O Agni, he shall dwell in peace, a guardian of Truth born of Truth; seeking the gods, he attains your wide light—whom you, O God, in harmony with Mitra and Varuṇa, protect from distress by casting off his affliction.
Whose flame is most brilliant, the lord of the woods, he has shone forth like a whip increasing on the path;
like a guileless runner, the immortal one, irresistible among the plants, takes heed of himself.
When the brilliance reached the lord of men for nourishment, the pure seed was poured down from heaven in the encounter;
Agni brought forth and perfected the blameless, youthful host, making them well-disposed.

O Agni, protected by your most powerful mind, grant us aid; O Giver, bestow upon us wealth and noble offspring. In the abundance of your most heroic riches, may we be the ones to offer you excellent praise for your treasure.
Like an archer drawing back his bow, he sharpens his brilliance like the edge of iron;
he whose course is wondrous, who as the steward of the night is like a bird perched upon a tree, swift in flight and rapid in his stride.
Agni, the bearer of oblations, is our undecaying father.
When Mātariśvan, having entered it, stirred him— the Hotṛ who belongs to all waters and all gods,
whom they have established among the human clans, brilliant like the sun, resplendent for the sake of beauty.

This is he, in whose protection and through whose assistance the singer prospers in the desire for aid— Agni, who, radiant and encompassed by the R̥bhus, moves about with the most excellent beams of light.
The self-luminous, far-shining Agni has shone forth; O Agni, worship the two wide-reaching worlds.
He whom the five peoples, offering oblations with reverence, anoint like Āyu, he who is well-nourished.
May he, the radiant one, like the eye that reveals the day, Agni who is to be known by the praiser,
grant us delight— he, the immortal who possesses all life, the guest Jātavedas, who has come around among mortals.
Agni, who shines forth with his rays, radiant through the gods, the observer of cosmic order, the eternal;
he who has extended his friendship to his friends, unassailable like a swift, well-trained steed.
O Agni, worthy of worship, when this divine assembly shall take place among the gods, O holy one;
and when you, O self-dependent lord, distribute treasures, grant us here our share, rich in wealth.
O Agni, O Ordainer, may these hymns of praise be pleasing to you, to your mind and to your heart.
May we be able to control the yoking of wealth, maintaining the glory bestowed by the gods.
O Agni, may the liberal patrons obtain nourishment; may the wise givers attain a full span of life.
May we win booty in battles against the enemy, securing our portion among the gods for the sake of glory.

Come to us with your auspicious friendships, O Great One, hastening with your mighty aids. Bestow upon us abundant wealth that crosses over all difficulties, and grant us a glorious portion accompanied by fair speech.

We shall perform those [rites] for you, O Agni, so that your life may be undecaying; provided that, once yoked, O Jātavedas, you do not come to harm, you shall then carry the portion of the oblation to the gods with a well-disposed mind, O well-born one.
Like one partaking of two oblations, you bestow a share upon the gods and you grant aid to men;
you are the youthful Hotṛ of the gods, so, being impelled, do you, the most skilled sacrificer, worship them.
O Agni, give, give to us, O Agni! Agni gives. O Lord of Food, grant us food; through Agni may one obtain wealth. O Bull, you gather together all those [gifts] which are yours.
Yama was the first to find the path for us; this pasture-land is not to be taken away, where our ancient fathers have passed away, being born according to their own paths.
Go forth, go forth by the ancient paths where our former fathers have departed;
there you shall see both kings rejoicing in the funeral offering—Yama and the god Varuṇa.
Come hither with the Angirases who are worthy of sacrifice; O Yama, rejoice here with the Vairūpas.
I invoke Vivasvat, who is your father, that he may sit down upon the sacrificial grass at this sacrifice.
Come and sit upon this sacrificial grass, O Yama, in harmony with the Aṅgiras fathers;
let the hymns recited by seers bring you here, and, O King, rejoice in this oblation.
Mātali is strengthened by the Kavyas, Yama by the Aṅgirases, and Bṛhaspati by the Ṛkvans;
those whom the gods have strengthened and those who [strengthen] the gods—some rejoice with the cry of *svāhā*, others with the ancestral offering of *svadhā*.
Honor with an oblation Yama, the King, the son of Vivasvat, the gatherer of people, who has departed along the great slopes and has spied out the path for many.
O Pūṣan, those golden ships of yours that travel within the ocean and through the intermediate space—
with those you go on a mission as the messenger of Sūrya, impelled by desire and seeking renown.
One part of you is bright; the other part is worthy of sacrifice.
May Pūṣan traverse all these regions; may he protect us with that which is most free from fear.
Bestowing well-being, glowing, possessing all heroes, may he go before us, never failing, full of wisdom.
Pūṣan was born upon the far path of paths, upon the far path of heaven, and upon the far path of earth;
knowing the way, he moves hither and thither toward both most beloved meeting places.
Pūṣan is the close kinsman of heaven and earth, the lord of nourishment, the bountiful one of wondrous luster;
him whom the gods gave to Sūryā, created by desire, powerful and self-moving.
The goat-horse, the guardian of cattle, whose abode is strength, who stirs the prayer, is established over the entire world. Pūṣan, wielding his supple goad, moves as a god surveying all beings.

O Gods, whatever offense against the gods we have committed, or whatever falsehood we have uttered with our speech—O Ādityas, release us from that; may he be freed from this through the power of Truth.
O gods, whatever untruth we have spoken through our speech out of a desire for life,
release us from that here, O all you gods, acting in harmony.
By the *ṛta* [cosmic order], O Heaven and Earth; by the *ṛta*, O Sarasvatī—protect us from the distress caused by whatever untruth we have uttered.
Indra and Agni, Mitra and Varuṇa, Soma, Dhātṛ, and Bṛhaspati—
may they release us from the sin, whatever falsehood we have uttered.

From the curse of one who is equal, from the curse of a kinsman, from the curse of an elder or even of a younger—whatever offense has been committed against us by the gods, from that, O Jātavedas, release us; for it is unassailable.

Whatever harm we have done to the atmosphere, to the earth, or to the sky, or to our mother or our father— may Agni Gārhapatya release us from that sin and from whatever misfortunes we have committed.
With that by which Trita emerged from the waters, with which the sun was released from darkness,
and with which Indra cast off all enemies— with that light, having attained light, I have sacrificed.
Whatever divine debt I have incurred, or whatever I have intended to seize from people,
may Agni and Indra, acting in harmony, release me from that.

Whatever debt I have incurred here through indolence or lack of confidence, by which we live as if by a deposit belonging to Yama—by this, O Agni, I become free from that debt; even while living, I pay back these debts with my own hands.

Whatever sins I have committed with my two hands, whatever I have smelled while playing with dice, and whatever I have seen while fierce— may the Waters and the Rāṣṭrabhṛts discharge those debts as debts owed to the Apsarases.
One who sees the fierce [deities] becomes a sustainer of the realm; whatever debts were incurred through gambling, these are now unpaid.
Like one seeking to discharge his debts, he does not remain a debtor in the world of Yama, for there is a treasure-store for him that never decays.
O Varuṇa, hear this my invocation; be gracious to me today as well. Seeking your protection, I long for you.
That I ask of you, adoring you with a sacred prayer; that the sacrificer hopes for through his oblations.
O Varuṇa, be present here without anger; O you of wide renown, do not steal away our life.
O Varuṇa, loosen the highest bond from us, untie the lowest, and release the middle one.
Then, O Āditya, being under your protection, may we be sinless before Aditi.
We appease your wrath, O Varuṇa, with prostrations, with sacrifices, and with oblations.
O wise Asura, O King, as you rule over us, loosen the sins we have committed.

O Agni, you who are wise, may you ward off from us the wrath of the god Varuṇa; being the best of sacrificers, the most excellent bearer of oblations, and blazing brightly, release from us all those who hate us.
As such, O Agni, be our protector, most helpful at the dawning of this very Uṣas;
being gracious, appease Varuṇa for us, grant us mercy, and be one who is easily invoked by us.
Saṃkasuka, Vikasuka, Nirṛta, and Nisvana—
drive the disease away from us, innocent as we are, far, far away.
He has driven away disease; he has turned back the sorcery and destruction.
With that [power], we send forth against him whoever shall encounter us.
With ill-will and good-will, with the solid and the secondary solid,
we send forth against him whoever shall encounter us.
We have united with splendor, with nourishment, and with our bodies; we have united with a gracious mind.
May Tvaṣṭṛ, the bounteous giver, bestow riches upon us and mend whatever in our bodies is injured.
Pure are the oblations for you, O Maruts, the pure ones; I present the pure sacrifice to the pure.
By the Eternal Law (ṛta) they have come, the true ones, the friends of ṛta, born of purity, pure, and purifying.
Those protections which you have for the one who exerts himself in worship.
Upon your shoulders, O Maruts, are rings; upon your chests rest golden ornaments.
Shining like lightning with rain, you wield your weapons according to your own nature.
The spears are upon your shoulders, O Maruts.
These Maruts bring the swift to rest; these bend force with force.
They ward off the curse of the attacker and lay heavy hatred upon the stingy one.
Like spokes, they are not last; like days, they are born forth, unimpaired in their greatness.
The sons of Pṛśni, the most excellent and most powerful, the Maruts, have mingled together by their own will.
O Agni and Soma, you two [have made] this; these [are yours].
O Agni and Soma, to him who today honors you with this speech,
bestow heroic vigor, abundance of cattle, and excellence in horses.
Mātariśvan brought one from heaven; the falcon churned the other from the rock.
O Agni and Soma, having grown strong through the sacred word (brahman), you have created a wide space for the sacrifice.
O Agni and Soma, whoever offers an oblation or presents a prepared sacrifice to you,
he shall attain full life, with offspring and heroic vigor.
O Agni and Soma, enjoy this presented oblation; accept it with pleasure, O bulls, and take delight in it!
For you have become providers of good protection and excellent aid; therefore, bestow well-being and prosperity upon the sacrificer.
The bull of the people, the king of the tribes, Indra, invoked by many, who fills the dwellings of men—
praised and seeking glory, come hither with protection toward me, having yoked your two vigorous bay steeds.
That which has entered me, which the creative impulse (dhiṣaṇā) brought forth.
His aids, his manly powers, and his teams of horses follow Indra together;
like rivers rushing to the ocean, our hymns, swelling with praise, enter him who is wide-expansive through our song.
This is indeed true: O Indra, there is no other like you, neither god nor mortal, who is greater.
You slew the serpent as he lay encompassing the flood; you released the waters toward the ocean.
O you who are invoked by many, you have overcome your enemies.
Bestowing upon us increasing splendor, O Indra, great dominion, and powerful might that overcomes men;
protect our patrons, guard the wise, and grant us wealth, good offspring, and nourishment.
